#1654. 'Bitter' Romelu Lukaku set to 'drop a bombshell' on Belgian football following his shock retirement, claims former team-mate after one-hour phone call

Published: 04:37 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 04:38 EST, 24 November 2026

Radja Nainggolan has claimed his former team-mate Romelu Lukaku is planning a 'bombshell' statement on Belgian football following his shock retirement from the national team.

Lukaku, 33, unexpectedly announced his retirement from international football following Belgium's Nations League matches against Turkey and Italy earlier this month.

Belgium's all-time record goalscorer had been left on the bench against Italy, while he had not been in the squad three days earlier for the match against Turkey.

Lukaku's shock announcement caught Belgian media by surprise, while his former international team-mate Nainggolan has claimed more news will follow from the star.

Nainggolan, who won 30 caps for the national team between 2009 and 2018, revealed on the Ongefilterd Voetbal podcast he had a one-hour phone call with Lukaku following his decision.

The former Inter Milan and Roma midfielder stated that Lukaku told him: 'You are only allowed to say that a bombshell is about to explode.'

Romelu Lukaku announced his shock retirement from international football earlier this month

Former team-mate Radja Nainggolan claims Lukaku is planning a 'bombshell' statement for Belgian football following a one hour phone call with the star. Source: Ongefilterd Voetbal

'So something is still coming,' Nainggolan said.

'What? I don't know. There were some internal problems between him and a certain person. But I'm not going to say much about that.

'Romelu will bring that up himself. He was a bit bitter, though. He was disappointed, frustrated.

'We will hear from him soon what will happen.

'About the real problems that were at play, he will be able to explain that better than I.'

Lukaku's retirement had marked a stunning reversal of his plans, with the former Chelsea and Manchester United forward having vowed in January that the 2026 World Cup would not be his last major tournament with the Belgium national team.

Describing his international career as a 'great ride', Lukaku had confirmed his international retirement on social media.

'16 years old', his Instagram statement began. 'For 16 years, I gave everything for the national team. I experienced every possible emotion. I played with fantastic teammates for whom I will always be grateful.

Lukaku vowed in January that the 2026 World Cup would not be his last major tournament

The Belgian forward has fallen down the pecking order and spent a lot of time on the bench

'I want to thank them all. I also want to thank all the coaches for pushing me and giving me the confidence to help the team. It was a great ride, and I enjoyed every moment.

'To the Belgian fans, thank you for the support you have given our team. I am proud to have represented my country at four World Cups and three European Championships. I will never forget those moments. I am at peace with my decision to stop here. It was amazing, it was a joy. I am grateful. Thank you.'

The Belgian veteran accompanied his post with a gallery of photographs from his storied international career, from his debut against Croatia under Dick Advocaat in 2010 to his final chapter wearing the armband.

Lukaku has captained Belgium on a handful of occasions since 2020, alongside the likes of Kevin De Bruyne and Youri Tielemans.

The 33-year-old forward, who became one of the hottest properties in world football after breaking onto the scene at Chelsea, has been a regular fixture in the international set-up for almost two decades.

Spearheading Belgium's golden generation, which included star-studded talents such as De Bruyne, Thibaut Courtois and Eden Hazard, Lukaku chalked up an impressive 135 caps for the international team.

He also retired as Belgium's all-time top scorer on 94 goals, just six shy of a century.

After suffering multiple injury setbacks, he featured at the 2026 World Cup under Rudi Garcia and continued to play a crucial role, scoring three times as a substitute to guide Belgium to the quarter-finals where they were ultimately stopped by eventual champions Spain.

Since Mark van Bommel's appointment in August, following Garcia's departure at the end of his contract, Lukaku has slipped further down the pecking order, with Charles De Ketelaere preferred to lead the line.

During Belgium's resounding 4-1 victory over Italy on Sunday, Lukaku warmed the bench as an unused substitute – and wasn't even in the squad to face Turkey three days before.

Lukaku, pictured with Kevin De Bruyne, was an unused substitute as Belgium beat Italy 4-1

While Belgium were winning in the second half against the Italians, Lukaku was seen warming up on the sidelines in the hope of featuring for one last time, but unfortunately was not given the opportunity.

VTM NIEUWS anchor Maarten Breckx claimed De Bruyne looked 'concerned' while speaking to Lukaku on the bench, suggesting the former Man City star was unhappy to see his team-mate overlooked.

'When it became clear that he wouldn't be allowed to come on, De Bruyne was talking to him. You could see the concern in his eyes,' he said.

'You could tell, especially from Romelu's attitude, that he was dissatisfied and displeased. He had probably counted on getting some minutes...'

With only Jan Vertonghen and Axel Witsel registering more international caps than Lukaku over their careers, boasting 157 and 140 appearances respectively, Belgium are expected to give the 33-year-old forward a send-off he deserves in the near future.

Witsel, who also called time on his Belgium career this year, was one of the team-mates to celebrate Lukaku's retirement on Instagram.

'Thanks for everything, legend. Thank you, what a journey we've had together,' he wrote.

#1651. Crystal Palace's Ismaila Sarr at centre of African Player of the Year controversy as agent demands transparency

By Naim Beneddra | 27 Nov 2026 15:21

Ismaila Sarr's agent has launched a fierce criticism of the Confederation of African Football (CAF) after the Crystal Palace winger was left off the final five-man shortlist for the 2026 African Player of the Year award, demanding that the governing body publish the full voting results.

The Senegal international enjoyed a remarkable European campaign with Palace, winning the Conference League and finishing as both the competition's leading goalscorer and its Player of the Season. He also scored four goals at the 2026 World Cup, equalling Roger Milla's African record for goals at a single edition of the tournament.

However, Sarr was overlooked in favour of Sadio Mane, Pape Gueye, Achraf Hakimi, Brahim Diaz and Ismael Saibari when the final shortlist was announced on Wednesday, prompting an angry response from his representative, former Premier League forward Diomansy Kamara.

Kamara, who represented Fulham, Portsmouth and West Bromwich Albion during his playing career in England, took to social media on Wednesday evening to question the credibility of the selection process.

The former Senegal international listed Sarr's achievements before demanding that CAF explain how a player with such a record could fail to make the final five.

"We demand transparency, clear criteria and the publication of the detailed voting results," Kamara wrote, before expressing his frustration with the way African football is governed.

Sarr's contribution to Palace's European success was particularly impressive. The 28-year-old scored nine goals in the Conference League, finding the net in both legs of the semi-final against Shakhtar Donetsk. His strike after just 21 seconds in the first leg also established a new record for the fastest goal in the competition's history.

Both his European triumph and his World Cup performances fell within CAF's designated assessment period, which ran from January 1 to September 15, 2026.

One possible explanation for Sarr's absence concerns the timing of the Court of Arbitration for Sport's decision to restore Senegal's Africa Cup of Nations title.

Voting for the African Player of the Year award closed on November 20, four days before Senegal were officially reinstated as African champions.

Consequently, voters submitted their selections while Morocco were still officially recognised as the tournament winners, despite Senegal having prevailed on the pitch in January's final.

Another possibility is that support for Senegal's three leading candidates was divided. Mane was named the best player at the Africa Cup of Nations, while Gueye scored the winning goal in the final. Both had strong cases, although neither could match Sarr's individual achievements in European club football and at the World Cup.

CAF has explained that the winners are determined by a voting panel drawn from several areas of African football, including national team coaches and captains, technical experts and journalists. The process is independently monitored by PricewaterhouseCoopers.

There is therefore no evidence that Sarr was deliberately excluded by the governing body. Equally, without a detailed breakdown of the votes, it is impossible to establish whether the timing of the CAS ruling or competition between Senegal's nominees materially affected his candidacy.

The winner will be announced at the CAF Awards ceremony in Lagos on December 2. For Kamara, however, the more pressing issue is establishing how one of the most productive African players in European football failed to make the final shortlist.

#1649. Man City owners facing fresh pressure as three Premier League rivals call for forced sale

By Naim Beneddra | 27 Nov 2026 15:42

The owners of Manchester City are facing renewed scrutiny after senior figures at three Premier League clubs reportedly called for them to be forced to sell the club in the wake of its financial breaches.

An independent commission found City guilty of 114 of the 115 charges brought against them by the Premier League, relating to alleged breaches of financial regulations between 2009 and 2018. The club denies wrongdoing and has appealed against the verdict, with sanctions yet to be determined.

While much of the debate has centred on potential points deductions, financial penalties and the possible removal of titles, some of City's domestic rivals believe that a change of ownership would be necessary to restore confidence in the competition.

Should Man City's owners be forced to sell up as punishment for breaking financial rules? ? https://t.co/YfIws1lvS6

According to BBC Sport, senior figures at three Premier League clubs have privately expressed their belief that City's Abu Dhabi owners should be compelled to relinquish control of the club.

One executive, speaking anonymously, suggested that any punishment would be inadequate if the current ownership remained in place, while also questioning the purpose of clubs funding an independent regulator if it was unwilling to intervene in such circumstances.

The independent commission found that City had inflated revenues and concealed losses amounting to approximately £900m through commercial arrangements deemed illegitimate. The findings cover nine seasons, during which City won three Premier League titles.

City strongly dispute those conclusions, arguing that the commission's decision contains fundamental errors of law and fact. Their appeal hearing is expected to take place in December, with a verdict anticipated in the new year.

The latest intervention from rival executives represents a significant development in the wider dispute. Even if City were handed a substantial points deduction or a financial penalty, those measures would not necessarily affect Sheikh Mansour's control of the club.

However, the power to enforce a change of ownership rests with the Independent Football Regulator (IFR), whose responsibilities extend beyond the Premier League's disciplinary framework.

Speaking before a parliamentary committee on Wednesday, IFR chairman David Kogan made it clear that the regulator would not be deterred by the prospect of taking action against one of England's most successful clubs.

"We cannot simply ignore our statutory duties in relation to a club because it happens to be of a certain size," Kogan said.

The Football Governance Act 2025 gives the regulator extensive powers over club ownership. Under Section 34, the IFR can assess whether existing owners continue to satisfy suitability requirements, including standards of honesty, integrity and financial soundness.

Should an owner be deemed unsuitable, Section 39 provides a mechanism through which the regulator can require them to relinquish their ownership within a specified period. Section 43 also allows the IFR to issue an ownership removal order and appoint independent trustees to oversee the process where the relevant legal conditions are met.

Such intervention would require a separate assessment of the individuals concerned. An unsuccessful appeal by Manchester City would not, in itself, automatically trigger a sale of the club.

The regulator's independence is particularly significant given Sheikh Mansour's position as vice-president and deputy prime minister of the United Arab Emirates, alongside the country's extensive economic interests in the United Kingdom.

However, Kogan has insisted that political considerations will have no bearing on the regulator's assessment of the evidence.

For now, the immediate focus remains on City's appeal against the independent commission's findings. Should the verdict be upheld, the club could find themselves facing two separate proceedings: one determining the sporting consequences of the financial breaches and another examining whether the individuals responsible for running the club remain suitable owners and directors.

The Reds desperately need a victory to steady the ship as their erratic and wayward form sees them enter 2016 still outside the top 4 and distant from any title challenge.

With a host of injuries to his main XI, Jurgen Klopp could be forgiven for dipping into the transfer market so early. The Reds have captured QPR right-back Steven Caulker along with Marko Grujic in the January transfer window.

With Grujic returning to his former club Red Star Belgrade on loan, Steven Caulker is likely to be given a run out as a substitute with the current spate of Liverpool injuries.

Ings, Sturridge, Lovren, Coutinho, Origi and Flanagan are amongst the Liverpool afflicted and will take no part in the match ahead. With Lovren out, Kolo Toure and Mamadou Sakho look likely to be Klopp’s first choice central defending partnership.

Alberto Moreno and Nathaniel Clyne should start as full-backs for the Liverpool side and will be crucial in any attempt to penetrate the Gunner’s defences. Emre Can and Lucas should marshal the midfield, while James Milner, Firmino and Adam Lallana look to give Petr Cech some concerns about his goal. Leading the line should be Christian Benteke, who’s lack of form doesn’t threaten this match as manager Klopp has few options in his position.

Probable Starting XI (4-5-1): Mignolet; Clyne, Sakho, Toure, Moreno; Lucas, Can, Firmino, Lallana, Milner, Benteke.

Arsenal must show that they have the one quality required of all champions : Consistency. The task is hereby straightforward for Wenger’s men. Win, keep winning, regardless of your manner and the title is yours.

With half the season concluded, Arsene Wenger must be wishing that he received a Christmas gift from the Arsenal medical team. Injuries have decimated his midfield with Wilshire, Cazorla, Rosiscky, Coquelin and Sanchez out of the game.

There is some good news with Mesul Ozil having managed to partake in some leisure instead of participating in the FA cup victory over Sunderland. Keeping the nimble playmaker fit would be key to Arsenal aspirations, both in this match and for the remainder of the season.

With both Petr Mertersacker and Gabriel available, it would be interesting to see whom Arsene Wenger picks out for his starting XI. Koscielny, Bellerin and Monreal have nailed down their place in the defence and the inclusion of the slower Mertersacker or the inconsistent Gabriel may have a defining moment in the game.

With Arsenal’s midfield woes, it should fall to Flamini to screen the defence with Ramsey alongside him. Walcott, Ozil and Joel Campbell should be the main thrusts of Arsenal’s attacking play with Giroud as the elegant, decisive focus.

Probable Starting XI (4-5-1): Cech; Bellerin, Gabriel, Koscielny, Monreal; Flamini, Ramsey, Ozil, Walcott, Campbell; Girourd.

With previous encounters between these teams resulting in high scoring draws, we favour a repeat of last year’s epic 2-2 result for the same fixture. Martin Skrtel’s 97th minute header in front of the Kop capped a memorable game which also had Fabio Borini sent off and we expect similar fireworks at Anfield tomorrow.

#1647. Prepare for another Saudi Premier League raid: Relaxation of foreign player rules set to spark mega-money recruitment drive - after near-$1BILLION spend in 2023

Published: 05:07 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 05:13 EST, 24 November 2026

Premier League clubs are bracing themselves for a new raid of their talent from Saudi Arabia, as the mega-money league considers relaxing spending rules.

Teams in the Saudi Pro League (SPL) are currently only allowed eight foreign players in their 25-man squads but are discussing increasing that number to 14 or even higher.

If the move is approved, it is likely to trigger a flood of cash in the market similar to the massive £765million spree in 2023 that saw the likes of Cristiano Ronaldo, Karim Benzema and N'Golo Kante sign for Public Investment Fund (PIF) teams.

In that 2023 window, almost half of the transfer fees received by Premier League clubs came from the SPL.

In total, 94 players were signed by Pro League clubs and the January transfer window could now follow a similar pattern.

The Saudi spending reached such astronomic levels that it eclipsed every other league in Europe aside from the Premier League.

Cristiano Ronaldo (right) and Angelo, pictured in action for Al Nassr, are among the foreign stars already plying their trade in Saudi Arabia and more will be on their way

The supposed reason for the proposed rule change is to elevate the standard of existing Saudi players at home by raising the overall level of talent ahead of the country hosting the World Cup in 2034.

But critics argue that the new rules would only force Saudi players out of their domestic league in place of high-profile foreign recruits.

While Premier League clubs are often reluctant to allow talent to leave in January midway through the season, the fees on offer from Saudi can be eye-watering and hard to turn down.

Aston Villa sold Jhon Duran and later Ollie Watkins for a combined £115million to the SPL.

Fulham accepted £50m for Aleksandar Mitrovic, while Wolves banked £47m for Ruben Neves and Liverpool were able to recoup almost £50m for Darwin Nunez.

West Ham were able to cash in on Crysencio Summerville after relegation last term when Al Hilal bought him for £60m.

Would Man United consider offers for Bruno Fernandes as his contract winds down? Or will they keep the club captain to help battle relegation?

Suddenly every Premier League club recruitment department will be reassessing their squads and be keeping a close eye on the rule developments in Saudi.

Ollie Watkins moved from Aston Villa to Al Hilal and the Premier League side have recouped huge fees from the SPL in the  past

Ivan Toney (second from left) and his Al Ahli team-mates celebrate a goal against Al Nassr

The SPL's decision on whether to allow the increase of foreign players will be clarified before the winter window opens.

The PIF are winding down their investment in golf through LIV having invested more than £3.7billion since 2021 but their operation in football shows no sign of slowing down.

Players weighing up a move to Saudi will perhaps have a more difficult decision than in 2023 over relocating, with conflict still affecting the country.

The Asian Cup was postponed earlier in November following a missile attack from Yemen-based Houthi rebels on Riyadh airport that killed 13 people and injured more than 300.

Security fears and geo-political uncertainty could make footballers think twice before accepting the lucrative contracts on offer in January and beyond.

#1644. FIFA Slaps Real Madrid, Atletico Madrid With 1-Year Transfer Bans

Home » Home 2 » FIFA Slaps Real Madrid, Atletico Madrid With 1-Year Transfer Bans

The ban will start from the July transfer window this year and finish with the January transfer market in 2017.

Atletico were also fined 900,000 Swiss francs (820,000 euros) and Real 360,000 (330,000 euros).

“The two clubs were found to have violated several provisions concerning the international transfer and first registration of minor players as well as other relevant provisions with regard to the registration and participation of certain players in competitions,” said a FIFA statement.

Barcelona has just ended a one year ban for similar reasons.

Real and Atletico were “issued with a reprimand and given 90 days in which to regularise the situation of all minor players concerned,” FIFA said. They can still sell players during the transfer ban.

FIFA said the alarm was raised over the two clubs by FIFA’s Transfer Matching System and its disciplinary committee completed the inquiry.

Under international football rules, players under 18 cannot be transferred to another country, except in limited circumstances. All transfers need the approval of a special FIFA committee.

“The investigations concerned minor players who were involved and participated in competitions with the clubs over various periods between 2007 and 2014 (Atletico Madrid) and between 2005 and 2014 (Real Madrid),” FIFA said.

The ban follows a similar sanction handed to European champions Barcelona, who were unable to register new players during 2015.

Barca were initially banned in April 2014, but managed to delay the sanction taking affect until the transfer windows in January and the summer 2015 by launching an ultimately unsuccessful appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS).

By delaying the ban, Barca managed to sign the likes of Luis Suarez and Ivan Rakitic in the summer of 2014 to propel them to a treble of La Liga, Champions League and Copa del Rey.

The news is just the latest institutional embarassment for Real Madrid just over a week after they appointed French legend Zinedine Zidane.

Madrid have sacked two Champions League winning coaches in Carlo Ancelotti and Rafael Benitez in the past seven months, as well as being thrown out of the Copa del Rey for fielding an ineligible player.

The sanction could also be bad news for the likes of Paris Saint-Germain and Manchester United, who had targeted Madrid stars Cristiano Ronaldo and Gareth Bale with Real highly unlikely to dispose of their best players without the chance to sign suitable replacements.

La Liga leaders Atletico Madrid’s usually hectic transfer policy will also be put on hold. However, Diego Simeone’s men look better placed to cope with the ban having invested heavily in young talent over the past year.

Neither Real no Atletico made an immediate comment on whether they would appeal.

#1642. Max Dowman-mania could make League Cup hottest ticket in town

There is an obligation on all of us, from supporters to pundits and journalists, to remain calm and measured about footballers as young as Max Dowman. But, my word, he does make it difficult. Arsenal’s 16-year-old sensation continues to sparkle whenever he steps on to the field, and he did so again with this superb display against Ipswich Town.

"The hype will only continue to grow!"Max Dowman that is delightful! 👏 pic.twitter.com/UfFY1VSyXn

At this rate, Arsenal supporters will be looking forward to Carabao Cup matches as eagerly as any Premier League or Champions League game, simply because it will be a chance to watch Dowman again. The forward’s age and inexperience means he is still used sparingly in those high-priority competitions. The League Cup, by contrast, may prove to be his domain over the coming months.

Dowman’s double at Portman Road made him just the second 16-year-old to score two goals in a game for a Premier League side. The first was Wayne Rooney, for Everton against Wrexham in 2002.

The two goals underlined why there is so much excitement around Dowman. The first was a demonstration of his prodigious dribbling ability, as he weaved through Ipswich’s defence and buried his shot with the weaker right foot. The second showed his composure: a slotted finish, rolled in with ease.

Max Dowman nets his second of the game! 😍 pic.twitter.com/XRZ9GqZx3x

As Mikel Arteta approaches the point of signing a new contract in north London, one wonders how much the idea of developing Dowman will excite him as he looks to the future. Which manager would not want to coach a player of such natural ability? Which manager would not want to see how good he could be? The same is true of Marli Salmon, the 17-year-old defender who also impressed on Tuesday night.

“A joy to have him,” said Arteta of Dowman. “It’s remarkable. It’s something very natural for him. He can deliver those actions effortlessly, I would say. What we have to do is look after him. He is 16. You don’t see that in this league. In other leagues in Europe, that’s a totally different context.

“Having two teenagers playing for Arsenal at this level is so fulfilling. Because I’ve been there and just to be able to contribute to somebody’s career and dream, to be able to experience a game like tonight, is phenomenal. And yeah, medium and long term, we know that if they continue to develop in the way that they are, we are going to have two tremendous footballers.”

"He was brilliant, he made the difference - we need to look after him" 🌟Mikel Arteta says Arsenal need to "be really cautious" with 16-year-old Max Dowman after he scored twice in Arsenal's 4-2 win over Ipswich 🔴 pic.twitter.com/1msJAEkK8z

Dowman’s two goals, along with strikes by Noni Madueke and Mikel Merino, secured a comfortable victory for Arsenal against Premier League opponents. Ipswich scored a goal of their own, through Anis Mehmeti, but never seemed likely to cause the visitors too much bother. A late strike from former Arsenal player Chuba Akpom was only a consolation. “We found a way to fight back into it,” said Gary O’Neil. “Losing by two goals to them isn’t a dreadful effort.”

Dowman is already developing a trademark goal, of sorts. His first strike for the club, against Everton last season, came after he left an opponent face-down on the turf at the Emirates Stadium. He inflicted the same pain here upon poor Cédric Kipré, who tried to tackle the teenager in the seventh minute but ended up with a mouthful of grass.

It was an image that encapsulated Arsenal’s dominance in the early exchanges, as was the sight of Madueke firing in the second. The chance came after Bruno Guimarães and Merino, majestic in midfield, had monstered Ipswich’s attempts to play out from the back. Merino was dominant throughout, winning tackles with steel and then spinning away opponents with style. “He’s unbelievable,” said Arteta.

Arsenal’s long-term relationship with the League Cup is not a particularly healthy one. For a club of their stature, it is a source of mild embarrassment that they have not won this competition since 1993. They came close last season, reaching the final at Wembley, but were defeated by Manchester City.

Given the depth of Arteta’s squad, Arsenal really should reach the final again. If this is a tournament for the B-team, at least in these early stages, then Arsenal probably have the best B-team in the country. They started this game without any of Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Martin Odegaard, and Kai Havertz but were still extraordinarily strong in midfield and attack.

The only pre-match concern was their defence, which has been weakened by a couple of early-season injuries. Arsenal started with Salmon at centre-back and the teenager was in direct combat with the physical, sharp-elbowed threat of Ipswich striker Zian Flemming. He stood up to the challenge with determination and class.

Ipswich had made 10 changes following their victory at Crystal Palace at the weekend, which was an indication of where the Carabao Cup sits in their priorities. They were able to get into Arsenal’s penalty area but never gave the impression they could really hurt the Premier League champions, apart from when Mehmeti converted Jack Clarke’s low cross.

Akpom struck in the 91st minute to encourage O’Neil, but by then the game had been lost. Arsenal’s work, and indeed Dowman’s work, had been done.

"He's 16 years old, and we have to be cautious of that" 💫Mikel Arteta reacts to an incredible performance from Max Dowman as Arsenal put FOUR past Ipswich 🔴Don't miss the Carabao Cup on @paramountplus 📺 pic.twitter.com/AIcAbMx6ub

On managing the hype that surrounds Dowman, Arteta said: “What we have to do is look after him. He’s 16 years old, you don’t see that in this league. In other leagues in Europe, that’s a totally different context, but in this league, with the demands... We need to make sure that every time we throw him in it’s in the right context with the right preparation.”

Conor Coady shares his thoughts on Arteta’s role in Dowman’s development:

"He'll know how to nurture him!" 🗣️Conor Coady says Mikel Arteta is the perfect manager for Max Dowman 👏 pic.twitter.com/YdgLxfKiOf

Asked about Dowman’s two-goal performance, Arteta said: “A joy to have him, Marli [Salmon] as well. Seventeen years old, to play at that level with the physicality they have to be able to handle that level, it’s remarkable. Max, yeah, it’s inevitable to talk about him when he scores and he creates the moments he has created tonight. It’s normal.”

He added: “He is coping better and better and better, he did the action where he regains the ball and wins it in the first goal, he loses his man... He’s an unbelievable player because of the character that he has and how much he loves to play on the biggest stage and still handles the situation with such naturality.”

Speaking in his post-match press conference, Mikel Arteta said: “Really pleased with a lot of things we did tonight, the way we attacked the game, how dominant, fluid and aggressive we were, right from the beginning to try to influence the result. We scored two very early goals that gave us obviously a great platform for the game.

“Individually some big performances as well. Some debuts tonight which is great to see as well, so we take a lot of positives from tonight.”

Ipswich's first act of this game was to launch a long ball towards Marli Salmon and Zian Flemming. Salmon won the header, and then continued to win the overall battle with Flemming. Such an impressive performance by the 17yo. You don't see many defenders doing that at this age.

Plenty of talking points: Dowman, Salmon and an ominous Arsenal showing... Leave your thoughts on the match and join the conversation in the comments section beneath this live blog.

Ipswich Town 2 Arsenal 4 (Akpom) Davis picks out Akpom who swivels to deceive Konsa before sweeping home. There was perhaps a foul in the build-up as Lewis-Skelly appeared to get held back by the goalscorer as he scrambled to get back.

Arsenal are finishing this match with a 16-year-old, 17-year-old and two 18-year-olds on the pitch. A good evening for the academy.

And right on cue, Salmon picks up the ball on the halfway line and drives forward, eventually forcing a foul from Nunez who goes into the book for his troubles.

The record for the youngest hat-trick scorer across all professional tiers of English football belongs to Trevor Francis.

Playing for Birmingham City against Bolton Wanderers in Division Two on February 20, 1971, Francis scored four goals in a 4-0 win at just 16 years and 307 days old.

Ipswich Town 1 Arsenal 4 (Mehmeti) Clarke makes an immediate impact, bursting down the left before cutting the ball back to Mehmeti who had just held his run and is able to beat Kepa from 10 yards out.

Ipswich have been outgunned in the centre of the park, with Arsenal seemingly always creating plus-one and even plus-two situations.

O’Neil makes a pair of changes, replacing Philogene and Flemming with Clarke and former Arsenal striker Akpom.

Ipswich Town 0 Arsenal 4 (Merino) Arsenal work the ball infield from the right in instalments, Madueke feeding Zubimendi who passes through Dowman to Merino on the edge of the box who opens up his body before guiding the ball around Walton.

Arsenal are FLYING!Merino puts another goal away for the Gunners 🔥 pic.twitter.com/nrzHHk1bou

Max Dowman was first spotted by Arsenal at four years old. He’s been running past opponents and scoring goals ever since. Now he’s just doing it on the professional stage, in front of the watching world, but it still looks completely normal to him.

Chance! It could, and maybe should, have been four. Merino threads a wonderful through-ball beyond Ipswich’s final line of defence and Madueke steals in to poke the ball across the face of goal with the outside of his left boot. Gyokeres was in the middle but could not divert the ball goalwards.

Kepa stretches to claim a looped Flemming cross which had echoes of the Spaniard’s game-defining error in last year’s League Cup final. This time he collects with a minimum of fuss. That Flemming was so far out on the left will be of concern to O’Neil.

Ipswich Town 0 Arsenal 3 (Dowman) Madueke picks out Zubimendi in the box who in turn finds Dowman in the right half space and he gallops on to the ball before arrowing the ball past Walton. The assist had grazed Greaves’ outstretched arm and would surely have led to a penalty had Dowman not done the honours.

Max Dowman nets his second of the game! 😍 pic.twitter.com/XRZ9GqZx3x

Arsenal’s kick-off routines caused a stir last season, but this term they have mixed things up once more. Here, Zubimendi lays off Lewis-Skelly, who punches in a line-breaking pass to get Arsenal on the front foot from the off.

Zubimendi gets us going again for the second 45 minutes. Konsa has replaced Gabriel at the interval.

Such is the midfielder’s versatility, his heat map tonight paints a wildly different picture to that from his 45 minutes at the Stadium of Light over the weekend. He has played the midfield-sentry role in Suffolk and has executed it well.

It is further evidence as to why Arteta was hell bent on signing him in the summer. You would imagine his all-conquering presence will relieve pressure from Rice and Zubimendi’s shoulders. They were out on their feet by the end of the last campaign.

Liverpool are ahead against Spurs at Anfield thanks to this strike from Mac Allister:

Pick that out!! 🇦🇷Alexis Mac Allister hits a beauty into the roof of the net 🔴 pic.twitter.com/G7OT27CA8P

Arteta’s nine changes are looking fairly sensible now. He will be particularly pleased to have seen fringe players like Dowman and Madueke get on the scoresheet so emphatically. Arsenal will need their full squad to achieve their lofty goals this season and that half will give Arteta confidence that they have enough firepower to last the course.

We’ll play one minute of time added on...

Arsenal inject a bit of calm to proceedings with a healthy spell of possession. Their horizontal and vertical rotations (Lewis-Skelly is now minding to drop into that Rice role alongside the centre-backs) are proving tricky for Ipswich to track.

Gyokeres gets a shot away after a clever run in behind by Merino but cannot get enough pace behind his strike to trouble Walton.

Mehmeti brings down a searching ball from deep and faces up to Gabriel as he enters Arsenal box. Such is the Brazilian’s poise, though, that even when the Ipswich forward appears to have worked a yard of space, he telescopes in his leg and stops Mehmeti’s advances with perfunctory ease.

Ipswich are getting more bodies forward, with both full-backs bombing on. The ball is worked out to Furlong out on the right but, in a promising position, he loses his footing and the ball rolls out of play.

Next comes a foray down the left, Philogene beats Salmon on the outside but Kepa gets down smartly to cut out his cross. The next goal will naturally go a long way to determining how this tie plays out.

Ipswich are in the ascendancy and Greaves heads goalwards off a corner but does not get the requisite contact to beat Kepa. Arsenal launch a swift counter which is snuffed out by McAteer, illegally, and he goes into the book.

Ipswich might have thrown the towel in at 2-0 but they are pushing quite hard here and have caused Arsenal a few problems since the second goal. Philogene looks particularly dangerous on the left flank.

Outtara has been Ipswich’s best attacking outlet and he threads another lovely ball into the path of Philogene who is just beaten to it by Gabriel. The subsequent corner is punched away by Kepa.

Kepa goes long and Greaves misjudges the flight of the ball. Madueke looks to be in, but Ipswich’s centre-half recovers well and is able to block the eventual effort.

Merino picks out Dowman between the lines and the teenager is straight into Ipswich’s backline. His effort is well-struck but is charged down and cleared to safety.

Better from Ipswich! Their best shot at getting back into this contest is through counters when Arsenal are not set, and here Outtara bursts down the left before swinging in a deep cross to Flemming who cuts the ball back to Mehmeti who fires the ball just over the crossbar.

Guimaraes is slotting in between Arsenal’s split centre-backs in Arsenal’s build-up and Ipswich are not prepared to go three vs three that high up the pitch meaning the Brazilian has all the time in the world to dictate play from there. We’ve seen this all season long from Rice.

Arsenal are in complete control. Madueke flashes a delivery across the face of goal which is just cut out by Kipre before Gyokeres can get a foot in.

Arsenal’s midfield is so powerful and they showed it there, as Guimaraes slammed into one tackle and then Merino followed up with another to create the chance for Madueke. Arsenal are completely dominant here.

A flurry of chances for Ipswich. Philogene’s lopping cross is tipped away by Kepa but the ball falls to Flemming at the back post and his effort pinballs around a thicket of Arsenal limbs before reaching Florentino on the edge of the box, whose effort sails over the bar.

Ipswich Town 0 Arsenal 2 (Madueke) That is goal of Ipswich’s own making. Walton’s loose pass out is picked off by livewire Guimaraes, and Merino spins in a ball in behind for Madueke to stride on to and spear beyond Walton into the bottom corner.

Arsenal are flying 🔥Noni Madueke adds a second for the Gunners 🔴 pic.twitter.com/gAVmAI3odx

Florentino’s loose pass is picked off by Dowman and the youngster earns a free-kick as the Ipswich midfielder attempts to recover. It’s taken quickly and Eze bursts into the box - there is a half-hearted shout for a penalty as the ball appears to strike Ouattara’s arm but the contact appears incidental and the referee waves play on.

Max Dowman’s second goal for Arsenal is quite similar to his first, scored so thrillingly against Everton last season. On both occasions he has put an opposition defender face-first in the turf before scoring the goal. Outrageous ability with the ball at his feet.

"The hype will only continue to grow!"Max Dowman that is delightful! 👏 pic.twitter.com/UfFY1VSyXn

Ipswich earn a free-kick on the left by-line but Gyokeres does his job at the near post and heads away Nunez’s delivery.

Ipswich Town 0 Arsenal 1 (Dowman) Simply majestic. A simple one-two with Eze on the left has Dowman running at Ipswich’s defence. He drops his shoulder and sells Kipre a dream before stroking the ball beyond Walton. “1-0 to the champions” sing the travelling fans.

Lewis-Skelly bursts down the left and picks out Dowman on the edge of the box. He attempts to tee up Guimaraes but Nunez gets a toe in and is able to avert the danger.

Early indications suggest Zubimendi will play in the nominal right-back position, inverting into midfield when Arsenal build up.

Madueke picks up the ball on the right flank and drifts inside before Guimaraes’ effort from the edge of the box is blocked.

Flemming gets us started. Ipswich kicking from right to left.

The players emerge from the Portman Road tunnel, Ipswich in their customary home blue shirts and white shorts, Arsenal in red and also white shorts. Last week Arsenal were made to change into red shorts to avoid a similar clash with Napoli, but apparently that’s no problem tonight. Modern football for ya!

Arsenal are warming up with Eze on the left, Madueke on the right and Dowman as the No 10 behind Gyokeres. In defence it looks like Zubimendi at right-back. The formation in the warm-up is not always the formation in the match, though...! They have played that trick before.

"You have to be patient with him" 🗣️Jamie Redknapp and Conor Coady on Max Dowman's potential for Arsenal 🙌 pic.twitter.com/O2bU0SQoJn

"They merit a start from the way they train"Mikel Arteta on Marli Salmon and Max Dowman being given their first starts of the season in tonight's game at Ipswich 🔴 pic.twitter.com/yYbFXn2Oje

Arsenal have won the League Cup twice – in 1987 and 1993 – meaning eight clubs have better records, including Aston Villa (five titles), Tottenham Hotspur (four), Nottingham Forest (four) and Leicester City (three).

Their rather modest haul is a far cry from their record-setting 14 FA Cup titles. In the 33-years since Arsenal’s most recent League Cup triumph, the competition’s title sponsor has changed hands four times (kudos to anyone who can name all five!).

No team has scored more goals through substitutes in the Premier League than Ipswich, which is a nod to the promoted club’s depth and work in the summer transfer window.

It has meant that Gary O’Neil has had to leave established players out of match-day squads. “It was really tough leaving out Darnell [Furlong] and Anis [Mehmeti] from the squad [against Crystal Palace],” he said. “Doing that to good people is one of the toughest parts of the job. But I have faith in them, it’s just that everyone’s fit at the moment and we’ve had to recruit a strong squad to get us through an unbelievably challenging season.

“On Tuesday, whoever I pick, I have 100 per cent faith that they’re ready and that they’re going to represent what we do and how we go about it.”

On Hincapie’s omission from the match-day squad:

“Some players were carrying some fatigue, some little issues that we have to look after and some other players are available, fresh and in better conditions to play.

On Timber being left out of tonight’s squad:

“Everything is fine, but obviously he has played much more than we would have wanted. He played 53 minutes [against Sunderland] after five months. I will need to look after him.”

When asked if Arsenal will set up with a back three tonight:

Alan Davies, the actor and comedian who is a famously passionate supporter of Arsenal, recently told a story about a charity event he once attended with former captain Tony Adams. Speaking on The Tuesday Club podcast, Davies said Adams revealed his football philosophy to be: “You need seven.”

The “seven” in question, Adams explained, are seven members of the team who are ready and willing to fight the opposition in the tunnel after the game. Once a team have those seven individuals, Adams said, everything else flows from there.

For much of the past two decades, Arsenal have not had seven. In some years in the latter stages of Arsène Wenger’s tenure, they probably did not even have three or four. But that has all changed in recent seasons under Mikel Arteta, to such an extent that the Premier League champions would now undoubtedly bring considerably more than seven combatants to any touchline scrap or tunnel bust-up.

Saturday’s gritty 2-0 victory away to Sunderland provided evidence that Arsenal have added two more of these characters to their squad this summer.

Tonight will be a good test for young Marli Salmon, the 17-year-old defender who is the latest high-class graduate of the Arsenal academy. Arsenal have extremely high hopes for Salmon, who made four senior appearances last season. He could be in the centre of defence or at right-back tonight. I suspect Ipswich striker Zian Flemming might try to target Salmon with some physical challenges, especially in the air. Let’s see how he handles it.

Ipswich Town Walton; Furlong, Kipre, Greaves, Ouattara; Florentino, Nunez; McAteer, Mehmeti, Philogene; Flemming

Substitutes Palmer, Davis, O’Shea, Walle Egeli, Enciso, Clarke, Lukic, Maeda, Akpom

Arsenal Kepa; Zubimendi, Salmon, Gabriel, Lewis-Skelly; Guimarães, Merino; Dowman, Eze, Madueke; Gyokeres

Substitutes Meslier, Calafiori, Konsa, Tzolis, Odegaard, Ibrahim, Julienne, Saka, Havertz

Max Dowman announced himself last season, showing off his gilded footwork in impressive cameos off the bench. Who could forget that lung-busting run and goal against Everton?

And while the 16-year-old winger featured in Arsenal’s pre-season, these will be his first minutes of senior football in the season proper. His only game time thus far has come in the Premier League 2 under-21s competition and he was not included in the match-day squad at the Stadium of Light on Saturday.

When asked about Dowman after the victory at Sunderland, Arteta said: “I wish we could have him here, but we have the limitation with the numbers that we can have. He will have his chance, he will have his minutes and he will have to earn them like anybody else. We know the talent that we have, we know the players that we have there and we need to help him and find a way to make sure he continues to develop and help the team.”

Although keeping Ipswich in the Premier League must be Gary O’Neil’s primary goal, he has insisted that the club will embrace opportunities in the cups.

When asked how he would approach tonight’s tie, O’Neil said: “We’ll have a strong side, we’ve worked our socks off in the transfer window to give ourselves a strong squad. Of course, a different level to Arsenal, but we’ll be strong on Tuesday and we’ll do our best to win the game.

“The club has worked so hard to have these moments and of course it’s a cup game, but to have Arsenal and Liverpool come to Portman Road a week or so apart is what everyone has worked so hard for in recent years, so we’re going to enjoy it, we’re going to have a right go and worst thing that can happen is we lose to Arsenal.”

Good evening from Portman Road, where it’s a gorgeous night for football. Ipswich have made 10 changes, which is an indication of where this competition sits in their list of priorities. Arsenal have made nine.

The Arsenal line-up is quite hard to decipher. It looks like it might be Martin Zubimendi at right-back or centre-back. I’ll keep an eye on the warm-ups and report back shortly.

Gary O’Neil wins the rotation battle, raising Arteta’s nine changes with 10 of his own. Greaves the only survivor from last weekend’s win at Selhurst Park.

Your Town tonight! ✊ pic.twitter.com/EEYjPFww4Y

Young defender Marli Salmon comes into the starting XI as Mikel Arteta makes nine changes to the team that started against Sunderland on Saturday.

🔴 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 ⚪️Introducing your Carabao Cup Gunners starting XI ✨🤝 @deel

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of the Carabao Cup third-round tie between Ipswich Town and Arsenal. Mikel Arteta’s side have won all six of their matches so far this season, but travel to Portman Road fresh off an incident-filled win over Sunderland which thrust officiating back into the spotlight after Ezri Konsa conceded a penalty having been – in Arteta’s words – “judo-rolled” by Dan Ballard.

After the match, the Arsenal manager said: “I watched [the incident] 20 times and I cannot find a way to understand how to even think to give a penalty in this situation or the way the VAR has to intervene. So I don’t know what to think, really. But I’m sad, that we have to discuss, after such a beautiful game, something at this level that has the gravity of that because that changes the course of the season and it can cost you the championship… This cannot happen.”

Arteta may be pleased that VAR is not in use at this stage of the Carabao Cup, and all eyes will be on Peter Bankes who takes charge of tonight’s match against Ipswich.

This season Arsenal hope to arrest a startling League Cup record. It has been 33 years since they last lifted the trophy, during which time they have been runners-up seven times. Losing last year’s final will have also added fuel to Arsenal’s fire, and Arteta may resolve he must field a strong starting XI. In fact, he may not have much choice in his backline as Ben White has emerged as a serious injury doubt after picking up an injury at the Stadium of Light and may join Cristhian Mosquera and William Saliba on the treatment table. This would likely mean starting Jurriën Timber, who is only just returning from a long-term groin issue. There is more scope for rotation in advanced positions, with Noni Madueke, Viktor Gyokeres, Eberechi Eze and Mikel Merino contenders to start.

A 90th-minute Zian Flemming winner against Crystal Palace on Saturday helped Gary O’Neil’s Ipswich to their second win in four Premier League games, a feat they required 16 matches to achieve the last time they were in the top flight. Heavy investment into Ipswich’s squad has proved fruitful thus far, though in-form striker Emersonn is expected to sit out tonight having taken a knock at Selhurst Park.

#1640. Tuttosport: Jashari ‘into the cauldron’ – chances arrive to justify €35m price tag

AC Milan will be without Luka Modric for the must-win game against Olympiacos, presenting a chance to Ardon Jashari.

According to Tuttosport, Modric will be missing this evening at the Karaiskakis Stadium in Athens, having suffered a muscle strain in his right thigh in the closing minutes of the match against Frosinone. It will also force him to miss Monday’s trip to Cagliari.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In his place, Jashari will have a new chance at being the midfield anchor. The 24-year-old Swiss midfielder arrived in the summer of 2025 thanks to Igli Tare, who pursued him for two months, then snatched him from Club Brugge for €35.7m.

Jashari hasn’t quite blossomed yet and his story has been a complicated one. It started with a fractured fibula that sidelined him for two months at the end of August in his first season, while Adrien Rabiot’s arrival and top performances gave him extra competition.

Ultimately, Jashari made 17 appearances in his first season nine of them as a starter, with zero goals and one assist. Under Massimiliano Allegri, the former Luzern player racked up 880 minutes, but now under Ruben Amorim he’s already at 666, and it is destined to rise.

Tonight, as mentioned, he’ll be a starter and will already be approaching the total minutes he played in his entire first season by the end of November. So, has Jashari turned things around with Amorim? Not exactly.

In the summer, it was thought this would be his season, but after the initial tests the Portuguese coach decided to obviously continue with the two more experienced man Modric and Rabiot. Jashari then saw himself overtaken in the pecking order by Yunus Musah as well.

So far, he’s started seven times and has only impressed against RB Salzburg and Udines,, while he disappointed against Benfica, Bologna and Ferencvaros. Tonight, he’ll have another important chance to prove not only that he should stay at Milan, but that he can be a starter.

“I know I can do much better. Against Frosinone, it was a good match for me, but it’s not the level I want to show,” the Swiss declared on the eve of the game at a pre-match press conference.

“In the past, in the teams I played for, I was a central player or in the starting eleven, so I always played. I think with Milan I have to learn to be ready even if I don’t always play, and I hope to be decisive.” It all starts with a tough night in Athens.

#1639. Inside Jude Bellingham's life in Madrid: Kisses from elderly ladies, coffee shop bliss and finding love - England star feels at home as he nears new £500k-per-week deal

Published: 06:30 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 06:30 EST, 24 November 2026

Jude Bellingham has more than settled into his routine in Madrid, with the England star learning Spanish, integrating into his community and spending time with his girlfriend in a mansion worth a reported £5.3million ($7m) after three seasons at Real Madrid.

The 23-year-old's settled life in the Spanish capital is thought to play a significant role in Bellingham's decision to sign an improved deal with the club, with Daily Mail Sport reporting on Monday that the midfielder is set to become one of Europe's highest earners.

New terms would see Bellingham raking in around £12.5million a year after tax until 2029, and will reportedly put him on par with his team-mate Vinicius Junior, whose latest deal is thought to be worth around £500,000 per week after tax.

But beyond the money, Bellingham has been flourishing turning out for the Spanish giants – both on and off the pitch.

Here, Daily Mail Sport details Bellingham's lifestyle in Spain, and the rituals that have grounded the player after his explosion into superstardom.

Jude Bellingham is inching closer to a new deal at Real Madrid to become one of Europe's highest earners

But more than just enjoying his football, Bellingham has made himself at home in the city (pictured at the Grand Prix of Spain in Madrid this year)

A recurring theme when Bellingham speaks of his love of living in Madrid stems from an established daily routine.

Speaking to his club just six months after he joined Los Blancos in the summer of 2023, Bellingham had already set up habits which helped him feel at home in the new city.

'I get up early to go to training, I train and then I head home,' Bellingham said. 'Sometimes I'll go out for a coffee near home or head into town to grab something to eat. Then I go back home to chill out in the garden for a bit if the weather is good and the sun's out.

'If my friends are over, we'll go out for dinner and then back home. It's great. You get to know the people at the places you visit more often. They don't see you as Jude Bellingham the footballer, but as Jude the guy who comes in for a coffee and that's great. The people I meet in the city really look after me. I feel at home.'

Over two years later, and the patterns are no different. The Calvin Klein ambassador told Vogue this month that his ideal downtime involves 'being in the company of my friends and family, having a coffee, going for a walk.

'You're always going to get recognised, but you're a bit safer in terms of not getting mobbed,' Bellingham said of his favourite spots on the fringes of the city, where many of his repeat haunts are located.

Not that Bellingham is a little averse to integrating with the community. In fact, mingling with the locals has been a positive aspect of Bellingham's life abroad, with the player admitting in the summer of 2025 that Spain was very much 'home'.

'When I go back to play with the national team, it's nice seeing people that I don't normally get to see – my family and friends – but I always feel more comfortable when I'm back in Madrid,' Bellingham said in an interview with FIFA. 'It's the weather, the people are so loving, the food.

'You mix all that together, as well as, especially, playing for Real Madrid… When you go out in public and the people see you, you see it's like a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity that they've had to meet you.

'They talk to you about the club and how much it means to them. A lot of the older ladies give me kisses on the cheeks and stuff like that! It's really nice.'

Bellingham has connected with new head coach Jose Mourinho since his arrival in the summer

Shortly after his move to Madrid Bellingham moved into a villa within the upscale complex at La Finca (flats inside the community pictured)

Bellingham and his girlfriend Ashyn Castro enjoy a life of habits when together in Madrid, involving coffee walks and going out for dinner (Source: Ashlyn Castro/Instagram)

The 23-year-old lives in his mansion with his mother Denise, who often drives him to training as he is without a license

Shortly after moving to Spain, Bellingham settled down in the exclusive La Finca neighbourhood, which plays host to a number of his team-mates including Kylian Mbappe and former club legends such as Zinedine Zidane, Cristiano Ronaldo and Iker Casillas.

The gated community is known as 'Madrid's Beverly Hills' to insiders and boasts extensive security to ensure the luxury villas inside the compound stay safe.

Bellingham is believed to have purchased his pricey six-bedroom home in 2023, moving into the complex, which boasts a home theatre, outdoor pool and gym according to Architectural Digest, with his mother Denise.

From there, his mum drives him to and from training, with the young star admitting in Vogue that despite his prodigious footballing talent, he remains borderline incapable in other aspects of life.

'I can't cook, I can't drive… I'm good at what I do, but everything else?' he joked. 'Not that great.

'I rely on my friends, my family to help me do stuff – chef, cleaner, mum, whoever else. That's where I'm at. I work hard every day and all day, and then when I get home, I've probably neglected learning how to do some of the more basic things. But there'll be a time and a place for that, I'm sure.'

In keeping with the idea that Bellingham has found his home in Spain, it stands to reason that the player has been working on his languages.

Bellingham revealed in Vogue that he has been learning Spanish for over two years, beginning in earnest just months after his move to the Santiago Bernabeu.

Confirming his aptitude for the language, Bellingham added: 'I think a big part of it is being confident enough to just speak.

'You know you're going to get stuff wrong, and you're probably not going to sound exactly right, (but if) people know what you're talking about, they'll probably think: "Fair play for trying".'

Castro and Bellingham have been dating for nearly two years since early 2025, having reportedly met on exclusive dating site Raya (Source: Ashlyn Castro/Instagram)

American model Castro is a frequent fixture in the stands whether Bellingham is playing for Madrid or England

With Bellingham settled in Madrid, his American model girlfriend Ashlyn Castro is, if not permanently based in the city, a regular visitor to both his La Finca villa and Real Madrid's home ground.

The former music video star and Bellingham have been dating since early 2025, with Castro becoming a frequent fixture at the Bernabeu alongside his mother Denise.

Castro has also been following his exploits for England too, travelling across the United States to follow the travails of Thomas Tuchel and Co as they reached the semi-finals at this summer's World Cup.

Most recently she was spotted in the stands closer to home however, with Bellingham and Castro snapped embracing after the final whistle blew on England's impressive win against Spain at Atletico Madrid's Metropolitano.

#1638. Manchester United Plan 20 Million Pound Bid For Bundesliga Defender

#1637. 'That's their problem' – Jose Mourinho sends clear message to Mbappe, Bellingham and Vinicius

By Naim Beneddra | 27 Nov 2026 16:17

Real Madrid head coach Jose Mourinho has insisted that Kylian Mbappe, Jude Bellingham and Vinicius Junior are subject to the same selection criteria as the rest of his squad, warning that any dissatisfaction with being named on the bench is a matter for the players themselves.

The Portuguese manager was questioned about the status of his attacking stars during Friday's press conference ahead of Saturday's La Liga encounter with Alaves at the Santiago Bernabeu.

Madrid's recent improvement has coincided with Bellingham's excellent form and a resurgence from Vinicius, who has faced increased competition for his place following the summer arrival of Yan Diomande. Mourinho, however, believes that the collective spirit he has established since returning to the Spanish capital is helping him manage those individual ambitions.

Speaking at his pre-match press conference, Mourinho dismissed the suggestion that certain members of his squad enjoy preferential treatment.

"If one day they are on the bench and they don't like it, that's their problem," said the former Chelsea and Manchester United manager, who stressed that Mbappe, Bellingham and Vinicius were on an equal footing with their teammates.

Mourinho acknowledged that Mbappe has yet to start a match on the bench this season, while Bellingham has only done so once. He explained that the difference in playing time between the pair and other members of the squad was justified by their performances.

Mbappe has registered 19 goals and five assists in 18 appearances across all competitions this season, while Bellingham demonstrated his importance to the team once again in Tuesday's 5-1 Champions League victory over PSV Eindhoven.

Madrid were trailing at half time when Mourinho introduced the England international, who subsequently scored a superb goal and provided the assist for Vinicius to complete the scoring.

Such performances help explain why Mourinho has been reluctant to rest either player. The Portuguese nevertheless insisted that the team's objectives take precedence over individual ambitions and expressed satisfaction at how his players have accepted that principle.

The debate surrounding Madrid's attacking options has intensified in recent weeks, with Vinicius returning to form after a difficult start to the campaign and a four-match La Liga suspension.

The Brazilian made an important contribution from the bench in last weekend's 2-1 victory over Celta Vigo before finding the net against PSV, giving Mourinho another selection decision to make ahead of the Alaves fixture.

However, Mourinho rejected the idea that Vinicius and Diomande should be regarded as rivals, explaining that both players share the same objectives and that the Brazilian has retained the support of his teammates throughout his difficult spell.

The Madrid boss also dismissed concerns about the atmosphere within the dressing room, revealing that he has not encountered any significant problems during his first five months back at the club.

His satisfaction with the current squad extends to his plans for the January transfer window, with Mourinho making it clear that he would prefer to finish the season with the players already at his disposal.

"I don't want anyone to leave either; the door is closed," the Portuguese explained after ruling out the need for new signings.

That stance is particularly noteworthy given the limited opportunities afforded to some of Madrid's younger attacking players. With Rodrygo also working his way back from a long-term injury, competition for places could become even greater during the second half of the campaign.

Mourinho's comments suggest that he would rather manage that competition internally than reduce his attacking options midway through a season in which Madrid are competing for honours on several fronts.

#1635. EPL Prepares for Most Exciting Title Race in Years

Home » Home 2 » EPL Prepares for Most Exciting Title Race in Years

Now that all of the top four English Premier League teams have had a chance to play each other, we find ourselves looking at one of the most wide open title races in recent memory. As of this writing, the league leaders are only separated by a mere six points. With the exception of Manchester City, we could very well see a new face hoisting the Premier League trophy at the end of the season.

For much of the year, it looked like Arsenal would be in the running for its first league title in more than a decade. With the Gunners’ recent victory against Leicester City, they are very much back in the conversation. Danny Welbeck returned to the pitch for the first time this season and made an immediate impact for Arsene Wenger’s squad, scoring the last-minute, game-winning goal to propel the team to within two points of the top spot. Given that even more key players are set to return to action for Arsenal in the coming months, this is easily the best shot they have had of winning a championship since their undefeated 2003-04 season.

Another surprise team that certainly deserves its own mention is Tottenham Hotspur. Following the club’s controversial defeat of Manchester City, the Spurs sit in second place, a mere two points behind Leicester City and ahead of Arsenal on goal differential. Tottenham have yet to win a title in the Premier League era and they have not won an English championship since 1961. The team has done a superb job of backing up star striker Harry Kane with a glut of promising young players, and their goal tally only helps to reinforce the wisdom behind the strategy of manager Mauricio Pochettino.

Meanwhile, Manchester City is still hoping to snag its third title as something of a swan song for exiting manager Manuel Pellegrini. It was recently announced that the club had hired Pep Guardiola . from Bayern Munich to take charge of the team beginning with next season. Thus, Pellegrini has been forced to endure the rest of the campaign as a dead man walking. Despite the impending exit of Pellegrini, City are still in the race for the Premier League title in addition to both the F.A. Cup and Champions League. Theoretically, the club could pull off a treble, if it can manage a solid string of performances during the final half of the season.

At the beginning of the season, it was expected that the usual suspects would once again dominate the league. Many predicted the reigning champs at Chelsea to repeat their success. However, a shocking season has seen the team part ways with controversial manager Jose Mourinho and struggle to remain in the top half of the tables with hopes of a Champions League spot dashed long ago.

For the first time in years, there’s a chance to see a completely new team win the league. No matter which club you support, there’s no denying that this has made for one of the most thrilling contests in recent memory. In a league where money talks, small fish like Leicester City are surprising everyone, and we can only hope that this means a new era of parity for the Premier League.

#1632. Como vs Juventus - prediction, team news, lineups

By Jonathan O'Shea | 27 Nov 2026 16:43, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 16:48

Midweek winners in Europe, Como and Juventus will resume their pursuit of Serie A's top four when they clash at Stadio Sinigaglia on Sunday.

Both teams are on track to qualify directly for the last 16 in their continental campaigns, but they currently trail Italy's top quartet.

Ascending to third place in the Champions League table - above the likes of Liverpool, Arsenal and Barcelona - Como continued their incredible European exploits on Tuesday evening, with a 1-0 home win over AEK Athens.

The little Lombardy club are firmly on course to reach the knockout phase on their continental debut, and they are still in an open Serie A title race.   Though they recently lost to Inter Milan once again, normal service was resumed last weekend, when Como beat Cagliari 2-0 at the Sinigaglia.

Victory kept them in touch with both Milan sides and the two unbeaten Rome clubs, and the Lariani have claimed a club record 26 points from their first 12 top-flight fixtures.

Unbeaten as hosts this season, Cesc Fabregas has seen his team concede just one goal in five home games, including four consecutive clean sheets - against Roma, Sassuolo, Venezia and Cagliari.

Como now face a crucial clash in the fight for Champions League qualification, and success on Sunday would open up an eight-point lead over Juventus.

Before doing the double over Juve last season, they had not beaten the Turin giants at home since 1952, but a pair of 2-0 wins helped them sneak past the Bianconeri to claim fourth place in the end.

Reflecting their sudden change in status, Juventus have never before faced Como while trailing in the Serie A standings, yet that is now the situation they face.

While the Lariani were dining at Europe’s top table, Juve extended their unbeaten run through this season's Europa League in midweek, defeating Omonia 4-1 in Turin.

Posing a potential solution to their striker problems, Jeff Ekhator found the net on his first start for the club, and across all competitions the Bianconeri have scored 14 goals across their last five games.

In Europe, Juventus are set to cruise through as one of the top eight finishers - having claimed 13 points from a possible 15 so far - but it has been a more mixed picture on the domestic scene.

Despite thumping Venezia 4-0 last week, Luciano Spalletti's injury-hit squad lag 11 points behind league leaders Lazio in sixth place, partly due to their sub-par away form.

Juve’s Serie A record on the road is two wins, two draws and two defeats - with eight goals scored and eight conceded - so visiting Como will surely cause some concern.

Como are still missing ex-Juventus striker Moise Kean, plus Willy Kambwala and Jesus Rodriguez, but Fabregas could have two wingers back from injury this weekend.

Jayden Addai and Assane Diao both face fitness tests, while midfielder Maxence Caqueret is a strong doubt.

Without Kean, Tasos Douvikas should continue to lead the Lariani’s front line, having scored 11 goals in all competitions this season.

Meanwhile, Juve’s top Serie A scorer is Brazilian centre-back Bremer with a modest three goals, though Nick Woltemade has been directly involved in three across his last two league games and is faring well in the Europa League.

The German striker must compete with Ekhator and Randal Kolo Muani to start at the Sinigaglia, where Spalletti will be without several key men.

Kenan Yildiz, Khephren Thuram and captain Manuel Locatelli are still sidelined, while Nico Gonzalez remains a doubt; more positively, Kerim Alajbegovic and Pierre Kalulu could both be named on the bench.

Butez; Couto, Chalobah, Ramon, Valle; Perrone, Milla; Da Cunha, Paz, Baturina; Douvikas

Vicario; Celik, Bremer, Lucumi, Cabal; Luiz, Koopmeiners; Conceicao, McKennie, Kolo Muani; Woltemade

Two of Italy's tightest defences will face off on Sunday night: since Spalletti's arrival in Turin last November, Juventus have kept 19 clean sheets and Como have 20.

While the hosts have been far more convincing, Juve are putting together a good run of results and their long absence list is starting to clear.

#1631. Gary Neville slaps himself in the FACE in bizarre on-air moment after Man United's humiliation at Anfield - weeks after claiming his old club are 'in a better place' than Liverpool

Published: 04:43 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 10:28 EST, 24 November 2026

Gary Neville showcased the dramatic decline of Manchester United this season as he bizarrely slapped himself in the face on Sky Sports after his former side's 4-0, 10-man, defeat to Liverpool at Anfield.

Neville's dramatic example of Man United's lack of hunger and sharpness came in stark contrast to his pre-season proclamations for the side, when he informed his co-pundit Jamie Carragher that he believed that then-manager Michael Carrick's starting XI was stronger than Liverpool's after a summer recruitment drive.

Instead, Man United saw their numbers reduced inside the opening stages of the game after a reckless challenge by Leny Yoro, and 2-0 down after 13 minutes, with the club legend resorting to drastic methods to convey the side's weaknesses.

Of his old club's defenders, he said: 'I never see any of them on their toes, alert, looking like they've got something fixed in here', before pointing to his head.

'I never see any of them look like that,' he added. 'They look like that -'

Neville then stared into the middle distance for a few moments to share the blankness he sees on the faces of the back line, before spitting: 'Wake up!'

Gary Neville took to slapping himself to convey the lack of focus he sees in Man United's stars

The club legend had previously tipped his old side to have a stronger XI than Liverpool's

But when the two teams met at Anfield, Man United were left woefully exposed after going down to 10 men

The Overlap broadcaster then slapped his own face a number of times repeating 'wake up!' before adding: 'You play for Man United'.

The gesture left Carragher in stitches, with the Anfield icon collapsing onto the sofa in hysterics - although less impressed with Roy Keane, who displayed his usual sangfroid.

So tickled by the moment was the former Liverpool star that he later changed his profile picture on social media site X to a still image of Neville's hand catching his face.

Neville had more sharp criticism for Man United's defensive selection assessing the inclusion of Matthijs de Ligt in the starting line-up.

The Dutch defender has been out of Premier League action for 51 weeks after suffering a back injury, but was named by Mauricio Pochettino in his first-ever XI.

'I have a lot of sympathy for him,' Neville admitted. 'It's like playing football after having six pints. It's a strange feeling.

'I have a lot of sympathy for him, it's alarming to watch.'

Less sympathy for Man United's players came from Keane, who attacked the team - and Neville and Carragher - after the heavy defeat at Anfield confirmed the club's worst start in over 53 years.

The firebrand midfielder was on his usual caustic form as he assessed the damage, hitting out at those who might have accepted the score line, having feared a greater deficit.

'If I hear that one more time from the lads in the commentary that 4-0 is not too bad when you're down to 10 men - has a team ever got a result with 10 men before?' Keane said immediately after the final whistle. 'It can be done.

'I thought United were desperate. I thought they were so bad and everyone and Nev, who played for Man United saying 4-0 ain't bad.'

'(The red card) doesn't help but you're telling me they couldn't have done better? They lost 4-0 with 10 men, that's not too bad? Has a team ever got a result with 10 men? It can be done. At least show a bit more fight, a bit more quality - I can't believe what I'm hearing from people.

'You played for the club, saying 4-0 isn't too bad. Wow. Fans are applauding. Applauding what? Performing rubbish. Liverpool were excellent, but how easy did United make it for them? I can't believe what I'm watching sometimes.

'This team two years ago finished 15th. The last year or two, we're talking. We're blaming the board, blaming ownership, blaming managers.

'When do the players take responsibility for some decision-making? Liverpool probably should have scored eight, probably eight or nine, unbelievable chances they had. And everyone's coming off the pitch saying 4 is not too bad? I feel like swearing.'

The difference between the two teams felt a far cry from Neville's late-summer prediction, when he told Carragher that he had greater hopes for Carrick and Man United over incoming manager Andoni Iraola at Liverpool.

'I think Manchester United are currently in a better place than Liverpool,' Neville said in August. 'Would you agree?'

Carragher said that he did not, and will have been confident in his assessment on Sunday night.
