#1576. Fenerbahce vs BB Erzurumspor - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Cole | 27 Nov 2026 19:12, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 19:14

Fenerbahce will aim to strengthen their position in the upper half of the Turkish Super Lig table when they welcome BB Erzurumspor to Chobani Stadium on Sunday.

The hosts sit sixth with 20 points from 12 matches, while the visitors are 13th on 14 points and are looking to end a three-match losing run.

Emre Belozoglu's tenure at Fenerbahce has been impressive so far, with the team remaining unbeaten under his leadership after playing four matches across all competitions.

His tenure kicked off with a 3-2 win over Liverpool in the Champions League before the Yellow Canaries recorded a 5-0 away victory over Corum.

That result preceded a 2-2 draw against Kocaelispor in the league, the only game they have failed to win under the manager so far, but they quickly returned to winning ways in midweek when they beat Shakhtar Donetsk 1-0 away from home.

However, there is still plenty of work to do for the Yellow Canaries in the Super Lig, as they are already 11 points off the top, having failed to win half of their dozen league games so far this season (W6, D2, L4).

Despite those dropped points, Fenerbahce have been the division's most productive attacking team, scoring 31 goals, and they will hope to overwhelm their opponents with their attack as they look to bounce back from defeat in their last home league game, when they lost 2-1 to Goztepe.

Further reason for optimism will be the hosts' record in this fixture, having faced Erzurumspor six times without defeat and winning their last five meetings.

Erzurumspor, meanwhile, have suffered three consecutive league defeats after a promising run earlier in the campaign, losing 1-0 to Goztepe last time out, having previously been beaten 2-1 by Caykur Rizespor and 3-1 at home by Corum.

This recent poor streak follows an encouraging run of four matches without defeat, during which they won three times and drew once while keeping three clean sheets, a far cry from their last three matches, in which they have conceded six goals.

Serkan Ozbalta will be concerned about his team's poor run extending, not only because of their unfavourable head-to-head record with Fenerbahce, but also their away record this season, with just one win in six matches on the road, losing three times and drawing twice.

Erzurumspor have also struggled to prevent the Yellow Canaries from scoring, having conceded at least two goals in their four visits to this ground, with at least three scored in each of the last three, all of which they lost.

Fenerbahce are expected to remain without Nathan Ake and Marco Asensio, two of their starters who have missed the last couple of games.

Jayden Oosterwolde is also listed as unavailable through injury, while Amara Diouf is considered doubtful, with the young forward recovering from a muscle issue.

Mason Greenwood has scored in three of the last four matches and is expected to play an important role from the start yet again, while Vedat Muriqi will hope his goal in the Champions League earns him a starting spot over Romelu Lukaku once more.

Erzurumspor have no confirmed absentees listed ahead of the match, although their final selection will depend on fitness assessments closer to kickoff.

Gyrano Kerk and Ibrahim Diabate started as the front two last time out and are likely to retain their places for this one.

Ederson; Semedo, Skriniar, Oppong, Brown; Guendouzi, Yuksek; Greenwood, Kahveci, Aydin; Muriqi

Taskiran; Gergxhaliu, Yumlu, Mujakic; Ovacikli, Baiye, Owusu, Rodriguez, Giorbelidze; Kerk, Diabate

Fenerbahce have enough attacking quality to make life difficult for Erzurumspor, particularly given their opponents' recent defensive struggles.

The visitors should find it difficult to keep the hosts quiet for 90 minutes, and a comfortable home victory looks the most likely outcome.

#1575. Arteta on Saliba, scoring goals, the January window, and more

Let’s do a quick Saturday round-up, starting with Mikel Arteta on William Saliba. I was a bit surprised that he didn’t feature against Borussia Dortmund in midweek, which could tell you something about where he is in terms of building his fitness, or maybe what the manager thought of the opposition (while also applying the context of the French international’s long absence).

At his press conference yesterday, the manager was asked if the plan had been to give him minutes on Tuesday had the game been scoreline been more comfortably in Arsenal’s favour, and said:

It depends, but obviously he hasn’t played football for a long time. He can play a certain amount of minutes, and we have to be really sure – especially in those kinds of games – that when he comes in, he can sustain a certain amount of minutes otherwise we won’t have enough subs or opportunities to make those subs. He’s training well, he’ll have minutes in the next few games, and then he’ll be able to prove what he’s already done, which is show what an unbelievable player he is.

It is interesting to look at the fixture list and wonder where exactly those minutes are going to come from. It’s Man City on Sunday, then Brentford and Sp*rs away, before Real Madrid and then Bournemouth who are on a great run of form and who beat us at home last season. Those are games where you’re going to need players at their sharpest, and Saliba is someone who has, in the past, needed a few matches under his belt to find his best rhythm.

Perhaps one answer is about being more comfortable. There were questions about Arsenal scoring goals too, and when asked if it matters how many his team score as long as they win, Arteta said:

I prefer to win by five, or six, or seven, for sure. I’m going to enjoy the game much more, especially the last few minutes. The boys are going to have more fun. I think scoring goals is ultimately what creates a good feeling, joy, happiness, celebration around the stands. It’s the most important thing in football, apart from winning.

What scoring more also does is allow a manager to make different changes. If you have a 1-0 lead, you’re not going to disrupt your central-defensive partnership because it’s so tight. You’re reluctant to take off your all-action central midfielder because he’s so important to your side. If you’re 3-0 up with 20 minutes to go, you have more leeway to make those substitutions, and over the course of a season that can protect some players for becoming overly-fatigued as well as providing opportunities to others. How nice would it be, particularly with this run of tricky fixtures, if he could do exactly that?

Here’s a stat from the presser: if Arsenal score tomorrow it will be the 700th goal under Arteta, reaching that tally 23 games quicker than Arsene Wenger. That doesn’t mean a great deal, but it’s mildly interesting, and who can ask for more on a chilly November Saturday? I’d like to see us hit 704 goals tomorrow, not being greedy.

Martin Odegaard spoke to Sky Sports about a new deal, and sounded a very positive note, saying:

It’s not something I stress about. I’ve said it so many times, I’m so happy here, I love it here. Hopefully I can stay for many more years – and I think the club is happy as well.

So it’s no stress, we’ll sort it out. I want to win more things here for sure. I want to win everything with Arsenal. The Premier League again, the Champions League, the cups – that’s what we want. We want to win everything. The rest of it, the individual stuff, will come as a result of what happens with the team. The team is the most important bit.

For me, he’s an important player to tie down. There aren’t many like him around, and if there was the vague outline of a succession plan in the shape of Ethan Nwaneri, that doesn’t seem to be particularly likely at this point. The next young man up is probably Max Dowman, but he’s still only 16. In four years time he’ll only be 20, which is ridiculous really, and in that period of time we have to be conscious of how he is integrated and developed.

Odegaard remains Arsenal’s creative hub in many ways, and this season looks like a player who has shaken off the impact of a series of injuries which prevented him from finding form and rhythm. So far this season he has created 43 chances across the Premier League and Champions League, the most of any player in the team (with Declan Rice and Noni Madueke behind him), and I think securing his future makes a lot of sense. With other renewals under way, let’s hope this is one they can sort out without much delay.

Finally, the manager was asked about the January window, and whether we might make a first addition to the squad since Leandro Trossard (and others) were brought in in January 2023:

We’ve always been very active in the transfer window. Especially that we have certain issues. Have we managed to get a deal over the line? Sometimes not. So we will see if there is an opportunity there and something that we believe is going to make a difference for the team.

In midweek, James reported that Arsenal are ‘aware’ the departures of Trossard and Gabriel Martinelli (as well as Gabriel Jesus let’s not forget), have left the squad light on that left hand side, and for many that’s the key for the winter window. That said, centre-forward is another position where you could make a strong argument that we need to improve. It’s always a tricky time in January, but not impossible, so let’s see what happens in due course. There’s plenty of football to play before then.

Finally for today, Arsenal Women relieved manager Renee Slegers of her duties yesterday after a poor run of form and results. Tim writes about her over on Arseblog News, and he and Jamie recorded an Arsenal Women Arsecast last night which you can find here or in all the usual podcast places.

#1574. Bloodthirsty Brighton feast on rattled Arsenal

Overpowered and overrun, Arsenal were subjected to the sort of gruelling treatment they usually inflict on their opponents. Mikel Arteta’s side did not look anything like Premier League champions here, as Brighton and Hove Albion produced a stunning performance full of swarming energy and breathless bravery.

In the biggest test of their season so far, Arsenal fell woefully short of the standards they have set themselves over the past few campaigns. This sort of thing simply does not happen to Arteta’s side. Well, it did not happen. Not before this monstering on the south coast, where the Brighton fans were whipped into a frenzy by the brilliance of Fabian Hürzeler’s players.

Brighton were everything that Arsenal are expected to be: aggressive, inventive and dominant across the field. They even scored with a set-piece, as one of Arsenal’s great strengths became a sudden weakness. Everywhere Arteta looked, the foundational truths of his team were being shaken by a Brighton storm. It was their first defeat by a three-goal margin since May 2023, also against Brighton.

Remarkably, this is now the third consecutive season in which Brighton have beaten the reigning Premier League champions. They are rarely happier than when they are on the hunt against more illustrious opponents, working as a team to snap at heels and then attacking in numbers. They are known as the Seagulls, but they played more like a pack of bloodthirsty wolves. The ferocity of their off-the-ball work, especially in the first half, was extraordinary.

Not for a long time have Arsenal been as rattled as they were here. David Raya misplaced passes, Gabriel Magalhães lost duels and Bruno Guimarães chased the ball in vain. It was Brighton’s Pascal Gross, rather than Arsenal’s Martin Odegaard, who shaped the game in midfield. It was Brighton’s Charalampos Kostoulas, rather than Arsenal’s Kai Havertz, who offered incisive class in attack.

Gross and Kostoulas both struck from range in a one-sided first half, before Chema Andrés added the third after the break. At half-time, Arteta had sprinted down the tunnel towards the dressing room. Whatever messages he gave to his players, they either did not sink in or did not work. By the end, Arsenal were lucky the scoreline was not even more humiliating.

Arteta’s players had come through some tricky assignments in winning their first seven matches of this season, but this was their toughest test yet and they failed it badly. They did not handle the emotions of the occasion particularly well, either: in stoppage time, a frustrated Declan Rice kicked out at Malick Yalcouyé. He was perhaps fortunate to avoid a red card.

It was the first time that Rice and Guimarães had started alongside each other for Arsenal and it quickly became clear that their £180m partnership will need some work. Arsenal would have hoped their experience in the Premier League would allow for an instant connection but, evidently, that is not the case. Guimarães was hooked after 60 minutes, but might easily have been removed at the break.

Both managers had a similar assessment of the match and how it was won: Brighton did the basics far better than Arsenal. “How we wanted to approach this game was getting into it through small wins,” Hürzeler said. “Everyone speaks about a goal or chance as a win, but a small win can be the first throw-in, the first corner, win the first header, win the first tackle. These small things. If you win these small steps, and celebrate them as a win, then you can gain bigger and bigger wins.”

It was typical of Brighton that one of their new signings produced an excellent performance in midfield. Andrés, a 21-year-old Spaniard signed from Stuttgart at the end of the transfer window, looks to be the latest gem identified by their data-led recruitment model. No one inside the Amex Stadium was thinking about Carlos Baleba, sold to Manchester United, when Andrés made his tackles and won his headers.

Another new signing, centre-back Luka Vuskovic, was similarly impressive at the back. Signed for £46m from Tottenham Hotspur, Vuskovic looks more than capable of going to the top of the game.

This was perhaps the first occasion this season in which Arsenal missed William Saliba, the injured centre-back who has been so fundamental to their success in recent years. The Frenchman can always be relied on to provide calmness and composure at the back, even under intense pressure. Without him, Arsenal were uncharacteristically jittery.

“The amount of technical errors we did in our own half...” Arteta bemoaned. “We didn’t respect any principle of play that you have to get out of those man-to-man situations. That put us always on the back foot.”

Gross, who at 35 is playing as well as ever, opened the scoring with a low shot from range after 31 minutes. Kostoulas then struck the second, from a similar distance, after some end-to-end action resulted in Arsenal’s midfield and defence melting away. The third was the most simple, as Andrés headed in at the back post from an inswinging corner.

Arsenal did have some chances, with Havertz missing the best of them, but there was never a sense that Brighton were vulnerable. The pressure on the home side was never sustained. For Arteta, who now has an extended international break in which to ruminate on this defeat, it all made for an unfamiliar and unexpected pain.

Mikel Arteta said his Arsenal players failed to “respect the game” as their perfect start to the season was ended in stunning style by a brilliant Brighton performance.

Arsenal’s capitulation on the south coast led to their first defeat of the campaign and Arteta admitted that Brighton had a different “edge” and “bite” throughout the match. The Arsenal manager also said the 3-0 loss represented a “big lesson” for his players.

“There are certain basics you need to accomplish in football, especially in the Premier League, that we were very far from,” Arteta said. “From the first throw-in you could sense it, it was so clear.

“It was a really disappointing result and performance. Brighton were another gear up from us. We were extremely poor technically and were not respecting the game.

“It is not going to take away what the team has done in the last six or seven weeks since coming back from the World Cup. What we have done and the way we have competed, and the amount of games we have won, has been remarkable. But this is a big lesson for all of us to understand what it takes to win at this level.”

Arteta added that his team did not “respect the principles of play” that were required against Brighton’s intense pressing, and also said his players were guilty of numerous technical errors.

“Credit to Brighton for what they have done because they have overcome us and they had another edge,” Arteta said. “There are a lot of moments when the ball is 50/50 and it changes hands and most of the time it was for them.”

Brighton are the Premier League’s top scorers this season with 16 goals in five matches so far, and this emphatic victory took them up to third place in the table.

“It was a special win,” Fabian Hürzeler, the Brighton head coach, said. “Not only because we played the best team in England but because of the performance. I am really proud of my team. It’s always important to enjoy these moments. We were horrible to play against. My players really trust each other on the pitch.”

Two things, one give credit to them. In the manner that they played and committed to every single action. We were below the standards that are required for us but in the Premier League as well.

When you miss chances like we did it becomes impossible. I want to congratulate Brighton for what they’ve done. It’s a big lesson for us to learn. If I have to describe how the team has played and competed in the last six or seven weeks, has been expectational but today has been a big lesson.

A very disappointing result and performance. Full credit to Brighton the manner they went about the game, they were a different gear from us. We didn’t do the basics right for long periods, especially in the first half. We didn’t win enough duels, and any second balls and that stretches you.

We were poor technically when we had the ball in our own half, we didn’t apply the principles that you need against a team that wants to press you man to man.

Arteta: "There are certain basics that you need to accomplish in the Premier League that we were very far from. The amount of technical errors we did... we didn't respect any principle of play. We were always on the back foot. They had another edge."

Beating the current champions and maybe the best team in England is something special. The result is nice but the performance is what makes it special, the boys showed real courage, real intensity and they were horrible to play against because we did the basics right.

Intensity, intensity, winning the personal duels...we have to have the belief to compete with the best teams in the league. My players really trust each other on the pitch. If one player is out then another can replace him.

Overall we wanted to be really good in every phase. We needed to be at the highest level. We go game by game. After the international break we have a lot of games. After wins like this we have to stay humble and understand why we had this win. We have to keep on going.

Our 125 anniversary & one of the best days! 💫 pic.twitter.com/YbZLTFPpWN

I thought we showed great intensity, waited for mistakes and punished Arsenal. It was a strong performance, a very complete performance.

We won the ball high up and attacked really fast. After the last two wins we are full of confidence and wanted to finish really strong before the international break.

I feel really good. I can’t complain. I just try to help the team when I can. I really enjoy life in Brighton, I’m loving it.

I know after the international break we play every three days and a lot of the lads are not used to that. It will be tough. I hope we can compete. We have a big squad this season.

Pascal Gross pulling the strings. 🔎 @Microsoft pic.twitter.com/DAgVsG2B3W

Brighton have beaten the reigning Premier League champions in three consecutive seasons.

Like Everton, Newcastle labour to a home win which should have been more comfortable. It would have been had Wissa scored his penalty, but it was a nervy finish as Hull pushed for an equaliser after Cho’s goal.

Everton up to fifth but they made hard work of that against Ipswich’s 10 men, but Thierno Barry’s goal proves the difference. Barry unfortunate that his second did not stand because of a contentious offside check.

One of the outstanding team performances of the season so far from Brighton, and it will take some beating between now and May. Arsenal were loose defensively in open play and from set-pieces, and were smothered by Brighton’s pressing. Arteta’s team beaten for the first time this season and emphatically so. Arsenal’s first defeat by a three-goal margin since May 2023.

Just three minutes of stoppage time remaining, but Hull are still pushing bodies forward.

Hull are knocking on the door at St James’ Park, and Newcastle are hanging on to their lead rather than pressing for a third goal.

Matt O’Riley has missed two great chances to make it four. Brighton have not given Arsenal a sniff. It will be interesting to hear how stern Arteta is in his post-match assessment.

Kai Havertz shoots straight at the goalkeeper when clean through, and that is surely Arsenal’s last chance of an unlikely comeback gone. Brighton have pushed Arsenal back for much of the season half, they have not been sitting on a lead.

At St James’ Park, Hull have pulled a goal back through Cho to set up a nervy finish for Newcastle.

The forward is shown a second yellow card for diving, and Ipswich’s hopes appear to be dwindling at the Hill Dickinson Stadium.

What a farcical five minutes we have had, from an absurd disallowed goal for Everton to a ridiculous red card for Abdul Fatawu, banished for a second bookable offence - which was diving. There is going to be plenty said about Thierno Barry’s second goal being chalked out because, when you see it, you will wonder what it was for. These are the situations with which I struggle most - if players do not appeal for a wrongdoing, if they don’t feel they have been the victims of an injustice, why are officials getting involved?

Thierno Barry thought he had made it two for Everton, but the goal has been ruled out because Brennan Johnson was judged to be interfering with play and offside. You’re never getting those this weekend after the Enzo Fernandez incident.

Arsenal undone from a corner, swung to the back post and Chema Andres rose above everyone to head home.

This is a remarkable performance by Brighton, who have battered and bullied the champions from the start. Three-nil, and they have even beaten Arsenal at their own game by scoring a set-piece.

I am struggling to remember the last time Arsenal were overrun and outplayed as comprehensively as this. It’s a thrashing.

No half-time subs from Mikel Arteta, which is a little surprising given Arsenal’s predicament.

The undisputed highlight of the afternoon so far – Raspberry Beret has just been played during the half-time interval and you will agree that this is Prince’s finest work. We feel the need to bring this to your attention because, really, the final 15 minutes of the first half were a hotchpotch and if Everton don’t raise themselves, they will find trouble.

Another shot from outside the box as Arsenal’s defenders backed off, and the Greek striker found the bottom corner. What a first half for Brighton, Arsenal need to pull something out of the fire in the second half. Just before the goal, Saka had a chance after a deflected Odegaard shot.

Brighton’s second goal was an even better hit than their first. End-to-end football resulted in Kostoulas having space 20 yards from Arsenal’s goal. It’s another thumping low finish. Brilliant, breathless half of football by Brighton.

As half-time approaches, Arsenal have mustered just one shot on goal worth 0.03 expected goals. When they have moved the ball beyond Brighton’s press, they have not done anywhere near enough with it.

This fixture last season was especially bad-tempered, with the Brighton fans (and manager) repeatedly accusing Arsenal of time-wasting. The memories of that defeat are clearly still fresh in the minds of the Brighton supporters, who are roaring with rage at every perceived delay by the visitors, despite the fact that Arsenal are losing. The bad blood is adding to the intensity of the occasion.

Ipswich don’t play like a team that is short of confidence and quality. You might assume, if you haven’t seen much of them, that they are destined for a season of toil but there is definite quality with Gary O’Neill’s ranks, including Abdul Fatawu, who has been magnetic in drawing your eye to him. They might be a goal down but they are playing as if they are a goal in front.

Arsenal had just enjoyed a spell of control, but trail to a goal from one of the league’s in-form players. Gross whips a shot from just outside the box around Raya and in off the post.

Brighton have the lead at the Amex and it’s their captain, Pascal Gross, who has provided it. Superb long-range effort, in off the near post. On the overall balance of play, Brighton deserve that. It’s reward for their courage and willingness to go after Arsenal, rather than sitting back.

It took almost 20 minutes but Arsenal have found their feet in this game now. They are starting to find avenues through Brighton’s aggressive pressing and have made a few promising runs in behind, through Havertz and Saka. This is a high quality match.

No goals at the Amex, but Brighton are the team making the running, Arsenal struggling to play out from their own half and are yet to register a shot on goal.

Barry kept himself onside and turned the ball into the back of the net with his stomach. He did well to avoid a handball.

Bright start from Everton and they have the goal they deserve, albeit it came in fortuitous circumstances. James Tarkowski’s volley clattered into Thierno Barry and the deflection took it away from Christian Walton in Ipswich’s goal. Barry now has five goals for the season and, while he is raw, it’s an invaluable contribution.

A storming response to a bad night at Leeds from Newcastle, and it looks like being a long afternoon for Hull. Two down in seven minutes.

What a start for Newcastle United and what will really please manager Matthias Jaissle is the way both goals have come from his players winning important tackles.

The German was incensed by the lack of physicality and intensity in the heavy defeat to Leeds on Monday but the first goal for Joe Wilock came when Lewis Miley won a tackle on the edge of the Hull penalty box.

The second came when Sven Botman came away with the ball just inside his own half. On both occasions Harvey Barnes provided the assist. A short, intricate pass to Willock inside the box and then a surging, twisting run from the halfway line and the perfectly timed pass to Lewis Hall who stroked a first time shot into the bottom corner.

Hull have been outfought so far which is precisely the response Newcastle’s manager had demanded.

The home team are pressing high and all over Arsenal in the early stages. Raya has just made a save to deny Kostoulas.

Brighton have started brilliantly against the champions. They are hunting like wolves, pressing Arsenal with remarkable intensity. We have played seven minutes and I don’t think the ball has left Arsenal’s half.

Big chance for Everton to take the lead, but after great skill to turn his man at the edge of the box Brennan Johnson shoots wide with only the goalkeeper to beat.

The perfect start for Newcastle with all their injuries: Joe Willock has put the home side in a strong position against Hull with a clean strike inside three minutes.

We are under way at the Amex, St James’ Park and the Hill Dickinson.

Another famous face in the stands at Hill Dickinson Stadium today but this time it’s not about politicians. Wayne Rooney is here to watch his boyhood club and he will be hoping Everton can go into the international break unbeaten. An extra special cheer too before kick-off for Jarrad Branthwaite, who has just been called up for England duty. Plenty of Premier League clubs would like to sign Branthwaite, if they were given half a chance, but David Moyes has made it quite clear that Branthwaite: “Isn’t for sale - I want to keep my best players.”

He was not part of the match-day squad at Sunderland but Ben White’s injury has opened up a place, and Dowman fully deserves it after his two goals against Ipswich in the League Cup. Sam Dean has the story of his rise to stardom as well as what Arsenal are doing to nurture such a special talent.

Brighton are wearing a special “125 anniversary” kit today, to mark 125 years since the club was formed in 1901. It’s inspired by the colours of their first ever kit, which means an all-blue shirt, pale gold shorts and dark socks. Personally I would not allow such nonsense. But I don’t make the rules.

Spurs scored two late goals to salvage some pride against Aston Villa, but it is another defeat for Roberto De Zerbi’s team who have two points from five games. This Emi Buendia screamer put the game out of reach.

It has been a term tossed around liberally at Newcastle United since Matthias Jaissle arrived as manager, but what does “vertical football” actually mean?

It is the new buzzword in football analysis, the latest fashionable phrase to describe a “new” style of football, and it has been referenced multiple times by both Jaissle and Ross Wilson, the sporting director, since the German coach’s appointment last month.

For some of us of a certain age, vertical football just seems like clever new terminology to describe an old idea.

The right back was due to start for Newcastle against Hull City this afternoon – his first start since April – but has picked up another injury.

That will surely mean he is out of the England squad for the Nations League having also picked up a tournament-ending injury at the World Cup in the summer before the first group game.

Livramento only played 17 Premier League games for Newcastle last season, scuppering his chances of a summer move to Arsenal, missing huge chunks of the season with groin and hamstring issues.

Injuries are already cutting deep into the Newcastle squad, with four teenagers on the bench for the visit of Hull. None have played in the first team before and three of them – Michael Mills, Mason Miley and Kyrian Thompson are just 17–years-old.

Very excited for this one today. Arsenal have won all seven of their matches so far. Only once before in their history have they won their first eight games of a season - that was in 1903, when they were playing in the Second Division as Woolwich Arsenal. pic.twitter.com/iNBxoHl4Gc

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of today’s Premier League 3pm kick-offs, with Brighton vs Arsenal the pick of the three matches.

Brighton are the league’s top goalscorers so far this season and have amassed the most expected goals, but the champions have the league’s best defence and are seeking five wins from five to start their title defence. There is some welcome needle between Fabian Hurzeler and Mikel Arteta, dating back to Declan Rice’s contentious second yellow for delaying the restart two years ago, as well as the Brighton manager’s comments about Arsenal’s style of play in March.

That 1-0 Arsenal victory at the Amex coincided with Man City dropping points at home to Nottingham Forest on a pivotal night in the title race. Bukayo Saka scored a deflected shot in the ninth minute, and Arsenal held on from there in an ugly but resolute display.

With Saka, Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz fit and firing, as well as the introduction of Myles Lewis-Skelly and Bruno Guimaraes to Arteta’s midfield stable, Arsenal’s football has been more technical and enterprising so far this season. Brighton are one of the few teams who will back themselves to play through Arsenal’s press, which should make for an absorbing game.

Elsewhere, Newcastle are looking to bounce back from their shellacking at Leeds at home to surprise package Hull City. Mattias Jaissle’s team took four points from Liverpool and Spurs but there is concern about how many shots they are conceding. Hull remain unbeaten and continue to confound the odds and underlying data, but that surely cannot last forever.

Everton are also one of the division’s unbeaten teams, but will be targeting three points from a home game against Ipswich after three consecutive draws. Ipswich are sitting comfortably on six points after their win at Crystal Palace, though they did have the extra man for the majority at Selhurst Park.

#1573. Eyupspor vs Istanbul Basaksehir - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Cole | 27 Nov 2026 19:12

Eyupspor will be hoping to end their prolonged winless run when they welcome Istanbul Basaksehir to Esenyurt Necmi Kadioglu Stadium on Sunday.

The hosts are bottom of the Turkish Super Lig standings with just three points from 12 matches, while the Grey Owls sit seventh with 20 points and will be looking to continue their push towards the European places.

Mustafa Dalci has been unable to turn around Eyupspor's fortunes this season, with the Purple-Yellows enduring a difficult start to the campaign and remaining without a league victory in their last nine matches.

No other Super Lig side is on a longer losing streak than Eyupspor, who have lost each of their last nine league games, while they have failed to score in 10 of their 12 matches, netting just three times, the fewest in the division.

They are also comfortably the worst side defensively, having conceded 31 goals, three more than the next-worst defence, while they are currently on a two-match run without finding the net.

Their latest setback was a 1-0 loss away to Trabzonspor, and on Sunday, they welcome an opponent they have never beaten in four top-flight meetings, losing two and drawing two, leaving little optimism as they look to end a club-record run of consecutive Super Lig defeats.

Basaksehir, meanwhile, have enjoyed a much more encouraging run and arrive in Istanbul's western suburbs having won their last three league matches.

Their latest victory was an entertaining 4-2 home triumph over Corum, with Bertug Yildirim scoring a hat-trick after coming off the bench to help his side secure all three points as they came back from a two-goal deficit, scoring all four goals in the final 13 minutes plus stoppage time.

That result followed a 1-0 victory against Goztepe and a 2-1 win over Kocaelispor, with Nuri Sahin's side demonstrating greater consistency and attacking confidence in recent weeks, scoring more goals than any other side over the last five games (13), while only three teams have accumulated more than their 12 points over that period.

The Grey Owls will also be confident of winning consecutive away matches, having ended their four-match winless run on the road (D1, L3) with victory over Goztepe on their last trip.

Istanbul Basaksehir Turkish Super Lig form:

Eyupspor are expected to be without Lenny Pintor, Talha Ulvan and Simone Giordano, who are all dealing with injuries.

Their absences could limit Dalci's options, particularly in defence and the attacking positions, while Yusuf Barasi could be considered for a starting role as the hosts look for greater threat in the final third.

Basaksehir will be without Christopher Operi, who remains sidelined with an injury, while Yusuf Sari is also unavailable.

Yildirim's hat-trick against Corum could earn him a starting opportunity, although Davie Selke remains an option in attack.

Bilgin; Yasar, Demir, Jules; Costa, Akman, Ilter, Raux-Yao, M. Demir; Abdullahi, Barasi

Eyupspor may attempt to keep the contest close through a compact defensive approach, but their prolonged winless run and Basaksehir's attacking quality point towards an away victory.

The visitors should have enough to secure three points without necessarily needing to produce another high-scoring performance.

#1572. 'Moments aren't enough': Inside Ethan Nwaneri's struggles on loan at Borussia Dortmund ahead of his return to the Emirates tonight - as Arsenal face dilemma over talented youngster suffering crisis of confidence

Published: 21:00 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 12:27 EST, 24 November 2026

Despite being shipped off to Germany’s finest finishing school for young English talent, Ethan Nwaneri’s time at Borussia Dortmund is already at a crossroads.

The 19-year-old joined the Bundesliga side on a season-long loan in September after enduring a frustrating five-month spell at Marseille earlier in the year.

This was supposed to be the loan move to reinvigorate one of England’s best young forwards, at a club well-versed in doing exactly that.

Nwaneri became the fifth Englishman aged 21 or under to sign for Dortmund in the past decade, following in the footsteps of Jadon Sancho, Jude and Jobe Bellingham, and Jamie Gittens. The stars seemed aligned for Nwaneri to shine.

But the opposite has happened. Having impressed and forced a Hoffenheim own goal off the bench on his Dortmund debut, Nwaneri started the team’s next four Bundesliga matches, but was hooked off around the hour mark in each one. The teenager has not made a starting XI since a goalless draw with Union Berlin on October 17.

It is understood Arsenal – who host Dortmund in the Champions League tonight – are closely monitoring the situation around Nwaneri’s lack of minutes, and there is a January recall clause in his contract. The clause was initially inserted as insurance in case an attacking injury crisis arose at Arsenal. Nwaneri's lack of minutes wasn't expected.

Ethan Nwaneri is on loan at Borussia Dortmund from Arsenal but has struggled for minutes – he last started a match on October 17

The 19-year-old is one of the most talented youngsters to emerge from Arsenal's prolific Hale End academy, but his career is in danger of stalling on loan in Germany

So why isn’t his move at Dortmund, a club that made their name by developing young players, working out?

Well, Nwaneri's short career so far has been a complicated one, featuring enormous highs and challenging hurdles. To understand his trajectory, you have to look back at his time at Hale End.

Having risen through the academy rapidly upon joining aged eight, Nwaneri burst onto the first-team scene in September 2022 against Brentford, becoming the youngest player to appear in the Premier League, aged 15 years and 181 days.

Mikel Arteta still values the player but hinted on Monday that he needs to produce more than just ‘moments’.

‘You can have patches, but to find that consistency and to play a big amount of minutes and have a huge impact in big football clubs like Arsenal or Dortmund, it's extremely difficult,’ he said.

‘That's the reality. You can just shine in moments, but moments are not enough. Now you need to show the consistency. Ethan has the capacity and the mentality to do that, and it takes some time.’

There's a feeling at Arsenal that Nwaneri has time on his side and shouldn’t be written off. He signed a five-year deal in August 2025 after all, with a plan to fully integrate the attacker into the first-team squad. His brother Emerson, 16, is thriving with the Under 18s.

However, if Nwaneri were to be sold in future, he would, as an academy graduate, generate pure profit on Arsenal's accounts.

‘His time at Borussia has been a disappointment so far because he was brought in to help immediately after Giannis Konstantelias tore his ACL,’ says Sebastian Wessling, who has covered Dortmund for 15 years at the Funke Media Group.

‘They tried to bring Nwaneri in, the summer before. So having tracked and spoken to him previously, they thought he would be ideal for short-term help. But he really hasn’t been that, it’s not worked out well so far.

‘He’s found it difficult to contribute with goals, assists, or just generally in Dortmund’s offensive game.

‘What the coach is looking for is a player to make a lot of runs in behind. Whereas Nwaneri looks to drop deep and have time on the ball, which the manager, Niko Kovac, isn’t looking for.’

'He lacks confidence and I think that shows in his play,' says Dortmund expert Sebastian Wessling of Nwaneri

There is still a serious player in Nwaneri, as seen in his two assists for England Under 21s in their 3-2 victory over France last week

Nwaneri's lack of confidence and progress feel striking. This summer, he joined England's pre-World Cup training camp in Florida, and was an unused substitute in the warm-up match against New Zealand. Nwaneri was alongside Bournemouth's Alex Scott, Fulham's Josh King and Liverpool's Rio Ngumoha – both Scott and Ngumoha have since made their senior England debuts, while King made Thomas Tuchel's squad this month. All three are flourishing as Nwaneri struggles to even feature.

To make matters worse for him, back at Arsenal 16-year-old Max Dowman is competing for a place in the starting XI. Nwaneri may have bundles of talent, but he is yet to fully kick on.

Wessling adds: ‘He lacks confidence and I think that shows in his play. Niko wants him to be brave on the pitch, but he plays it very safe.

‘When he did feature, he often played short passes and didn’t advance Dortmund’s play. He’s not a total disappointment, but he hasn’t really contributed.’

There is still a serious player in Nwaneri, as seen in his two assists for England Under 21s in their 3-2 victory over France last week. He is eligible to feature at the Emirates tonight, and will be desperate to show Arsenal what they are missing.

In any case, his next two months at Dortmund will reveal plenty about his future. It’s now about consistency – more than mere ‘moments’.

#1568. Feyenoord vs. Ajax - prediction, team news, lineups

By Seye Omidiora | 27 Nov 2026 20:14, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 20:18

Ajax travel to Feyenoord's De Kuip on Sunday looking to heap further misery on the out-of-form Rotterdam giants in this season's first De Klassieker.

Having previously led the Eredivisie table, Giovanni van Bronckhorst's men have suffered a dramatic decline in form and face the prospect of falling six points behind second-placed De Joden after this weekend's matchweek 14 encounter.

Van Bronckhorst was not in charge of Feyenoord last season, but the returning title-winning manager may fear a repeat of the Stadium Club's collapse given their recent results.

The Rotterdam giants are winless in seven matches across all competitions, including four in the Eredivisie, following a nine-match unbeaten league start that featured seven victories.

De Stadionclub topped the Eredivisie standings after matchweek nine's thrilling 4-3 victory over Telstar, with AZ Alkmaar three points behind and PSV Eindhoven and Ajax trailing by four and five respectively.

Their decline in performances and results is reflected in a four-match winless league run, including defeats in the last two, that has left them fifth, four points behind PSV and three adrift of this weekend's visitors.

With a defence that has failed to keep a clean sheet in five consecutive matches after conceding just once across their previous four top-flight fixtures, Van Bronckhorst's men risk falling further behind if this weekend's results go against them.

De Stadionclub's predicament bears similarities to last season's collapse, when Robin van Persie's side started impressively before fading ahead of Christmas, ultimately costing the former striker his job despite a second-placed finish.

That Feyenoord team ended the campaign 19 points behind PSV after holding a three-point advantage over Peter Bosz's men following the ninth round.

Whether those parallels are being discussed in Rotterdam is anyone's guess, but Ajax will back themselves to increase the pressure on their hosts when they visit De Kuip on Sunday afternoon.

Michel's men remain unbeaten against every Eredivisie opponent except PSV, with the Amsterdam giants collecting 28 points from an available 36 when their defeat to the four-peat-chasing Eindhoven outfit is excluded.

Since losing to Bosz's side in gameweek four, Ajax have dropped points in only three of their subsequent nine matches, claiming maximum points in the other six.

De Joden have notably been almost flawless away from home, remaining unbeaten in six matches and winning five, in contrast to their record at the Johan Cruyff Arena, where they have won only three of seven.

That stark disparity between home and away results may be far from ideal for sustaining a title challenge, but it should give the travelling supporters considerable encouragement ahead of Sunday's trip to Rotterdam.

With Ajax able to finish the weekend top of the standings, trailing PSV by just one point after 13 rounds, the league's strongest away side could be forgiven for targeting a sixth victory on their travels in this season's first De Klassieker.

Feyenoord will assess Jakub Moder (knee) before Sunday's showdown, but Bart Nieuwkoop (knee), Jeremiah St. Juste (leg), Thomas Beelen (broken leg), Tijme Wessels (knee) and Jordan Bos (knee) are sidelined.

After missing last weekend's 3-2 Rotterdam derby defeat to SBV Excelsior through injury, Anis Hadj Moussa returned to the starting XI for the Stadium Club's midweek Champions League loss to Porto and should retain his place.

The Algerian remains a joint-leading scorer for the hosts, who can also call upon summer signing Nacho Ferri (seven goals, three assists), Gjivai Zechiel (five goals, four assists) and Luciano Valente (five goals, two assists).

Tolu Arokodare and Julian Brandt lead Ajax's scoring charts with a combined 13 goals, while Davy Klaassen has contributed a respectable five Eredivisie strikes.

Oscar Gloukh has been a creative force, registering a league-high seven assists in 13 appearances and creating more clear-cut chances (12) than any other player in the division.

Four-goal midfielder Jorthy Mokio suffered a broken leg during the 3-0 victory over ADO Den Haag, ruling him out for around four months.

Kasper Dolberg (ACL) is also a long-term absentee and is expected to miss the remainder of the season, while Viktor Tsygankov, Caio Henrique and Simon Adingra remain sidelined.

Ernst; Read, Kraaijeveld, Marmol, Lopez; Zechiel, Vanhoutte, Targhalline; Hadj Moussa, Ferri, Valente

Ter Stegen; Rosa, Bouman, Baas, Wijndal; Bissouma, Amrabat, Brandt; Bounida, Arokodare, Gloukh

Feyenoord's failure to keep a clean sheet in five consecutive matches is particularly concerning before facing an Ajax attack boasting Arokodare, Brandt and the division's leading assist provider.

The hosts should create opportunities through their own productive forwards, but the visitors' five wins from six away league games suggest that Michel's men can prevail in an open De Klassieker.

#1567. Meet the world's most famous pub team: How a Sex Pistol, Superman and Vinnie Jones took Hollywood United  beyond Sunset Boulevard via private jet - and even rubbed shoulders with David Beckham's LA Galaxy

Published: 09:00 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 12:29 EST, 24 November 2026

They had a World Cup winner in defence, Superman in their squad and a Sex Pistol in charge of recruitment.

There's a clue in the name, but Hollywood United must have been the wildest, most star-studded pub football team of all time.

Ray Winstone, Jason Statham, Mike Myers and Vinnie Jones all turned out for a team that grew out of a gathering of British expats at the Cat & Fiddle pub in the late Eighties.

It being Hollywood, they travelled to matches by private jet and they even took on David Beckham in a charity match.

Now, as the Sex Pistols prepare to embark on a tour marking the 50th anniversary of their debut single, guitarist Steve Jones has revealed how he assembled the extraordinary side on Hollywood's Sunset Boulevard.

Among those who pulled on the shirt were France's World Cup-winning defender Frank Leboeuf, former Scotland captain Richard Gough and Brandon Routh, the American actor who played the superhero in the 2006 film Superman Returns.

Routh was given no special treatment by his team-mates, who would mockingly shout ‘Superman!’ whenever he made a mistake.

Hollywood United is the world's most famous pub team - featuring a littany of high-profile stars

Created by British expat and Sex Pistols star Steve Jones (right), United have rubbed shoulders with the likes of David Beckham

Vinnie Jones, meanwhile, had apparently lost none of the competitive instincts that characterised his career in English football.

In 2002, it was reported that he had been sent off just 15 seconds after coming on as a substitute in a Hollywood United friendly.

Anthony LaPaglia, the Australian actor who starred in the hit television series Without a Trace, was their goalkeeper.

There were members of the Sex Pistols, The Cult and Def Leppard, as well as actors such as Ralf Little.

But there were also rather less celebrated footballers.

‘The start of it was with me and Anthony LaPaglia; he was a goalie, and from there it turned into Hollywood United,’ Jones told the Telegraph.

‘We always used to play in a league with a bunch of regular blokes, carpenters and so on, then we got a few more faces who wanted to start kicking about with us like Vinnie Jones.’

The two Joneses met in a video shop in Los Angeles and the former Wimbledon hardman, who had embarked on a film career with Lock, Stock and Two Smoking Barrels, needed little persuasion to join.

‘He was up for a laugh, and he knows where to put a ball. Most of the team were amateurs, but we were decent and reached a certain level.’

In November 2007, Hollywood United took on Beckham's LA Galaxy in a charity match.

England manager Steve McClaren had flown to California to assess Beckham's fitness ahead of a European Championship qualifier against Croatia. It's not clear whether he attended the match, which Hollywood United lost 12-4. Beckham scored twice, as did Leboeuf and over 5,000 spectators raised more than $100,000 for victims of the California wildfires.

Steve Jones, now 71, had himself broken one of football's golden rules by changing his allegiance.

Vinnie Jones (left) and Ray Winstone (right) have turned out for the amateur football team

Actor Anthony LaPaglia lets the team travel on his private jet to matches across America

Having followed QPR as a schoolboy in west London and also been associated with Fulham, he became a Chelsea supporter after moving to California and getting sober.

Chelsea's games were available on American television and his lifelong friend and fellow Sex Pistol Paul Cook was already a diehard Blues fan.

Hollywood United played at Griffith Park, beneath the famous Hollywood sign, but their adventures would take them considerably further afield.

LaPaglia would arrange private jets to transport the players to matches.

Gough recalls one trip when the team flew to Vancouver for a charity match before heading straight to the Mexican resort of Puerto Vallarta to play a side of former Mexico internationals.

Vinnie Jones also told the Guardian in 2007 that Hollywood United had fielded nine former international footballers in a single match.

The club's ranks included former Liverpool and Newcastle defender Barry Venison and United States internationals Alexi Lalas and Eric Wynalda.

Winstone, a lifelong West Ham fan, found playing in the Californian heat rather more demanding than he had anticipated.

He later recalled being so exhausted by the time the ball reached him that he was barely able to kick it. And he wasn't particularly impressed by the willingness of former Chelsea defender Leboeuf to pass the ball, describing the Frenchman as a greedy player.

Among those watching from the touchline was the actor John Hurt, who was in town filming Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull with Winstone.

Some of the rock stars had impressive footballing pedigrees.

Ian Astbury, the lead singer of The Cult, had played boys' club football in Glasgow alongside future Everton and Scotland striker Graeme Sharp.

Gough, meanwhile, struck up a conversation with a team-mate from Northern Ireland without having the slightest idea he was Vivian Campbell, the guitarist of Def Leppard.

Sex Pistol Jones, who has lived in Los Angeles for more than 40 years, is returning to Britain next month for a tour marking the 50th anniversary of the release of Anarchy in the UK.

He still regularly attends football matches whenever he is back in England, although he has little time for the corporate hospitality enjoyed by many of his celebrity contemporaries.

‘I don't care where I sit, but I'm not interested in sitting in some box with a bunch of t***ers.’

#1566. Opinion - They'll regret this: Chelsea give green light for Liverpool for signing

Chelsea have given Liverpool the green light to go and complete a signing. The Blues will regret this.

Liverpool do desperately need to sign someone in midfield. Or at least, it felt that way not very long ago but Trey Nyoni’s form in the middle has been fantastic.

Which again brings about the question of potentially doing business in January. And there’s been a development there.

Chelsea leave the door wide openLiverpool's big problem with signing a midfielder has been Chelsea. Liverpool's big problem with signing a midfielder has been Chelsea. The Blues also need a high-profile midfielder, having sold Enzo Fernandez at the transfer deadline without a replacement.

They did try to sign one, of course. Lamine Camara was a serious option and they did bid. AS Monaco ended the deal right at the death, however, as they felt a bigger one could be had in 2027 - Liverpool were supposedly the reason why, essentially.

Alex Scott is another heavily linked with Liverpool, especially as his former coach, Iraola, is in charge at Anfield. But Chelsea were supposed to be ahead in that race, going all-out for the Bournemouth star.

But David Ornstein reports that Chelsea aren't actually going for a midfielder right now, in what's a massive surprise to everyone. He told USA Sports that he's not aware of any January ideas from the club. Instead, it appears they're going to wait for the summer.

That leaves the door wide open for Liverpool, who could conceivably make a move for an elite midfielder before Chelsea even get to the table. Their biggest rival for competition isn't putting up a fight - and that's a huge advantage in any talks.

It stops the price rising too high, it stops players' heads getting turned, and it also takes away an immediate time pressure to strike a deal. Though, there is still the time pressure of getting it done in January.

But there's no question about it: Chelsea's stance is an advantage for Liverpool if the Reds are still happy to sign a midfield player.

#1564. Amorim analyses Olympiacos comeback, Hutchinson’s potential and need to cut out mistakes

AC Milan head coach Ruben Amorim believes that the comeback win over Olympiacos is something that could ‘change the future’.

After 50 minutes of the game on the outskirts of Athens, it looked like Milan were heading for a fourth defeat in five Europa League games. Lorenzo Pirola crashed a header in off the bar via Mike Maignan, then Jota Silva scored a second early in the second half.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Then, out of almost nowhere, Omari Hutchinson inspired a run of three goals in 15 minutes. Firstly he scored a goal of his own with a brilliant solo run, then he set up Alphadjo Cisse for his 10th goal of the season, then he crossed for a Christian Pulisic volley to make it 3-2.

Diego Moreira added a fourth late on to make sure of the points. Amorim spoke to Sky after the final whistle to give his thoughts on what was a rollercoaster night, but one that thankfully ended well. His words are via MilanNews.

Will this second half change the Europa League season?

“I think this is the biggest problem: focusing on the small details like set pieces, goalkeeping, and the plays we need to make. It comes with time and experience.

“The technical aspect is fine, but concentration is the most important thing. It’s tough to play physically every three days, but it’s even tougher to constantly have this pressure of having to win.”

“I always expect this. He has the potential to do much more. He’s talented, like other players on the team. It’s no surprise, he’s very talented. It’s the mentality that counts.”

“We lost the ball without being pressured, trying to play the ball. We left Jashari alone to set up a team with four of our players behind their midfielders. When we had the ball, we gave it away without pressure.

“Koni sometimes put the ball in areas where there was pressure, but instead he was supposed to carry the ball. He’s responsible for pushing the team forward and guiding us forward. We went to get into their pressing zones.”

It’s your first comeback win of the season…

“I think it’s a great feeling. If you look at the Benfica match, we had several opportunities. We created more than today. You have to see it to believe it, and today we saw that we came from two goals behind and won 4-2. Our confidence will grow.”

#1563. Spitting row mars feisty Millwall-West Ham clash

A spitting row marred the 100th Millwall-West Ham United derby and first for 14 years.

Taty Castellanos was facing trial by video after being accused of spitting on Filip Marschall during Saturday’s febrile 2-2 draw at the Den.

Millwall goalkeeper Marschall made the allegation to referee Paul Tierney, who was expected to include it in an official report that would then be assessed by the Football Association.

Spitting on an opponent is punishable with a six-match ban.

Telegraph Sport has been told West Ham striker Castellanos denies he spat on Marschall and believes he will be vindicated by video footage of the incident.

Lying little prick. Taty didn't spit ❌ pic.twitter.com/5vYxOtKqof

Millwall manager Alex Neil said after the game that fourth official Lewis Smith had confirmed a spitting accusation had been made.

Asked if he had spoken to Marschall about the claim, Neil replied: “I haven’t asked him about it. But it’s like anything else; I’m sure there’ll be footage of it, or not of it, if it didn’t happen.

“I’d be extremely surprised if Fil’s made an accusation and nothing’s happened. But that’s not really for me to deal with; I’m sure the authorities will deal with that.”

West Ham manager Nuno Espírito Santo said: “I’m aware of the allegation. I didn’t see the image; I didn’t speak with Taty. I cannot go much further on that.”

He added: “I’m going to try to look at the images.”

There were also ugly scenes at full time when players had to be separated at the end of a derby that had been at the centre of an unprecedented police operation.

There were six arrests as of 4pm on Saturday for offences including tailgating, assault on a police officer and entering or attempting to enter a stadium while intoxicated.

Eleven men were also arrested at around 7.15pm on Friday on suspicion of conspiracy to commit criminal damage.

The group, believed to be Millwall fans, were detained in the vicinity of a known West Ham supporters’ pub in Stratford.

Saturday’s fixture was subject to a five-mile dispersal zone, the largest ever for a football match in London, with officers granted special powers to stop and search people and vehicles without reasonable suspicion and to remove anyone causing disorder.

Riot police were out in force outside the ground, with dog units and mounted officers among 400 personnel deployed – roughly quadruple the usual number for a game there.

Those and other measures – including the use of live facial recognition, a strict segregation policy and a 12.30pm kick-off to minimise supporters’ pre-match drinking time – prevented a repeat of the kind of violence which has marred this fixture down the years.

West Ham fans also received a police escort to a game that saw both sets of supporters hurl foul-mouthed insults at each other throughout.

Plans to keep rival spectators apart after the match were reportedly tested by scuffles that broke out as people left the ground.

If the police were ready for a fight before the game, West Ham’s players were not as Millwall tore into them from the first whistle and dominated a first half in which they scored twice through Caleb Taylor and Camiel Neghli and hit the crossbar through a stunning 35-yard strike by Mark Sykes.

That was only after Marschall gestured that he had been spat at by Castellanos following a melee in the penalty area.

The foul denied Lisbie the chance to hand Millwall their first win over their bitter rivals for 22 years, much to the frustration of fans who had roared them on from first whistle to last.

Lisbie darts to the by-line but his cutback does not make it through the thicket of limbs and West Ham clear their lines.

Millwall earn a free-kick to the left of the box as Mavropanos climbs all over Dykes. Servais picks out Baggott at the far post and his knock-down lands to Dykes who, will spinning, strikes the ball over the bar.

There will be five minutes of time added on...

RED CARD 🟥West Ham are down to ten men, after Kante was sent off for denial of a goalscoring opportunity. pic.twitter.com/jRlVwLNiOs

Millwall have put so much into this and it’s starting to tell. Their players look leggy and aren’t able to track Kante’s run into the channel though Cooper is just about able to clear his lines. Bowen’s corner comes to nothing.

Pablo’s at it again, steaming his way into the left half-space, but Mazou-Sacko does well to track back and block the Brazilian’s effort. The resulting corner is gathered by Marschall who attempts to send Servais away but Kilman is wise to it and takes a booking for a professional foul.

Mazou-Sacko has his hands all over Pablo’s back and while the Brazilian is awarded a free-kick he slams the ball to the ground feeling he had broken free. He earns a booking for his troubles and the resulting free-kick comes to nothing.

Bowen earns his side a corner and his delivery comes out to Solomon on the edge of the box, and while Cooper is able to partially clear, Austbo stings the gloves of Marschall from distance to win another corner.

Millwall 2 West Ham 1 (Kante) The substitute strokes a right-footed effort into the bottom corner from outside the box. A great finish.

Arconte chases down a lost cause and telescopes a leg through Taylor to earn a corner. He spins around to the home supporters and windmills his arms in their direction as the volume increases. Metcalfe’s cross is well overhit, though, and sails out for a goal-kick.

Kante’s runs in behind are threatening to disrupt Millwall’s backline shape, but Neil’s midfield sentries Mazou-Sacko and Metcalfe are doing such a great job to cover the gaps that the hosts still look like they have things under control.

Penalty shout! Metcalfe drives forward into the right of the box and Kante, who is hot pursuit, pushes the midfielder to the ground. Tierney immediately waves away the appeals and replays concur that the contact is probably not strong enough to warrant a penalty.

Bowen is presented with some grass to run into but his cross is well cleared.
