#1548. Please, Oliver, can we have some more? Celtic boss Martin O'Neill tells Danish midfielder Sorensen it's time to up his game

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 13:00 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 13:13 EST, 24 November 2026

Martin O’Neill has told Oliver Sorensen that it’s now time for him to deliver in a Celtic jersey.

The Danish midfielder arrived in Glasgow with a big reputation after coming in on a one-year loan from Parma. But in his seven appearances to date, the 24-year-old has failed to show why the Italian club paid Midtjylland £8.4million for his services a year ago.

With Mika Baur sidelined for up to ten weeks with an ankle injury, Sorensen is likely to be afforded further opportunities to show his worth. But with Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain, Luke McCowan and Joel van den Berg all showing up well in the weekend win over St Mirren, O’Neill has warned that Sorensen needs to do more if he’s to force his way into his side.

‘He has, by his own admission, found it difficult,’ said the Celtic manager.

‘I think that he also arrived late as well, trying to get to know people, trying to get his position, trying to get up to speed with what we do. And whatever we do, I bet you it’ll be something really different to what he was doing at Parma.

‘But now it would be up to him. And, certainly, it will be up to him to try and do something as quickly as possible, whether it’s in the next couple of weeks.

Danish midfielder Oliver Sorensen has been lesser spotted at Celtic this season

‘His strength is picking the ball up deep and running and going with it. I think that Van den Berg can do that as well. But that was the idea with losing (Arne) Engels, we were trying to get a like-for-like replacement.

‘At this minute, he has found it difficult. But he’s willing and he wants to learn.’

Celtic face Torreense on Thursday with the game being played in Leiria as the host club’s normal ground doesn’t meet UEFA stadium requirements.

After losing their first three Europa League games to Ferencvaros, Benfica and Celta Vigo, O’Neill’s men earned a lifeline in the competition when they defeated Besiktas last time out.

With ten points likely to be needed to secure progression to the play-off round, the Celtic manager feels it’s imperative that his side are on the seven-point mark after they take on Omonia on matchday six on December 10.

‘We just want to try and do well,’ he stressed. ‘I said after the Besiktas game that it gives you a chance.

Sorensen struggled along with the rest of his team-mates in a Europa League defeat at Benfica

‘Because nobody’s made it after having lost the first three games. So, the next two matches are vital for us.

‘You’d have to think that we’d need to get four points in the two games to give ourselves a chance.

‘After that you’ve got two left over, a home game (Marseille), which will not be easy. And then the away match (Union Saint-Gilloise).

‘It would be nice to carry it into January and still have a chance.

‘We’ve taken enough criticism for not doing well enough in Europe and rightly so. It’s the aim of the football club, it’s what we’ve always said, and that’s been really disappointing.’

Meanwhile, O’Neill believes Kieran Tierney is rediscovering the form which earned him a £25million move to Arsenal in 2019.

The full-back played the entirety of Scotland’s double-header with North Macedonia and Switzerland and lasted 71 minutes of the win over St Mirren – a game in which he claimed two assists.

O'Neill believes Kieran Tierney is close to the form that earned him a £25m move to Arsenal

Delighted that the player appeared to be putting fitness concerns behind him, O’Neill said: ‘Kieran has done great for me. He’s been brilliant, he really has, and he’s getting fitter too.

‘He will be big for us in Europe again. You look at the Besiktas game. Our winning goal late on came from his shot when he was still getting high up the pitch.

‘Kieran has done so well for us and there are signs that he’s back to the Kieran Tierney who got a move to Arsenal.

‘He defends well, he creates goals and he comes up with some too. I genuinely couldn’t speak highly enough about him. He’s a great lad too, very popular in the dressing room.

‘Kieran can play as a centre-half, there’s no doubt about it. He competes better in the air than I ever thought he could. It was only when I came back to Celtic that I realised that.

‘He will battle in the air and he’s a reliable defender. If we are ever dropping into a back three, then it wouldn’t be a problem for him.’

#1546. GdS: Milan ‘conquer Athens’ – how Hutchinson and Amorim’s changes inspired a comeback

When it looked like they had been knocked to the floor for good in the Europa League, AC Milan got up and produced a stunning response in Greece.

La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) begin their analysis this morning by writing that Milan showed their ‘true Italian colours in Europe at last’ in a ‘magnificent, incredible performance’. It took a while to get going, with two goals from the home side needed as a wake-up call, but it worked.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Ruben Amorim reshaped his side and they produced epic comeback, turning a 0–2 deficit into a 4–2 victory, with the Rossoneri suddenly appearing courageous, aggressive, and dominant. For one night, Omari Hutchinson was the god of Athens, with his Messi-like goal and two assists.

In stoppage time, the tireless Diego Moreira also got on the scoresheet. It’s a massive boost to both energy and morale, putting the team back into the play-off places. There is more work to be done, but it feels like a start.

Also worth examining is the Milan side seen in the first half and the beginning of the second, a period when Joao Silva’s quick goal to make it 2-0 threatened to turn into yet another cursed night.

The Rossoneri were off the pace again, completely at the mercy of Olympiacos’s frenetic pace and 4-2-3-1 formation, which hemmed them into the final thirty metres and stifled any chance of a counter-attack.

It was a case of no Luke Modric, no party. In truth, one counter did materialise, coming down the left flank. Despite being off-balance, the ever-present Cissé managed to get a shot on target from the ground, only for Pirola – an Italian playing in Greece – to clear it off the line.

Milan need to be built around Cissé, but in the first half it was Goncalo Ramos who occupied the centre of the 3-4-2-1, functioning less as a ‘false nine’ and more as a centre-forward who simply wasn’t there, much like the team-mates who should have been supporting him.

Milan got off to a poor start. Entrusting the protection of the midfield to the Jashari-Rabiot duo – neither of whom are a true defensive specialist – proved to be a questionable strategy against Freuler and Gustavo Sà.

In truth, the whole side struggled. Hutchinson was ineffective as a right-sided attacking midfielder; Cissé was never brought into play on the opposite flank; and Estupiñán – tasked with a hybrid role as both full-back and wing-back – looked completely flat on the left.

Amorim’s tactical experiments backfired, not least because De Winter was far from flawless at the back, while Diawara appeared somewhat naive. At the other end, Pirola looked every bit the Achilles among the Greeks.

He scored the opening goal with a header (officially recorded by UEFA as an own goal, as the ball ricocheted off the crossbar and then Maignan), and later made a crucial intervention to deny Cissé.

One could have held endless debates over why Milan wins five out of six matches in Italy, yet was on the verge of a fourth defeat in Europe. Arguments about the ‘pace of European competition’ feel a bit reductive: fair enough regarding Benfica, but we are talking about Ferencváros and Olympiacos.

Milan simply needed to restore their balance. Amorim took drastic measures: he brought on Yunus Musah to bolster the midfield and Pulisic to inject energy into the attack, while taking off Estupiñán and Ramos (the latter due to a knock), effectively reshaping the entire side.

In defence, Mario Gila and Koni De Winter remained (though Fikayo Tomori, who soon replaced the latter, performed much better), joined by Sankhoun Diawara. In the middle, Hutchinson and Moreira took the flanks, while the well-balanced duo of Jashari and Musah took control of the centre.

Up front, Rabiot and Pulisic flanked Cissé. When Jota Silva made it 2–0 just four minutes in, it seemed as though there was no effective remedy, but it was merely a matter of regrouping.

Moving away from his hybrid role as an attacking midfielder/central midfielder, Hutchinson transformed into a devastating wide player. In the 11th minute of the second half he won the ball in midfield, embarks on a brilliant slalom run and found the bottom corner.

From that moment on, the Greek side effectively disappeared from the match. They ran around aimlessly, lacking any tactical cohesion or ideas, while their manager Alguacil faltered with his substitutions.

The equaliser came from Cissé, who headed home a pinpoint assist from Hutchinson after more good work on the right. It was his tenth goal of the season (four in the Europa League, six in Serie A): when Cissé plays he scores, simple as that.

The 3-2 goal arrived courtesy of Pulisic, who executed a stunning mid-air half-volley, once again set up by the Englishman. Pulisic himself squanders a chance to make it 4-2 on the counter-attack, but Moreira eventually sealed the deal in the closing seconds.

It can’t be said that ‘we’ve found the real Milan’ even after the comeback, not with a Milan that possesses so many different identities. It’s clear that Ramos needs to reflect, but the urgent need for points suggests it’s time for Cissé and Pulisic.

A defensive-minded player is a must in a two-man midfield. If Hutchison is such a dynamo on the right, then Moreira could perhaps be ‘sacrificed’ on the left. And at the back, maybe Tomori was cast aside a bit too soon.

Half the squad is sidelined with injuries, yet there are more resources available than one might imagine. Six points is not enough: the team need another six from their last three games to make the knockouts. The night in Piraeus, however, is a start.

An exciting left-back has been promoted to Liverpool's first-team.

Milos Kerkez is getting back to his best. With his former manager Andoni Iraola's guidance the young Hungarian, yes it's easy to forget, he is still young, is playing like the version that we all fell in love with at Bournemouth.

Over the last year, Liverpool's players have faced a lot of criticism. Some of it, probably rightly. But others have been over the top, such is the nature of social media these days.

Well Neco Williams could be an easy solution but the costs might be significant. Liverpool also have the likes of Lewis Hall on their radar, and other players like Mahamadou Nagida will be well-liked by the club as well. But there is also an internal solution.

That is not to say because Kerkez is producing that the need for a new left-back to come in isn't there. Kostas Tsimikas cannot be relied on as a deputy.

Liverpool need to recruit someone else to provide competition and adept cover for Kerkez.

It's imperative that is resolved in the coming windows and will be one of the main objectives for Julian Ward as he takes control of the sporting director position.

Well Neco Williams could be an easy solution but the costs might be significant. Liverpool also have the likes of Lewis Hall on their radar, and other players like Mahamadou Nagida will be well-liked by the club as well.

That solution is Scottish youth international Cameron Williams, who has been catching the eye in the academy recently.

Williams trained with Scotland's senior national team when he was just 16-years-old. He is a highly talented left-back, with excellent qualities going forward, who many regard as the new Andy Robertson.

The youngster has struggled with a few injuries here and there. However, he is now back playing regularly for the club's U18 side and has subsequently earned himself an official promotion.

Looking at Liverpool's squad on the UEFA website, Williams has been added to the team through the B-list, as highlighted by Lewis Bower as well.

It means Williams is now officially a member of the first-team squad and could even feature in the Champions League. A player to keep a close eye on!

#1540. Freddie Potts on the pain of leaving West Ham, why he had to move on this summer, upsetting the odds in the Champions League with Club Brugge - and why they don't fear Liverpool!

Published: 08:00 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 14:15 EST, 24 November 2026

There are few transfers that get West Ham supporters talking quite like the sale of an academy graduate.

Who can forget the uproar after Grady Diangana joined West Brom in 2020, when club captain Mark Noble released a public statement voicing his anger and disappointment at the move.

Noble’s thoughts were echoed by team-mates at the time, while supporters were similarly up in arms at the sale of the winger.

So, when Freddie Potts joined Club Brugge for £10million on the eve of the season to mark the controversial departure of another product of the proclaimed Academy of Football, you can imagine the reaction.

Potts represented more than a graduate. A boyhood West Ham fan whose dad Steve is a club legend and still serves as a first-team coach, he joined the academy aged six. His brother Dan also came through the ranks.

The midfielder had just enjoyed a breakthrough campaign despite West Ham’s relegation, and many felt he was the perfect player to build their Championship promotion push around.

Freddie Potts is shining in Belgium with Club Brugge after joining from West Ham in the summer

Potts joined the Hammers academy aged six and enjoyed a breakthrough year last season

Hammers favourites Kevin Nolan and Tony Cottee weighed in with their disapproval at his sale, while celebrity fan Ray Winstone expressed his shock and anger live on talkSPORT.

‘Of course you see it (the division about the move) on social media,’ Potts tells Daily Mail Sport. ‘Every player does. But even though last season was tough I always felt I had a connection with the West Ham fans.

‘No matter if I played well or bad I always felt I understood what it meant to play for West Ham. It's a great club with great fans and people. In the end, I had to do what was best for me. I wanted to play this season, and I felt like this was the best place to do that.’

Potts, 22 at the time of his exit, admits it was extremely tough and emotional for him and his family to leave a club he had been at for 16 years.

But, during pre-season he became aware he wasn’t likely to play as much as he wanted to under Nuno Espirito Santo.

‘In the end it’s the manager’s decision,’ Potts says. ‘I wasn’t getting the minutes I wanted. The feeling was that I wasn’t guaranteed to be in the plans as much as Club Brugge were promising me, so I thought it was best for me to move.

‘It was very hard. West Ham have been my club my whole life and I have a lot of love for West Ham. But I had to take into account what was best for my career and I’m loving it at Brugge. It’s a really exciting place full of great people and a great manager.’

Potts had multiple options in the summer, including Premier League interest, yet the chance to play in the Champions League and compete for titles with Brugge attracted him.

Their record of developing young players and a talented squad that includes the likes of Carlos Forbs and Nicolo Tresoldi was equally compelling, and the midfielder hasn't looked back.

Potts started Brugge’s first 10 league games, missing their final one before the international break due to suspension. He returned at the weekend as they thrashed Mechelen 5-1. Ivan Leko’s side are one point adrift of Union Saint-Gilloise at the top of the Belgian Pro League, and they have also impressed in the Champions League.

In Europe, Brugge have beaten Inter Milan, PSV and Lens on their way to nine points from 12, only narrowly losing 3-2 to Aston Villa. Potts has started each match, including their memorable 4-3 win against Inter at the San Siro, and they host Liverpool on Wednesday.

‘It's a really good group of lads,’ he says. ‘Everyone speaks English as well which helps me. It's a good team and we're happy playing with each other.’

He is clearly enjoying life and is just the fifth English player in history to play for the club. Potts did take time to settle though, and admits he initially suffered from homesickness.

‘I found it difficult because East London and Essex have been my home for my whole life,’ he says. ‘West Ham was my life. It was tough in terms of moving into a new language and everything but you get used to it and I’m really enjoying it here. It’ll be strange going back home to England.'

Potts has been a regular and has had a key role in Brugge's impressive early exploits in Europe

Brugge have beaten PSV, Lens and Inter Milan, and they take on Liverpool this Wednesday

Potts’ family have popped over to see him and he has enjoyed exploring his new surroundings. He is yet to learn the local language and scolds himself for being lazy for relying on English, although he has picked up little bits of Flemish.

He has immersed himself in the culture too, and reveals he has tried the world-famous Belgian fries and a few local beers, albeit only when he has enough time to recover between games.

Despite his new life in Europe, Potts remains a West Ham fan and tries to watch them on TV every week.

He has been surprised by their struggles on their return to the Championship for the first time in 14 years, with Nuno paying the price by losing his job. Former Hammers midfielder Scott Parker has since taken the reins.

‘I still think they're playing well,’ Potts says. ‘They've got a great team and Scott Parker is a really good manager. You get ups and downs but I still 100 per cent think West Ham will get promoted this year.'

Potts’ stay in the Hammers first team may have been brief, yet there were still plenty of highs, not least a storming performance on his first Premier League start. That came in a win over Newcastle last November in the Hammers’ first home victory of the season. He was also coached by his dad, an experience he jokes had positives and negatives.

He left West Ham after realising he was unlikely to be first choice under Nuno Espirito Santo

Potts is a boyhood West Ham fan and is fully expecting them to get promoted this season

Attention now turns to Brugge’s clash against Liverpool. It promises to be a tricky challenge for Andoni Iraola’s side against a team who are determined to prove themselves on the European stage.

The two teams are level on points in the league phase, and Potts is keen for his side to take another scalp.

‘I don't think there's much difference in the way we've been performing in the Champions League,’ Potts concludes. ‘It'll be difficult for them to come to our place as well.

‘They're a great team, but we're going to approach it like we have with every Champions League game. We've gone away and beaten Milan, we've beaten PSV away. These are top teams.

‘Results like that give you a boost of how far you can go. You don't want to look too far ahead but every game in this competition is a chance to show everyone what you can do.

‘Liverpool will be a tough game but we've proved it against top teams before and we're going in thinking that we can do it again.’

#1539. Opinion: Liverpool's next Trent Alexander-Arnold passes audition, what a player

Liverpool's next Trent Alexander-Arnold may now be known. He's passed his audition in front of Andoni Iraola and co. - now he can be signed.

Liverpool lost Trent Alexander-Arnold to Real Madrid in 2025 and with that, one of their best creative players disappeared. A unique one, too - no one in the history of football has done what Alexander-Arnold can do from right-back.

We don't think that's too controversial. The Scouser's ability to create and progress the ball from a full-back position is unheard of and he was a core reason why Liverpool were such a standout side during his time at the club.

But with Alexander-Arnold's exit, the Reds knew they had to move in a different director. Conor Bradley was chosen to be first-choice, though injuries have essentially ruined that plan. It might get back on track, but it's a waiting game involving a lot of hope.

Jeremie Frimpong is an entirely different full-back to Alexander-Arnold. To the extent that he's arguably not even a full-back but a wing-back. The Dutchman hasn't ever made the role his own, unable to offer solidity while his attacking game feels too limited to be a threat with another wide player on that side.

So how about going back to the Alexander-Arnold way? It's difficult for as we've said, he's essentially unique in football for what he can do. But there is a player who looks like he could replicate it.

Kyriani Sabbe: Maybe Liverpool's answerMake no mistake: Club Brugge are a fantastic side and Liverpool's 3-0 win in Belgium was a brilliant one. They kept a clean sheet against a team that usually dominates, even if they had to ride their luck at times. One notable facet of that match is that Liverpool didn't have the majority of possession against a Belgian side. This Brugge iteration is a brilliant one with some brilliant players. One of those is Kyriani Sabbe, who is doing notable things from right-back. He's someone averaging over 100 touches per 90 minutes - a ridiculous figure for a right-back but he's a player Brugge turn to for progression. It was the same against Liverpool on Wednesday. Sabbe had the fourth-most touches in the match and second-most for Brugge as they won the possession battle.

Make no mistake: Club Brugge are a fantastic side and Liverpool's 3-0 win in Belgium was a brilliant one. They kept a clean sheet against a team that usually dominates, even if they had to ride their luck at times.

One notable facet of that match is that Liverpool didn't have the majority of possession against a Belgian side. This Brugge iteration is a brilliant one with some brilliant players.

One of those is Kyriani Sabbe, who is doing notable things from right-back. He's someone averaging over 100 touches per 90 minutes - a ridiculous figure for a right-back but he's a player Brugge turn to for progression.

It was the same against Liverpool on Wednesday. Sabbe had the fourth-most touches in the match and second-most for Brugge as they won the possession battle.

Notably, Sabbe used these touches to move his side forward. His 12 line-breaking passes were five more than any of the four players with more touches than him, and only Jeremy Jacquet managed more in the match (13).

And that number is fewer than Sabbe usually manages. He's averaging an absolutely ridiculous 17 per 90 minutes in Belgium this season, to go along with a long-ball success rate of 56 per cent.

So here's a 21-year-old with the kind of passing numbers you'd only really see from Alexander-Arnold. And he's doing it in the UEFA Champions League and in a successful side that's used to lots of possession.

It makes Sabbe an incredibly interesting prospect and one that Liverpool simply must look at as they look to solve their right-back problem. Wednesday felt like an audition of sorts and one that the player certainly passed.

#1537. Fortuna Sittard vs Heerenveen - prediction, team news, lineups

By Nsidibe Akpan | 27 Nov 2026 23:58, Last updated: 28 Nov 2026 11:23

Fortuna Sittard play host to SC Heerenveen in the 2026-27 Eredivisie at the Fortuna Sittard Stadion in Sittard on Sunday.

Heerenveen are sixth in the Eredivisie table on 24 points and Fortuna seventh on 23, with leaders PSV Eindhoven on 29, so Sunday's winner will leave a direct rival for one of the European playoff places trailing in December.

Danny Buijs's side have lost only twice in 13 league games and are unbeaten in seven since a 5-1 home defeat by Ajax on September 12, leaving the Fortunezen seventh on 23 points from six wins, five draws and two defeats.

Both of those defeats, the other being 2-0 against AZ on August 22 with Ole Romeny sent off early, came at the Fortuna Sittard Stadion, whereas Fortuna are unbeaten away from home, with a 1-1 draw at Feyenoord on October 31 featuring an equaliser from Feyenoord loanee Shiloh 't Zand.

Home draws have been the problem, as Fortuna led Twente 1-0 on October 10 through an Anthony Descotte header from a Mohamed Ihattaren cross before drawing 1-1, and led Telstar 2-0 on November 7 through an Ihattaren penalty and a Sem Valk own goal before conceding twice before half time in a 2-2 draw.

Their latest home win was a 1-0 victory over Excelsior on October 25, decided by a Rodrigo Guth header from an Ihattaren corner in stoppage time, when Descotte and Lequincio Zeefuik were unavailable and Ihattaren started on the bench.

The most recent result was a 1-0 win at Go Ahead Eagles on November 22, when Descotte scored his sixth goal of the season in the 50th minute after Ihattaren sent substitute Kristoffer Peterson clear, ending the hosts' unbeaten home record.

Off the pitch, Buijs announced on Wednesday, November 18 that he will not extend a contract expiring in 2027 and will leave after four seasons, which leaves Fortuna a little over six months to appoint a successor.

Robin Veldman's De Superfriezen have won their last six matches in all competitions, including five straight in the league against Excelsior (4-0), ADO Den Haag (3-2), NEC Nijmegen (1-0), Feyenoord (5-3) and Groningen (3-1), scoring 16 goals and conceding six.

The 5-3 win over Feyenoord on November 8 ended the leaders' unbeaten league record, with Heerenveen recovering from 2-0 down after 31 minutes through Maas Willemsen, Levi Smans and a hat-trick from half-time substitute Ringo Meerveld in the 61st, 84th and 93rd minutes.

At Groningen on November 21, Dylan Vente scored in the 41st minute after a blunder by goalkeeper Lovro Stubljar and again in the 73rd, with substitute Dirk Proper adding a third in the 80th to secure a first win at the Euroborg since March 19, 2023.

Heerenveen's 27 goals scored and 17 conceded give them a goal difference of +10, nine better than Fortuna's +1 from 21 scored and 20 conceded.

The run followed a September wobble that ended with a 4-0 win at Sparta Rotterdam on September 19 after a five-game winless spell, and the only league defeat since was 2-0 at PSV Eindhoven on October 9.

Heerenveen have also won their last two league games on the road, 3-2 at ADO Den Haag on October 24, when Jacob Trenskow scored twice, and 3-1 at Groningen.

Fortuna have a goalkeeping problem, as first-choice Mattijs Branderhorst sprained an ankle in training before the Go Ahead game and Luuk Koopmans, who made several saves in that 1-0 win, is expected to deputise again.

Buijs is also without attackers Zeefuik and Romeny, who are both expected back around January 8, plus midfielder Edouard Michut, who is due back around December 5, and defender Daley Sinkgraven.

The losses matter because Descotte, Zeefuik and Ihattaren had scored 11 of Fortuna's first 16 league goals before the Excelsior game, which leaves Descotte, Sven Simons and Peterson to carry the attack.

Yassin Oukili is a doubt after a spell out, and Buijs is expected to keep the back-five shape used at Deventer.

Heerenveen have one doubt in defender Hristiyan Petrov, who returned from Bulgaria duty injured, missed the Groningen derby and was still not fully fit on Friday, when Veldman said the club would decide whether he travels.

The rest of the squad trained on Friday morning without problems, no suspensions have been reported, and Veldman is likely to keep the side that won at Groningen, with Mees Hilgers covering at centre-back if Petrov is not risked.

Fortuna Sittard possible starting lineup:

Koopmans; Van Ottele, Guth, Hubner, Pinto, Dahlhaus; Ihattaren, Brittijn, 't Zand; Simons, Descotte

Klaverboer; Braude, Kersten, Willemsen, Zagaritis; Linday, Courtens; Trenskow, Smans, Meerveld; Vente

Heerenveen have scored three or more goals in four of their last five league games and field five forwards of their own in Vente, Meerveld, Trenskow, Smans and Rivera, whereas Fortuna have lost Zeefuik and Romeny and lean heavily on Descotte and Ihattaren for goals.

Fortuna's unbeaten run and their record of two or more goals in four of the last five meetings cannot be ignored, but they have won only two of six home league games, twice surrendered a lead against Twente and Telstar, and will start a stand-in goalkeeper against a side that has scored 16 goals in their last five league games.

Five of the last six meetings have produced at least three goals, including Heerenveen's 2-1 win on April 25, 2026 and Fortuna's 2-0 win on November 8, 2025, so Descotte should score again, but Heerenveen's depth and momentum make them the likelier side to land the decisive second.

#1536. Alisson’s brilliance takes the breath away to show way forward for Liverpool

Andoni Iraola spun on his heels, turned his back to the action and began to bite his nails. Managers often envisage the worst outcome when the clock ticks down, and here, in the 93rd minute, Bournemouth had a corner.

He needn’t have worried. As the set-piece was swung in, Alisson Becker moved powerfully off his line and plucked the ball from the air, a catch that essentially confirmed Liverpool would leave Dorset with three points. It was a catch, too, that put the gloss on another impeccable personal afternoon.

When Iraola took charge at Anfield, one question he had to answer – given Bournemouth had conceded 167 goals in his three years in charge – was whether he could make Liverpool defensively resilient. This dour 1-0 success, though, proves he is taking them in the right direction: he is the first Liverpool manager since Joe Fagan in 1983 to start with five unbeaten league games.

Alexander Isak might have scored the goal that leaves Bournemouth winless in the Premier League but this success owed everything to Alisson’s enduring brilliance – a comment that also applies to Virgil van Dijk – the enormous promise of Jérémy Jacquet and the grit of Ronaldo Araújo.

You go to top level football matches hoping to see something that will take your breath away and how Alisson did that in the 17th minute with a reflex save from an Evanilson backheel, the shape of his body resembling a fielder in the slips diving to prevent a boundary.

It proved to be the foundation stone from which Liverpool were able to build and inflict Bournemouth’s first home defeat since January. There are plenty of [valid] questions to ask of Liverpool’s attack at present but, defensively, it is starting to come together.

“It was a really good fight,” Alisson said, in that self-effacing way of his. “But we have to improve a lot – on the ball and sometimes off the ball as well but we improved in the second half. We adapted to the opponent and that’s what we are doing.”

Any manager with a well-drilled defence stands a chance of improving and that is what Liverpool are doing. Only four weeks ago the discussion was about how easy it was for teams to play through their middle – remember that chaotic afternoon at Newcastle to start? – but that is changing swiftly.

Since Iraola replaced Jeremie Frimpong with Araújo at right-back, three consecutive Premier League clean sheets have followed. Araújo, the Uruguayan on loan from Barcelona, revels in doing the dirty work while Jacquet, the £60m signing from Rennes, oozes quality.

“He’s [Jacquet] very young and adapted really well to the Premier League,” Iraola said. “The first games, he was physically feeling the change of rhythm and I had to sub him. This was a step forward. He looked solid until the end. He’s in a good place physically and I hope he can continue his development.”

Don’t confuse positivity about one aspect of the team as being a guide to its collective health. There was always a chance this contest would become a cagey affair and, Evanilson’s chance aside, the opening 45 minutes were as flat as you could imagine.

Iraola again played his three £100m+ signings but Bradley Barcola is still adjusting to the physicality of English football and Florian Wirtz is still finding it difficult to impose himself on a game; patience with the German will not be infinite.

He would do worse than to look at Isak, who is now on a run of four goals in four league games and is influencing games in the manner Liverpool envisaged when they broke the British transfer record to sign him last August.

Isak had an unusual afternoon. His only shot in the first half almost took out some low-flying pigeons, a cross early in the second half was sliced so badly that the weekend hackers on the nearby Queens Park golf course would have felt a flood of sympathy but then he got his third opening.

Cody Gakpo, who could have been in Manchester City blue had the cards played out differently earlier this month, wriggled down the right flank and squeezed in a cross that Isak seized upon and turned in from six yards. Liverpool never looked back.

Alexander Isak grabs his fourth Premier League goal of the season! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/5ehwhl1it4

“A striker’s job is like this,” Iraola said, who badgered Isak persistently to press Bournemouth’s defence. “He had a couple of crosses that he did not hit properly or control. He has to help us to be closer to the box, to play in the opposition’s half and have more meaningful possession. And then if the team is playing there, he will receive rewards in terms of goals.”

One, ultimately, was enough to see off Bournemouth, whose start to the campaign is something of a riddle. They shouldn’t be anywhere near the relegation places but that is the reality and Thursday’s historic Europa League win in Real Sociedad couldn’t mask the home crowd’s frustration.

“Our attitude and effort is good,” head coach Marco Rose said. “But, at this level, small things and little details decide games.”

Speaking to Sky Sports after the match, Iraola said: “I’m obviously happy with the result because I know this is a difficult place to come, very difficult place to get three points. And we could see it, especially in the beginning of the game. In the first 20 minutes we weren’t at the level [required] and it cost us. We finished the first half better and in the second half we played better, but that beginning of the game has surprised us, not surprised us [because] we knew where we were coming but it [was] difficult for us.”

Jeremy Jacquet has made the kind of quietly authoritative start to his Liverpool career that showed why there was such excitement in February within the club when they completed his deal. So much focus on so many players but Jacquet has never been anything other 7.5/8 out of 10.

"Let's go! One of many!" Virgil van Dijk giving Jérémy Jacquet his POTM award after Liverpool's 1-0 win at Bournemouth ⭐️ pic.twitter.com/6xWvjmrF8Y

"That's a big moment to me to play with Virgil!" 🫡Jérémy Jacquet after Liverpool's 1-0 win at Bournemouth! pic.twitter.com/UsTimGME39

Cody Gakpo has been Liverpool’s stand-out forward this term and he was at the heart of Isak’s goal this afternoon. Speaking about the job the Dutchman is doing to fill the void left by Mohamed Salah on the right flank, Ashley Young said on Sky Sports: “Players have to step up when you lose big players and you get the opportunities. I think Cody Gakpo is doing that. He’s a bit fortunate [in the build-up to Liverpool’s goal] but you create your own luck. He gets the ball down the line, that’s what you want to do and he puts the ball in the box. That’s what Isak’s waiting for.”

Fair play to anyone who retained Brobbey in their Fantasy Football teams this week...

Erling Haaland has now scored against all 25 teams he has faced in the Premier League ✅⚽ pic.twitter.com/X9uqcrgbwk

Araujo gets his pocket picked in the corner but Jebbison cannot compose himself and blasts his cross off the other side of the pitch.

Liverpool go the other way and win a corner, but Mac Allister puts too much air on his delivery and it is easily dealt with.

Rayan wins a free-kick as he holds off Kerkez on the halfway line. Bournemouth then switch play to the far side but Truffert’s speculative effort flies well over the bar.

Nyoni shows off his composure on the ball, playing simple passes on the half-turn to keep play flowing. The midfield area is quite congested, which suits Liverpool at this point in the game.

Liverpool are baiting Bournemouth’s press in an attempt to play around their front line. They are doing a good job at holding on to the ball and frustrating their opponents, for now.

Gravenberch and Koumas are on for Gakpo and Isak.

Brooks has brought some energy to Bournemouth’s forays down the left. He attempts to slip a ball into the left channel but Nyoni is wise to it and positions himself perfectly to cut it out.

Liverpool have dropped deep and Bournemouth wait patiently for an opening. They eventually find Tavernier in the left half-space but his cross flies over everyone.

That is his last contribution to the match as Rose rings the changes: Tavernier, Smith and Christie make way for Brooks, Jebbison and Cook.

Truffert spins in a teasing ball from the left but Jacquet does well to flick the ball away from the danger zone.

Wirtz and Barcola make way for Nyoni and Munoz. Quiet afternoon from both of the outgoing players.

A stunning block from Hill prevents Isak pulling trigger as he looked to have the goal in his sights.

Truffert clears the resulting corner to safety.

Isak is concentrating his efforts in more central areas and here he almost gets played in behind but the ball just runs away from him. Better.

Worth mentioning that Jacquet has been fantastic in all phases of the game. Plenty of advanced regains and tidy passes forward.

It’s raining goals in Manchester and no prizes for guessing who has scored for Sunderland. Brobbey has his hat-trick.

Brobbey has his hat-trick and the look on Enzo Maresca’s face as he assesses the defending from his team. They’ve been great pouring forward, less so trying to stymie Sunderand’s attack. But this is one of those games where you just sit back and enjoy the unfolding drama. It’s been so good from both teams.

Semenyo gets his second goal of the afternoon to extend the league leaders’ advantage.

Chance! Jacquet jumps and wins the ball well inside Bournemouth’s half and his intervention sends the ball into Isak’s path. The forward just drags his effort wide and turns out he was in an offside postion anyhow.

What an afternoon this is turning out to be. There have been more slices than on an erratic day on the local municipal golf course and Ronald Araujo is the latest to be afflicted by the condition. None of that will matter to Andoni Iraola, though, as Alexander Isak’s fourth goal in four Premier League games has given Liverpool a huge advantage. They haven’t played with fluency but the breakthrough was significant.

Isak opens the scoring at the Vitality, finally getting into the box and sweeping in from close range. So much credit has to go to Gakpo who tiptoes past two Bournemouth defenders by the touchline before spearing a cross infield, and while he may not be attributed with the assist owing to a touch off Wirtz, his delivery makes it all the way through to Isak who taps in.

Alexander Isak grabs his fourth Premier League goal of the season! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/5ehwhl1it4

Adams has been superb as one of Bournemouth’s two midfield sentries. Kerkez looks to have been played into the left channel but the American swoops in and shields the ball out of play before staring down his Hungarian opponent.

Mitchell thinks he’s given the visitors the lead but his goal is ruled out for offside.

Tyrick Mitchell's opener is disallowed for an offside in the build up! ❌ pic.twitter.com/7y975TxaUj

Liverpool give up possession in Bournemouth’s half and Christie strides forward releasing Rayan before continuing his run to the near post. The Brazilian picks out his team-mate but Christie gets too strong a contact on the ball and the ball sails wide.

Truffert passes the ball straight to Gakpo inside his own box but Adams is on the scene in a flash and snaps into a tackle and takes the ball away from the Liverpool forward.

The second has already settled into a holding pattern, with neither side creating much. Isak makes a run down the right hand side and, with players loaded in the box, he blasts the ball high into the sky and beyond his team-mates. That pretty much sums things up.

Wirtz has given the ball away twice in the first minute of the second half. Carragher is on Sky Sports commentary duties and he says he’s surprised to see him back out on the pitch.

Szoboszlai concedes a foul on the far side but the subsequent delivery is too heavy and sails over everyone.

No half-time changes from either manager.

3 - This is the first time that @ManCity have taken the lead three times in the first half of a Premier League match.Overall, it's just the seventh time in competition history that a side has gone ahead on three separate occasions in a first half.Canvas. pic.twitter.com/JaQ4qDarls

Isak’s first-half heatmap makes for interesting reading. The good news, for Liverpool fans, is that he’s stationed himself predominantly in the final third. The bad news... those positions have been everywhere but the box.

There must be significant temptation to drift out to the wide areas and drop deep when the ball is not coming to you, but surely Liverpool need their No 9 closer to Bournemouth’s goal?

Bournemouth 0 Liverpool 0Leeds United 0 Crystal Palace 0 Manchester City 3 Sunderland 2

Big chance missed from Haaland of all people to make it 4-2 to City in what has been a pulsating, spell-binding first 45 minutes. It’s fast, furious and a helluva lot of fun to watch. Brilliant from Ndiaye to tee up Haaland who shoots wide of a post. A game for attackers shall we say ...

There are significant advantages to having a goalkeeper who is 6ft 5in with long arms and massive hands. Brobbey’s shot cannons off Guehi and would have looped over a number of goalkeeper but Donnarumma sticks out a giant arm to help nudge the ball over the bar and keep City 3-2 in front in the fifth minute of first half stoppages

Not a pretty half from the returning Iraola’s side, who will need to be much better in the second period to challenge for the three points.

Bournemouth have dropped points late on in a number of matches this season and will perhaps rue not being able to capitalise on their early advantage.

City are in front. Again. Semenyo this time, he fires the ball beyond Roefs having collected a loose ball int he box.

Antoine Semenyo gets his first goal of the season! 🎯 pic.twitter.com/1n2W5Cyxz0

A relatively slick Liverpool move sees the ball worked out to Araujo on the right who has minded to bomb on with increasing frequency, and while he’s able to win a corner, Szoboszlai’s delivery is cleared with a minimum of fuss.

Iraola came into this game saying that his side held an advantage having played two days earlier than Bournemouth in midweek. You would never have guessed it from what we have witnessed here today.

And right on cue, a frustrated Isak attempts a specultative effort from range which sails high and wide.

Sunderland are level again as Brobbey scores after lengthy VAR check for offside.

Sunderland fans sing “F--- VAR” and City fans boo the delay while they both awaited the verdict, which has now gone Sunderland’s way

Brian Brobbey levels it AGAIN! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/YvelzwnmY8

Can’t hold a lead today City. Wow, Sunderland are level again in an instant and it’s that man Brobbey again. There’s a VAR check going on to check for offside

So, this is not a rush to make a sweeping criticism, it’s simply an observation. But Liverpool fans will be looking at Bradley Barcola and  waiting to see that first burst, that moment of electricity, that has showed why they bought him. It’s like you look for a touch, a pass, a moment of skill. He’s just had a shot saved but it all seems very tentative for him at the moment. And that is what he needs - a moment.

Jacquet does brilliantly to close down Christie as the Scot was stealing into the box and looking to pull the trigger.

Chances! Barcola forces Petrovic into an awkward-looking save, before follow-up efforts from Wirtz and Gakpo are charged down.

Mac Allister is fouled 25 yards out moments later and Szoboszlai gets another go. Here, he drags his effort just wide.

It’s all happening at the Etihad. Cherki restores City’s lead with his third Premier League goal of the season.

It’s a great finish from Cherki to put City back in front but it doesn’t happen if Ndiaye is quick to read Danso’s risky pass and win possession. Sharp as a button in that moment.

Rayan Cherki puts Manchester City back in front! 💫 pic.twitter.com/PP4MAV9kw3

A really poor piece of defending from Kerkez gives Bournemouth a free-kick out on the right. Tavernier spins in an inswinger but Van Dijk heads clear. Truffert launches another assault on Liverpool’s box off the second phase but Alisson is wise to it and gathers.

It appears that Liverpool are beginning to settle, they take the opportunity to circulate the ball in front of Bournemouth’s first line of pressure, waiting for the right moment to pounce. The final pass is poor, though, and Araujo through-pass goes all the way through to Petrovic. It was aimed at Isak ...I think.

Some signs of life from Liverpool, as they create a substantial overload down their left, Kerkez, Mac Allister, Barcola and Isak meeting on that flank. Barcola attempts a sprint into the channel off the shoulder of the ball-side centre-back but he is deemed offside. Looked close, but a bit better from Liverpool.

Araujo has the chance to launch a long throw into the box but Silva beats Van Dijk to the summit and Petrovic gathers the loose ball.

Scott then sprays a wonderful ball over to Rayan on the right but his cutback to Tavernier comes to nothing after the midfielder loses the ball. Liverpool then spring a counter of their own, but Bournemouth recover and charge down a hopeful Gakpo effort from the edge of the box.

Liverpool will not be pleased with their start to this match. They’ve struggled to string more than three passes together without ceding possession and Isak has cut an isolated figure up top.

First time that Bournemouth have gone through the gears and the move ends with Alisson Becker saving brilliantly from Evanilson. It’s a funny stadium, here, as it can be quiet then all of a sudden a tempest whips up and you can sense the mood changing. Liverpool are struggling for alacrity and Andoni Iraola is keeping an eye on Florian Wirtz, who is moving gingerly after taking a bang to his left foot.

Some start at the Etihad. You had to wonder if a big early missed chance from Nilson Angulo was going to haunt Sunderland with City taking the lead just a few minutes later through a quite sublime free-kick from Enzo Fernandez. But Sunderland have immediately hit back. Maresca will decry the defending but it’s brilliant from Enzo Le Fee, who surges forward and then splits Nunes and Dias with an inch perfect pass that Brobbey takes beautifully in his stride before finishing.

On Fernandez’s free-kick before then, he’d very much shaped as if he’s going to cross the ball from a free-kick on the right side of the penalty area. He’d clearly spotted an opening in the top right though and, while giving the firm impression to Roefs he was going to whip in a cross, he obviously had other ideas. The execution was immaculate but it was telling just how effectively he’d managed to deceive the Sunderland goalkeeper. It was world class

A slight mix-up sees Kerkez and Wirtz bump into each other by the touchline. The Germany international limps away and grimaces but should be fine to continue.

Chance! Alisson makes amends with a stunning save. Tavernier had hit the by-line and lasered a cross to Evanilson who, with the ball slightly behind him, improvised and flicked it toward the near post. Alisson gets down swiftly and turns behind for a corner which comes to nothing.

Jacquet gives away a needless foul on the near side but Scott’s delivery goes straight into Alisson’s hands. The Brazilian’s throw out is poor, though, and Scott darts into Liverpool’s box, just unable to pick out a team-mate.

Barcola is presented with green grass to run into, but just as he builds a head of steam Hill comes across in a flash and snuffs out the foray forward.

Woah, Brobbey responds immediately, stealing in between City defenders before slotting past Donnarumma.

Instant response from Sunderland as Brian Brobbey equalises! 💥 pic.twitter.com/et6AHGPAbl

Enzo Fernandez opens the scoring at the Etihad with a direct free-kick from out wide. Really poor from Roefs who was caught napping. That’s Fernandez’s first City goal.

Enzo Fernandez gets his first Manchester City goal in style! 🤩 pic.twitter.com/fVOnJvACYY

Wirtz earns a free-kick just outside the D. Bournemouth feel aggrieved as there looked to have been an earlier foul on Scott and to make matters worse Szoboszlai is standing over the ball.

His effort leaves Petrovic rooted to the spot but the ball veers just wide of the mark.

Evanilson’s willingness to drop deep is asking questions of Liverpool’s centre-backs. Do they follow him and risk disrupting their backline coverage?

The hosts attempt to work a short corner routine but Truffert’s eventual through-ball is too strong and the ball rolls out for a Liverpool goal-kick.

This wouldn’t go down as a fixture you would circle for being noteworthy but make no mistake this is a huge afternoon for Liverpool. They have had some days at the Vitality Stadium in recent years and last season’s defeat put a huge dent in Arne Slot’s hopes of trying to find a revival. It’s also a big test for Bournemouth, coming down from the euphoria of beating Real Sociedad. Let’s see how it all transpires.

Evanilson makes a smart run into the right channel and while Jacquet gets his foot on the ball he’s instantly smothered by Scott and the ball goes out for a Liverpool goal-kick. A sign of how high both sides will be willing to jump in search of the ball.

Both sides will look to force mistakes out of the other and Szoboszlai is able to pick Adams’ pocket on the halfway line. He offloads to Araujo who runs into a cul de sac down the right flank.

We are under way at the Vitality. Bournemouth are in their customary black-and-red home shirts kicking from right to left and Liverpool are in their white away kit and red shorts.

The players have emerged from the tunnel, Van Dijk and Smith at the front of the lines. A few pyrotechnics add to the atmosphere but one thing missing is the accidental sitting in the wrong dugout from the returning Iraola. He knows where he’s going.

Here is a reminder of today’s squads in full:

The Egyptian king grabbed his first hat-trick for Trabzonspor yesterday, in a 4-0 win over league-leaders Galatasaray no less. That’s his seventh goal in eight matches.

When Salah is happy, we're all happy 👑👑👑 pic.twitter.com/DtzaOl3hD3

"He's certainly very quick"Jamie Carragher's first impressions of Bradley Barcola ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/oXjzXBuZwm

Since losing to Arsenal 3-2 on January 3, Bournemouth have not lost at the Vitality in 12 matches, picking up four wins and eight draws.

Jan 7: Bournemouth 3 Tottenham Hotspur 2Jan 24: Bournemouth 3 Liverpool 2 Feb 7: Bournemouth 1 Aston Villa 1Feb 28: Bournemouth 1 Sunderland 1Mar 3: Bournemouth 0 Brentford 0Mar 20: Bournemouth 2 Manchester United 2Apr 22: Bournemouth 2 Leeds United 2May 3: Bournemouth 3 Crystal Palace 0 May 19: Bournemouth 1 Manchester City 1Aug 29: Bournemouth 1 Everton 1Sep 8: Bournemouth 4 Lincoln City 0 (League Cup)Sep 12: Bournemouth 2 Brentford 2

Andoni Iraola returns to Bournemouth this weekend knowing what to expect from players he understands so well. Sadly, I do not mean Liverpool’s.

Having built his reputation creating a hard-working, well-drilled team rich in potential, Iraola is responsible for infusing those same characteristics into the most expensively assembled squad in Liverpool history.

His first six games demonstrate it is no quick fix. The Basque coach is the first Liverpool appointment to work with more than £700m of recent signings while being entitled to feel he has been dealt a bad hand.

Everything Iraola has said and done so far screams that he is searching for the right blend in his starting XI while having to eradicate negative traits, with and without the ball. It was telling that the excellent performance of his youngsters against Tottenham Hotspur in midweek offered the clearest hint of Iraola’s vision than anything we have seen with all the high-priced stars on the pitch.

There is a reason the Kop stood to acclaim the energy and application of youngsters Lewis Koumas, James McConnell and Trey Nyoni – and why Iraola keeps name-checking them. Iraola is indebted to them for issuing a reminder of the non-negotiables that come with being a Liverpool footballer; regardless of price tag and reputation, leaving everything on the pitch is compulsory. It is a concern that so many of the renowned players need to hear that message.

Jurgen Klopp named Florian Wirtz in his first squad as Germany manager and has said that fans must refrain from expecting “special moments” from the Liverpool playmaker as a matter of course.

Of Wirtz, he said: “I think he’s the player who covered the most ground at Liverpool this season, so the willingness is absolutely there.

“We have to move away from the idea that we need to see special moments from him. He is there to help us as a team. We have to make sure that Flo feels comfortable with us.”

Wirtz has delivered seven goals and 11 assists in his 54 Liverpool appearances.

Adam Smith, 35, played for Iraola 81 times and he admitted his former manager’s visit to the Vitality will be a sentimental affair. He said: “It’s going to be an emotional day for everyone I think, [for] our ex-manager and some of our players that have played under him, but we’ll be up for the game for sure.”

Your Eagles at Elland Road 🦅 pic.twitter.com/QGBqKJoSD1

📋 Your #LUFC XI... pic.twitter.com/U0fRnjJLjv

Bournemouth signed Truffert from Rennes in the summer of 2025 to replace Kerkez – who had just joined Liverpool – and the left-back has been a revelation at the Vitality. So much so that this week he earned himself a call-up to Zinedine Zidane’s first France squad.

Truffert topped the charts for most overlapping runs by any player in Europe’s top five leagues last season and laid on five assists.

Speaking before his return to the South Coast, Iraola said: “I know where we are going [the Vitality], and I know the stats they have there [unbeaten in 12 matches], not only in their stadium, overall, I think if you see the games they’ve lost in a long while, you realise how difficult it is to beat Bournemouth.

“But, I suppose I also have the advantage that I know them very well, they also have the advantage that they know me very well, so you never know who has more advantage in that sense.

He added: “On a personal side, I’m very much looking forward to meet them [his former players], to hug them. It’s players that I love, staff that I’ve been working with who I appreciate so much, and I was pushing for them [against Real Sociedad] when they were playing their first European game. I wish them all the best, but there is another part, which is the most important one right now that we need to go there and win.”

Just the one alternation to the side Rose fielded last weekend as Christie comes in for Kluivert.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the Premier League match between Liverpool and Bournemouth as Andoni Iraola returns to the Vitality Stadium for the first time since his big move up north. The Basque propelled Bournemouth to new heights, guiding the club into Europe and his successor, Marco Rose, ensured they made a winning start to life on the Continent by defeating Real Sociedad in midweek.

Previewing Iraola’s Vitality Stadium return, Craig Beazley, host and creator of the Up The Cherries In All Departments podcast, said: “We’ve now got the Andoni Iraola return … Andoni is very much a legend really, there should be a statue of Sir Eddie Howe and Sir Andoni Iraola [outside the ground] as well.”

Across three seasons, Iraola guided Bournemouth to 12th, ninth and sixth in the Premier League, winning 47 of his 127 matches in charge (37 per cent).

Liverpool are still acclimatising to his exacting style of play and their results suggest as much. They are 10th in the table having drawn three and won one, impressing in flashes but struggling to maintain consistently productive final-third patterns and pressing structures. Deploying Ronald Araújo at right-back has proved effective, though, with Liverpool conceding just two goals in their last four matches.

The Cherries are searching for their first Premier League win of the season and have retained the 4-2-3-1 shape from the Iraola days, with Rose preferring a similarly vertical attacking strategy. They continue to leverage their strengths in transitions and in wide areas as Adrien Truffert rains in crosses for any one of Bournemouth’s exuberant frontline to pounce on.

Elsewhere, Manchester City welcome Sunderland, who also secured a Europa League win during the week, to the Etihad while in-form Leeds United host Crystal Palace knowing a win would lift them into the top four.

#1535. Saturday's Premier League predictions including Man United vs. Brentford, Ipswich vs. Aston Villa

By Ben Knapton | 28 Nov 2026 00:00, Last updated: 28 Nov 2026 00:00

Today's Premier League predictions include Mauricio Pochettino's Manchester United home debut against Brentford, and Aston Villa's visit to Ipswich Town.

Mauricio Pochettino’s first match at Old Trafford as Manchester United head coach takes place on Saturday afternoon when Brentford visit the Theatre of Dreams for an intriguing Premier League contest.

While the Red Devils occupy a place in the relegation zone, sitting 19th in the Premier League table, the Bees are nine points and 13 places better off in sixth spot after 11 matches.

Despite Man United’s dismal start in the top flight, Pochettino's first Premier League home match in charge should spark enough attacking urgency from the hosts to trouble a Bees side that has struggled on its travels.

Taking into account that each of the last six head-to-head battles has seen both teams score, while 12 of Man United’s last 14 home matches have produced over 2.5 goals, we can envisage a wide-open, end-to-end affair ending all square on this occasion.

Two teams hoping to build on Premier League victories last weekend meet at Elland Road on Saturday afternoon, as Leeds United play host to Coventry City.

These two teams last butted heads in February 2025 when the Whites secured a 2-0 away victory in the Championship en route to promotion as champions.

With Leeds and Coventry both arriving at Elland Road in high spirits following victories last weekend, all signs point toward an entertaining clash given that five of the Sky Blues' last six league outings have featured at least four goals, and nine of the previous 13 meetings between the two sides have seen both teams score.

While a rejuvenated Coventry outfit will fancy their chances of breaching the hosts' backline, Leeds remain unbeaten on home soil this season and possess more than enough attacking firepower to claim their third league win in a row.

Aston Villa travel to Portman Road to face Ipswich Town on Saturday evening seeking to climb back into the top half of the Premier League table.

Both meetings between these two sides during the 2024-25 season ended in entertaining draws (2-2 in Suffolk and 1-1 at Villa Park), leaving the Tractor Boys still searching for their first top-flight triumph over the Lions since February 1993.

While Portman Road remains a far more forgiving environment for O'Neil’s side, who have collected seven of their 11 points on home soil this term (W2 D1 L2), Villa should relish the opportunity to rediscover their scoring touch against a porous Ipswich defence shipping an average of two goals per game.

Although the Tractor Boys are capable of keeping things competitive in Suffolk, we are backing Emery’s men to shake off their recent slump and grind out a hard-fought victory.

#1534. A tale of stars and struggles: Player ratings for Olympiacos-Milan from Italian papers

AC Milan recorded their second win in the Europa League by beating Olympiacos, and it came in dramatic circumstances.

When Jota Silva put Olympiacos 2-0 up after Lorenzo Pirola’s header cannoned off Mike Maignan to produce the opening goal, it looked like being another miserable night of continental football for Ruben Amorim’s men.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Yet, they roared back thanks to 15 minutes of madness. Omari Hutchinson inspired it, scoring a wonderful solo goal and then setting up both Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic to complete the comeback, before Diego Moreira sealed it late on.

This morning’s edition of La Gazzetta dello Sport starts us off with an 8 out of 10 rating for the team’s overall performance, and a 7.5 for Ruben Amorim after he made the right changes to inspire the comeback.

Hutchinson was the man of the match, getting an 8.5, while Koni De Winter struggled the most and scored a 5. Cisse and Pulisic each got a 7.5, while Moreira, Ardon Jashari, Yunus Musah and Fikayo Tomori received a 7.

Mario Gila, Adrien Rabiot and Filippo Terracciano were all praised (6.5s). Mike Maignan got a passing score of 6, while Sankhoun Diawara (5.5), Pervis Estupinan and Goncalo Ramos (5s) all struggled.

#1533. Report: Liverpool face transfer threat as club opens up contract talks

Liverpool have been linked with a lot of transfers this season.

Nobody knows exactly what's going to happen in the January window or even the 2027-28 summer window but, change is almost certainly afoot.

Without that, Liverpool will fall even further behind their title rivals and cause themselves more harm than good.

January is a notoriously hard time for clubs to agree deals with teams from across the globe demanding more money than usual due to the restricted time available to replace their players.

However, that doesn't mean it's impossible to get some over the line with one club now trying their luck with a Liverpool star.

Trabzonspor have opened up contract talks with Virgil van Dijk

One of the main players to have been linked with a Liverpool exit this summer is Virgil van Dijk.

The Dutchman's contract is set to expire in June 2027 and, since Liverpool don't know whether he's going to be able to keep his performance levels this high for another two years, they're waiting to decide whether he's worth another deal or not.

Most fans believe that he is because, on the market right now, there are little to no options available for Liverpool to explore, not ones that wouldn't cost a fortune, anyway.

But, because another two years will obviously be a lot of money for the Reds to commit to, they need to be 100% sure about their decision.

So, thanks to their stalling, media outlets have started to link Van Dijk with a move away from Liverpool with A Spor now sharing an update on the 35 year old's future.

"Trabzonspor, which caused a stir with the signings of Mohamed Salah , Andre Onana , and Fabinho, is showing no signs of slowing down in the transfer market," they wrote.

"It has been claimed that the Black Sea representative has begun official negotiations for 35-year-old veteran defender Virgil van Dijk, who is in the final year of his contract with Premier League giant Liverpool .

"While it is not yet clear whether the transfer will be finalized during the mid-season break or at the end of the season."

Liverpool can only let Virgil van Dijk go if they sign a replacement or have one lined up

Van Dijk has been Liverpool's rock at the back for as long as anyone can remember now.

The Dutchman has been their leader and is one of the main reasons why they've been so successful.

Without signing him in 2017, it feels like the Reds would have been nowhere near as dominant as they were.

Right now, they're trying to get back to that era and, while that's going to be difficult, it's certainly something that they can do.

But, if they sell Van Dijk and don't sign a replacement or at least have one lined up for the summer, they're going to dig themselves into a massive hole.

Nico Schlotterbeck, Jacobo Ramon and even Murillo are all solid options for Liverpool to explore but, if they don't get a deal for at least one new centre-back done before they allow Van Dijk to leave, some serious questions will need to be asked.

Here's hoping that Julian Ward and Iraola have a plan in mind.

#1531. Senegal KEEP Africa Cup of Nations title: Champions see crown restored in huge CAS verdict despite walking off the pitch in chaotic final against Morocco

Published: 09:30 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 14:47 EST, 24 November 2026

Senegal have been reinstated as Africa Cup of Nations winners after succeeding with an appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS), ten months after they beat Morocco in Rabat.

The ruling follows a controversial final in which Senegal initially won 1-0 after extra time, only for the result to be overturned following an appeal to Confederation of African Football (CAF) by the Moroccan Football Federation.

Two months after the final, the CAF appeal board ruled that Senegal had forfeited the match because their players had walked off the pitch in protest over a controversial penalty decision.

Morocco were subsequently awarded a 3-0 victory and the title. Despite that, Senegal refused to hand the trophy over.

That decision was based on Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON regulations, which state that leaving the pitch constitutes a forfeit.

However, following an appeal to CAS, Senegal have been reinstalled as champions, with the court ruling that FIFA's law that the referee’s decision is final takes precedence over the competition regulations.

Therefore, because the officials did not enforce the competition regulations at the time, there were no grounds to overturn the result.

The Moroccan FA, though, have not given up and have vowed to take the matter beyond CAS after questioning the integrity of panelist Ulrich Haas.

The Court of Arbitration for Sport has restored Senegal as Africa Cup of Nations winners after they were successful in their appeal

Morocco were awarded a 3-0 victory two months after the final, after it was ruled Senegal had forfeited the match by walking off the pitch in protest over a late penalty decision

Senegal fans clashed with security in Rabat after the controversial penalty decision

Ruling in favour of Senegal on Tuesday, CAS said: 'In the Panel’s view, there is no doubt that the effects of the Referee’s decision were limited to the pitch.

'As such, the Panel considers that the Referee’s decision was covered by the "field of play" doctrine.

'Since Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON Regulations are intended solely to determine the outcome of a match when a team’s conduct leads the referee to call off the game permanently, they are therefore not applicable in this case.'

A statement from the Moroccan FA later added: 'We take note of the decision of the Court of Arbitration for Sport regarding the appeal filed by the Senegalese Football Federation against the decision of the CAF Appeals Committee, relating to the final match of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations. In this context, the Royal Moroccan Football Federation expresses its surprise and protest at the failure to take into account its demand to arrange the necessary legal consequences for practices that would compromise the integrity and credibility of the arbitration procedure, especially what has been confirmed regarding communication between the German referee Ulrich Haas (who sat on the CAS panel) and the president of the Senegalese Football Federation, 48 hours before the decision was issued.

'The Royal Moroccan Football Federation also notes that the decision did not take into account the approach recently adopted by both the International Football Association Board (IFAB) and FIFA, regarding players leaving the field of play without the referee’s permission, and the resulting disciplinary responsibilities and penalties.

'Accordingly, the Royal Moroccan Football Federation confirms its intention to pursue all available legal avenues to appeal the decision of the Court of Arbitration for Sport.'

The chaos was triggered by events at the end of normal time, when referee Jean Jacques Ndala awarded Morocco a contentious penalty in the 98th minute after being called to the monitor by the video assistant referee to review El Hadji Malick Diouf’s challenge on Brahim Diaz.

The decision came just minutes after Senegal had seen a goal ruled out.

Furious with the penalty decision, Senegal manager Pape Thiaw instructed his players to leave the pitch in protest.

After a 17-minute delay, the team eventually returned, with former Liverpool forward Sadio Mane earning praise for remaining on the pitch and encouraging his teammates to continue.

In the dramatic aftermath, Real Madrid forward Brahim Diaz saw his Panenka penalty stopped by Senegal goalkeeper Edouard Mendy, before Ndala brought normal time to an end.

Senegal went on to score early in extra time, which has now led to a second title in the past three editions of the tournament with their 1-0 victory eventually confirmed in the courtroom.

#1526. Aston Villa's fortunes this season may depend on how quickly Unai Emery can make up his mind on his best XI and tactics as substituting John McGinn backfires in Galatasaray defeat, writes TOM COLLOMOSSE

Published: 15:24 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 16:26 EST, 24 November 2026

Aston Villa made a miserable return to Istanbul as they wasted a wonderful opportunity to put one foot in the last 16 of the Champions League.

In the city that saw them lift the Europa League in May, Villa produced a limp display against a Galatasaray side missing star centre-forward Victor Osimhen. Villa failed to register a shot on target and are now without a win in six games in all competitions.

Substitute Deniz Gul headed the only goal 13 minutes from time as Villa boss Unai Emery cut an angry figure on the touchline and was booked late on. He also appeared to have a tense exchange with midfielder Ross Barkley.

Here Daily Mail Sport's TOM COLLOMOSSE looks at the key moments from another unconvincing Villa display.

Aston Villa left John McGinn out of the starting XI last Saturday and dropped two points in a drab 0-0 draw with Sunderland.

The skipper was back here but three minutes after he was taken off, Villa conceded. Careless defending at a corner allowed Gul to head home, though he took an accidental boot in the face from Nicolas Jackson that required lengthy treatment.

Unai Emery's decision to substitute John McGinn backfired as Aston Villa lost at Galatasaray

Villa conceded three minutes after Emery decided to take off his captain (left) in Istanbul

Deniz Gul scored the only goal of the game with a close-range header on Tuesday evening

With McGinn on the field, Villa would surely have defended the corner better. Jackson's attempted clearance was poor and when the ball looped to Gul, others were too slow to spot the danger.

McGinn and Tyrone Mings are the leaders of this squad and in a period of such change, their role is more important than ever. Though Mings played here, he is no longer a regular starter.

While Emery's wish to protect McGinn is understandable, right now it is a luxury he cannot afford.

Aston Villa (4-2-3-1): Suzuki 6; Harwood-Bellis 6, Lindelof 7, Mings 6, Maatsen 5; Kamara 7 (Buendia 82), J Gomes 6 (Goretzka 66, 6); Alysson 5 (Mbaye 66, 5), McGinn 7 (Barkley 74, 6), Manzambi 5 (Hemmings 74, 6); Jackson 5.

Jackson has nine goals in 15 appearances for Aston Villa - but he has also picked up four yellow cards. Needless bookings proved the forward's downfall during his time at Chelsea and while he has been calmer at Villa, there is still work to do.

During one clash in the first half with Gala defender Davinson Sanchez, Villa boss Unai Emery raced to the edge of his technical area to stop Jackson talking his way into the book. Emery succeeded that time, but not long afterwards, Jackson was punished for a needless tussle with Wilfried Singo.

Jackson plays on the edge. That is a big part of his game. He is also 26 next June and has enough experience to understand when to step into an argument and when to hold back. Emery does not count on Tammy Abraham much these days and Brian Madjo is raw, so he needs Jackson to keep his cool.

The Senegal forward was not the only one to test the patience of referee Daniel Siebert. Joao Gomes was lucky only to be booked for bringing down Yunus Akgun and then grabbing his opponent, while John McGinn was furious that Aleksey Batrakov escaped with a booking for appearing to kick out at the Villa skipper.

Nicolas Jackson's ill-discipline is a concern, with the striker having collected four yellow cards

For most of the last four years, any Villa fan could have written down Emery's first choice XI. Not these days, as Emery still seems to be searching for the ideal formula.

His uncertainty is understandable after losing five key outfield players in the summer but Villa's fortunes this season may depend on how quickly Emery can make up his mind.

Zion Suzuki is the clear first choice in goal and then of the 10 outfield players, how many are lock-ins? Matty Cash and Victor Lindelof in defence. Boubacar Kamara in the middle. John McGinn and - probably - Johan Manzambi in the three-man attacking line, and Nicolas Jackson as centre-forward.

That leaves four spots still up for grabs and not enough of those players are doing enough to convince Emery they deserve the shirt.

Why Liverpool's future is extraordinary under IraolaPart of the reason why the positivity has returned to Anfield is not because the performances have been extraordinary. But it's because there is a future there. Liverpool fans can see the vision. It's hard not to when Alexander Isak is firing on all cylinders, Florian Wirtz is playing mesmerising football and on top of that Rio Ngumoha and Trey Nyoni are becoming stars in their own right. All the while Jeremy Jacquet has already established himself as the best young centre-back in Europe alongside the likes of Pau Cubarsi and others. There's the players yet to come through. Joshua Abe, Erik Farkas and Ifeanyi Ndukwe. Liverpool are making more and more signings like Lucca Brughmanns and Samuel Martinez.
