#1500. The two things Roberto De Zerbi demanded from Luca Williams-Barnett's first Tottenham start as 18-year-old star signs new lucrative deal, writes MATT BARLOW

Published: 08:08 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 18:17 EST, 24 November 2026

Having summoned Luca Williams-Barnett to his office to let the teenager know he would be making his first Premier League start, Roberto De Zerbi could not resist a little bit of fun.

De Zerbi cast a serious demeanour and told him he had weighed the options and figured the best course of action would be 60 minutes with the Under-21s.

Williams-Barnett did not hide his disappointment. 'Why, do you think you are ready to start for the first team?' asked the Spurs boss. The 18-year-old said he thought so.

De Zerbi cracked a smile and told him he was in the team against Ipswich but demanded two things in return.

First, that his young star would play with freedom as though 'in the park with friends' and second that he would work without the ball in the manner of the world's best players in his position, such as Lamine Yamal.

This is where the comparisons to Yamal emerged soon after Williams-Barnett lit up the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. On Tuesday, he was rewarded for his progress with a new contract at the club.

He said: 'This is a special moment for me and my family, and one I have worked really hard to reach. But this is only the start.

Luca Williams-Barnett scored his first Premier League goal for Tottenham on his first start in the top flight

The talented academy youngster may not be lightning fast but he has pace and creates goals

'Spurs is a family to me. I've been here for so long – it's a second home, where I trust the people and coaches who have pushed me to become the player I am today.

'The club has trusted and believed in me, now I'm ready to repay that.'

Hopes are indeed high. Similarities with Yamal are evident in physique, his fluency of movement on the ball and the bursts of pace, the way they look to play. Even the hairstyle.

Just as Yamal, a left footer, likes to operate wide on the right for Barcelona and Spain, De Zerbi deployed Williams-Barnett as a right footer on the left, although most of his youth career has been spent centrally in the No 10 position.

He does not possess what you would consider in modern football to be exceptional pace, but he is quick, and his strengths are on the ball. He likes the ball. He creates. And he scores goals.

From wide on the left against Ipswich, he scored within 15 minutes, darting in at the back post to finish, and created the second for Dominic Solanke, with a 60-yard run from inside his own half and cross with his left foot.

His brilliance lit up the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, where there has not been a lot to celebrate in the last 18 months. Terrible home form was the crux of last season's relegation fears.

Here, they rose to salute a new talent, one of their own. One De Zerbi believes has the attitude to match his outrageous talent. Confident, certainly. Aware of his natural gifts and his technical skills. Perhaps bordering on arrogance when on the pitch.

De Zerbi was pleased to see Williams-Barnett, in a seat nearby on the team bus from the training ground to the stadium, watching YouTube clips of Ronaldinho, Eden Hazard and Neymar.

The Spurs boss, who has faith in the power of inspirational video footage, took this as a positive sign. The youngster was relaxed but more than this he had a passion for football and always looking to learn.

'I'm positive about his character and behaviour because I've been working with him for three or four months and I know him enough,' said De Zerbi, whose tactical instructions involved James Maddison operating closely to Williams-Barnett, a kindred spirit in a footballing sense able to talk him through the game.

When the teenager set off on the swaggering run for Solanke's goal, Maddison could be seen nearby urging him forward into the ocean of space left open by Ipswich.

The 18-year-old had rival clubs circling but Spurs have now tied him down

Born and raised in Luton, Williams-Barnett comes from a strong, grounded family - which will only help as he looks to assimilate into the senior side

Spurs have prioritised Premier League experience in the transfer market under De Zerbi to create a more mature dressing room environment. Signings such as Andy Robertson have been key to this.

The policy is not purely for the benefit of academy graduates stepping into the first-team environment, but it does help when it comes to setting the standards required in elite sport.

Anyone gifted enough to break into the Spurs squad will have been feted as a star through the youth development phase and well rewarded to resist others trying to lure them away.

Williams-Barnett was under contract until 2028 but his new deal means clubs circling must now look elsewhere.

It is easy for impressionable teens to become conceited in this situation. Williams-Barnett has had discipline and time-keeping issues but most at Spurs speak of a young man devoted to his football from a strong, loving family who are sure to keep him grounded.

He was born and raised in Luton, starting out in Luton Town's pre-academy to Under 10s, before Spurs paid a small fee for him.

His father Jonathan Barnett was a central midfielder in Step Three of non-league football, known as 'Jono' and playing for various clubs in the region including Dunstable Town and Arlesey Town and renowned for his passing, set pieces and with an eye for goal.

Although more of a dribbler, Luca grew up with football in the family, polishing his technical skills with his dad in the back garden. 'He is from a very good family and it's crucial for this type of players,' said De Zerbi.

Spurs have been here before, of course, with talented teens breaking through with N17 at their feet.

There was Mikey Moore's wonderful cameo against AZ Alkmaar after which Ange Postecoglou called for patience and commonsense, and Maddison went on TV and said it was 'like having Neymar on the left wing'.

There was Jose Mourinho taking the match ball from Son Heung-min, who had just scored the most incredible solo goal against Burnley, and handing it to Troy Parrott on his Premier League debut.

There was Mauricio Pochettino dubbing Marcus Edwards his 'mini Messi'. Pochettino soon came to wish he had not burdened Edwards with such lavish praise.

The pitfalls are well known and progress is rarely a smooth upward trajectory. It is a balancing act between maximising potential and getting carried away.

De Zerbi is quietly confident Williams-Barnett has what it takes to handle the hype.

On the new deal, thought to be for five years, the manager said: 'Luca is a player I think the world of, and I'm so happy that he has signed a new contract.

'He has benefitted from being around the first team every day, growing in stature and consistency, and has deserved his place in the matchday squad over recent weeks.

'Everyone can see how technically gifted Luca is on the pitch but I also love his calmness and decision-making under pressure.

'The best players have confidence on the pitch and humility off it. There is still plenty of room for Luca to improve, and I know he will continue to work hard every day to be the best version of himself.'

No team has won more Bundesliga games than Schuster’s men this season, while only Borussia Dortmund boast a better defensive record.

The Breisgau Brazilians will also take encouragement from their last head-to-head meeting with RB Leipzig, which ended in a 4-1 win last May.

Chasing their fourth successive win across all competitions, it is fair to suggest that RB Leipzig are on fire.

Florent Muslija is the only major name on the sidelines, with the player still recovering from April’s knee surgery.

Winger Cyriaque Irie has scored two goals in three games and is pushing for his first Bundesliga start this season.

Top Freiburg goalscorers Igor Matanovic and Yuito Suzuki - who have five goals each - are both expected to lead the attacking efforts once more.

RB Leipzig, on the other hand, have a handful of names on the injury list heading into Sunday’s match.

Young forward Marc Guiu, for instance, has not played since September due to a hamstring injury.

Defender Castello Lukeba missed the win over Lens through a knee injury and is expected to remain on the sidelines.

Assan Ouedraogo, on the other hand, has only managed to make two competitive appearances this season, as he continues to nurse a shoulder injury.

#1497. Bruno Fernandes: The staggering numbers that explain why Man United cannot afford to lose their captain

By Naim Beneddra | 28 Nov 2026 08:53, Last updated: 28 Nov 2026 08:53

Manchester United have reportedly activated a one-year extension in Bruno Fernandes's contract, tying their captain to the club until June 2028 and removing the immediate risk of losing him on a free transfer at the end of the season.

However, with negotiations over a new long-term agreement on hold and interest in the Portugal international from elsewhere in Europe and Saudi Arabia, a departure in 2027 remains a possibility.

At 32, Fernandes could still command a significant transfer fee, but the statistics behind his six years at Old Trafford illustrate the scale of the rebuilding job that would await Mauricio Pochettino should United decide to sell their captain.

Fernandes has scored 115 goals in 343 appearances for United since joining from Sporting Lisbon in January 2020, but it is his creative output that makes him particularly difficult to replace.

Between February 2020 and April 2026, the Portuguese created 638 chances in the Premier League. No other United player managed more than 190 during the same period.

Fernandes also registered 67 assists, compared with 22 for his closest teammate, while his 171 through balls were more than four times the tally of United's next-best performer.

Numbers since his arrival in January 2020

Bruno vs. the squad's second-best in each category

Premier League, February 2020 to April 2026. Bar length = total over the period

Games, goals and assists up to 26/11/2026. *Chances created in the Premier League counted up to the end of 2025/26. The internal ranking compares Bruno with all United players over the same period.

Sources: Manchester United, Opta, Opta Analyst, ESPN and TNT Sports

The comparison also stands up beyond Old Trafford. By May 2026, Fernandes had created 220 more Premier League chances than any other player since his debut in the competition, with former Manchester City midfielder Kevin De Bruyne his closest challenger.

Last season alone, Fernandes created 136 chances, 58 more than any other player in the division, and established a new Premier League single-season record with 21 assists, surpassing the previous benchmark shared by Thierry Henry and De Bruyne.

What makes the figures particularly remarkable is that Fernandes has sustained such productivity throughout a period of considerable instability at United, working under several managers and occupying different midfield roles.

Fernandes has not consistently reached the same heights this season, but he has still registered eight goals and three assists in 16 appearances across all competitions, including a brace against his former club Sporting in Wednesday's Champions League draw.

Pochettino could get an early indication of how his team functions without the Portuguese, who has emerged as a major doubt for Saturday's Premier League clash with Brentford due to illness.

Over the longer term, Como's Nico Paz has emerged as a potential successor to Fernandes, but recruiting another talented attacking midfielder would only address part of the problem.

The Portuguese regularly drops deep to initiate attacks, takes responsibility for set pieces and provides a goal threat from midfield. His ball recovery figures also demonstrate the extent of his contribution without possession.

Replacing that range of qualities could require changes across several positions, with greater creative responsibility placed on United's wide players and deeper midfielders.

There is a legitimate financial argument for considering offers for a player who will turn 33 next September, particularly if the proceeds can help fund Pochettino's rebuilding project.

However, United's recruitment strategy would need to account for how much of their attacking production has come from a single player over the past six years.

The contract extension gives the club additional time to address that imbalance. Selling Fernandes before establishing a more productive and less dependent midfield would risk creating another major problem for a manager already facing a considerable rebuilding job at Old Trafford.

“[He was] Very instinctive – I say this with a smile – very American, full of slogans in the early days of that revolution, now much more cautious, much more thoughtful, much more attentive. “He will be alongside the coach, he will be alongside the team, he will obviously direct the transfer market, but not only the transfer market. He will have a very important role within the Milan world, but what I can say is that Cardinale will no longer delegate like before.

“I understand that this time he doesn’t want to be serious: this time he wants to put his face on the line, he wants to put his money and also his commitment. He will travel and continue to travel. From Italy, from Milan to New York and from New York to Milan, as if it were a simple Milan-Rome journey, and he’ll do it practically every week because he doesn’t want to take a step back.

“So, ok, Krösche, but Milan remains and will remain in his hands, in my opinion, including his decisions. In fact, Endrick was an idea born even before Krösche, and I believe that Milan is pursuing it and will continue to pursue it in the coming weeks.”

#1495. Nottingham Forest 3-2 Chelsea: Xabi Alonso responds to Wesley Fofana boos, chants in City Ground defeat

By Darren Plant | 28 Nov 2026 09:25, Last updated: 28 Nov 2026 12:07

Xabi Alonso has encouraged Chelsea supporters to show unity with the team after Wesley Fofana was booed during the 3-2 defeat to Nottingham Forest.

The Blues suffered a fourth defeat in five top-flight fixtures to face the likelihood of ending the weekend in the bottom half of the Premier League table.

Alonso made headlines before the match through naming Fofana in his starting lineup, despite comments made by the Frenchman earlier in the week.

At his pre-match press conference, Alonso had revealed that the centre-back had apologised for revealing that he was convinced not to retire from football due to the wages that he earns and joking about his decisive miss in a penalty-shootout defeat to Liverpool in the EFL Cup in October.

Chelsea's away support at the City Ground vented their frustration that Fofana kept his place in the team.

Fofana was responsible for giving away a needless penalty against Forest, who took a 2-0 lead, before he was eventually substituted.

Nevertheless, Alonso has called for unity between the team and supporters as they continue to struggle on the pitch.

He told Sky Sports: "Everyone in the club and team, we need to stick together and go through this moment. We have to deal with it and we are responsible.

"It is a difficult moment for everyone at the club. For the team and the fans. Disappointed to lose again but we need to keep trying to find solutions.

"We can't stop. We are low in confidence and the team is struggling to hold a result.

"After getting to 2-1, we concede to 3-1. We are responsible for that and responsible to try and find solutions."

When specifically asked about Fofana's confidence, Alonso said: "We need to support everyone. We know that we are going through difficult moments. We need to stick together."

Despite Chelsea's productive start where they scored a hatful of goals, they have looked weak in defence throughout the season.

Alonso has made a range of mistakes across his early tenure, and selecting Fofana against Forest was one of his most glaring errors.

Although Chelsea officials naturally want some stability, this Chelsea side are performing worse the more that they work with the former Bayer Leverkusen and Real Madrid boss.

If Chelsea lose at home to Crystal Palace on Wednesday night, Alonso may already be at the point of no return.

The report claims the 23-year-old France international does not suit the wing-back system Alonso has built at Stamford Bridge. It also floats a surprise swap that would send Gusto to Liverpool and reunite Alonso with Jeremie Frimpong, his former Bayer Leverkusen right wing-back.

Liverpool’s interest has history. They tried to sign Gusto on loan on deadline day, but Chelsea refused anything short of a permanent deal. Their right-back problem has run since Trent Alexander-Arnold left. Frimpong cost around £29.5million and has battled injuries and form, while Ronald Araujo is a centre-back covering on a season-long loan from Barcelona.

Gusto’s standing has slipped quickly. He started three of the first four league games, yet Josh Acheampong has since taken his place, and reports say he will be fourth choice behind Acheampong, Marco Palestra and Reece James once James returns from injury in early 2027.

His strength is defending, with 73 tackles and 36 chances created in 45 appearances last season. The weakness is end product, because three goals and five assists are modest for a wing-back who must supply Alonso’s right-hand width.

Frimpong supplies exactly that. The 25-year-old Dutchman scored 28 of his 30 Leverkusen goals under Alonso and thrives on pace and early crosses. Defending is his flaw, at 5ft 8in and with a poor injury record at Anfield.

No. Chelsea are fifth with 16 points from 10 games, but they have lost four, including 1-0 at Sunderland last Sunday and 3-0 at Brentford, and they concede too easily. Sell Gusto instead, preferably abroad, since Paris Saint-Germain have been linked and Chelsea are reportedly open to cutting their asking price. Then spend that fee on a defensive midfielder or centre-back, because that is where Alonso’s team needs help.

#1491. England throw it away with defending unworthy of a top nation

There had been so much talk – first raised by Thomas Tuchel after the shocking World Cup exit to Argentina – about England’s DNA. About whether they could keep the ball, pass the ball, control the ball, the way Spain do.

The world and European champions were England’s first opponents – after the World Cup – in this Nations League campaign and came away from Wembley with a deserved win. They are now 39 games unbeaten with substitute Mikel Oyarzabal, who scored the winning goal against England in the final of the last European Championship, doing so again.

Mikel Oyarzabal SCORES against England AGAIN! 🎯Spain retake the lead after a slick finish from the Spaniard 👏#ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/pPT3KvRHWl

That may have been no surprise, even if the inevitable “olés” after Spain’s third goal will have hurt. But the nature of it? For the England manager this was another shocker. Not in the way his team went about the task. They were positive, fun, attacking. But in the way they conceded – goals and chances – and lost.

On this performance, DNA, for England, stands for Defensively Not Able, as they threw away what could have been a famous and restorative victory. Instead, with Croatia beating the Czech Republic in the other group game, England are under immediate pressure to win in Prague on Tuesday.

In fact, England have conceded 13 goals in their past six matches – in fairness including four in that third-place World Cup 6-4 win over France – and that is not good enough for a top-tier nation. Tuchel needs to sort it out defensively.

It could have been very different if Harry Kane had not missed from the penalty spot, slipping as he struck the ball, with England improbably 2-1 ahead. “It would have been the decisive punch,” Tuchel stated. Maybe so, even if there was always the feeling that Spain could go through the gears.

Kane MISSES from the penalty spot! 😧Harry Kane slips when he strikes the ball, let off for Spain and Luis de la Fuente#ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/pvg3GGa9ma

Afterwards there were claims, led by the impressive Anthony Gordon, that this was a missed opportunity for England. A bit like the World Cup. They need to shake this theme.

The irony was this was one of their best creative displays for quite some time. They took the game to Spain and could have scored more. And conceded more.

In truth it could have been Spain 4 England 0 inside half an hour and before Tuchel’s team laid a glove on their opponents.

Another let off for England 😧Ferran Torres misses another big chance one-on-one with James Trafford #ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/KFkJoJUW6c

The manager had also spoken about how England should “embrace the chaos” as their best route to success. That may appear a questionable tactic – does chaos ever win a tournament? – but England certainly did that. This was as chaotic and, admittedly, entertaining as it gets.

England attacked with pace and power with the pick of their players the two based in Spain: Gordon, who scored, and Jude Bellingham. And the defenders? This was a bad night for Marc Guéhi, his Manchester City team-mate Nico O’Reilly (cue speculation about whether they were distracted by the verdict on the Premier League charges against their club) and for Jarell Quansah at right-back who is so evidently a centre-half.

A penny, once more, for the thoughts of the unused Trent Alexander-Arnold. The fourth defender, Ezri Konsa, vented his frustration at what was happening around him.

It was not just the errors but the unforced nature of them. Poor in possession with misplaced passes and defensively wide open. There is a gap between Spain and England but not as big as the gaps that were exposed in England’s back four. They endured a full house of calamities. They seemed strangely unaware – or incapable of dealing with – the danger posed by the outstanding Lamine Yamal.

Maybe because of the opposition – or the criticism – England felt the need to play out. But what an horrific start. What an inexplicable moment for Guéhi as he received the ball from O’Reilly and turned into trouble, gifting possession to Yamal who ran on and scored. Inside two minutes.

WHAT A START FROM SPAIN 🇪🇸Lamine Yamal pounces on a Marc Guéhi error to give Spain an early lead at Wembley #ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/Et83EyTPlp

Spain walked out with the second star on their shirt – to mark their second World Cup triumph. That was the star Tuchel had promised for England.

Now, straight away, they were up against it. It could have turned very ugly. Ferran Torres, who had scored the winner in the World Cup Final, had one disallowed for offside, then was thwarted by James Trafford after – inexplicably again – being played onside by Quansah.

BIG SAVE from James Trafford 🧤The Leeds United goalkeeper keeps out Ferran Torres#ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/nj5b8AUSQU

Then Torres was sent clear following Elliot Anderson’s poor pass, only to drag his shot wide. The third miss came from Dani Olmo, again set up by Yamal.

It could – it should – have been game over. Then England unexpectedly turned it around. They had kept attacking despite what was going on at the back and struck through a truly thrilling counter-attack, with Gordon and Bellingham combining before the Barcelona winger calmly beat goalkeeper Unai Simon.

ENGLAND ARE LEVEL! 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿A brilliant finish from Anthony Gordon after a breathtaking counter attack 👏#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/z0nSfWIHVd

It was an exceptional goal and was quickly followed by a fortunate one as O’Reilly’s cross was met by Kane who stooped to steer in a header, only for it to strike Marc Cucurella, who made a mess of clearing, and it went past Simón.

I think we'll give that goal to Harry Kane 🎯England come from behind to lead Spain thanks Harry Kane, with assistance from Marc Cucurella ⚽️#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/X3qSOWUhVT

The Spain left-back hit the post with a cross, misjudged by Trafford who was given this game and the next to stake his claim ahead of Jordan Pickford who has so long been the undisputed first-choice.

England dominated for a while and Bellingham won a penalty, after a VAR intervention, only for Kane to strike the crossbar.

How Spain made them pay and worryingly so. O’Reilly passed the ball straight to Olmo who swept it inside. Substitute Álex Baena checked and beat Trafford from the edge of the area. Even worse was how Spain cut through the heart of England defence with Baena finding Oyarzabal. Why was no defender closer to him? What was Guéhi doing? And O’Reilly? Oyarzabal exquisitely dinked the ball over Trafford.

Thomas Tuchel does not think Manchester City’s guilty verdict over almost all of their Premier League charges distracted his England players in the Nations League defeat to Spain.

City players Marc Guéhi and Nico O’Reilly were at fault for two of Spain’s goals and both Tuchel, the head coach, and England captain Harry Kane confirmed news of the verdict had been discussed among the squad.

Tuchel does not plan to address the issue with his players ahead of the remaining Nations League games against Czech Republic and Croatia.

Asked if the City verdict had been a cause of discussion ahead of the Spain game, Tuchel replied: “Not for me, but I can imagine maybe for the Man City players. I won’t comment on it as it’s an ongoing case.

“I didn’t make it a topic. It was not a topic for me. I’m just thinking about Spain and the team and meetings. The players have more time than me. So I can imagine they talk about it. It’s good they do. I don’t think it was a distraction for them.”

Kane added: “There was a discussion, but when we’re with England, we kind of put club football to one side and it was no different this week.”

Tuchel also refused to point the finger of blame at Guéhi, O’Reilly or Kane, who missed a penalty, for England’s defeat despite admitting his team got off to the worst possible start by conceding a goal after two minutes.

“We will focus on the positives, but also highlight the stuff we can do better,” Tuchel said. “Not even speaking about individual mistakes because this is normal. It just happens. It should not happen, and for sure not in this amount. But there is no sense in showing the individual mistakes or telling them ‘please don’t make mistakes’. That is normal, but we can do things better. We can defend the third goal better. But we will focus on the positives. There is a lot to take away from the game.

“We wanted to be the team desperately to beat them [Spain] and we think we had them. We still think we had them at half-time. That was the way the team showed up after half-time. So we will focus on that, but the reality is we lost and the reality is we need to prove it again.”

“It was a terrible start, the worst possible start, which makes it so difficult against a team like this. The reaction was very good. After 10/12 minutes, we were the better team but we gave away too many mistakes. We were the better team. If we had converted the penalty, it could have been the decisive moment. We have to keep going and learn from the mistakes. We could have created more if we had been more clinical in the final 20 metres. We showed great bravery and courage with our high-ball wins. There will always be moments you suffer against teams like this. The effort and quality were there tonight but the result does not prove it today.”

“I think there is a gap [between Spain and England]. They [Spain] are the world champions and European champions. Mikel Oyarzabal was never going to miss. He was always in control of the situation. Honestly, people talk about sexy football, that is sexy football. I would watch that all night.”

🗣️ "We went toe to toe with the European and world champions" 💪Harry Kane remains positive about England performance despite their 3-2 defeat to Spain 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿🇪🇸#ITVFootball | @gabrielclarke05 | @England pic.twitter.com/qkhqsqmPEl

Marc Guehi and Nico O’Reilly may want to look away now but Jude Bellingham and Anthony Gordon scored well. Our very own Mike McGrath has provided his player ratings.

Tonight: England 2 Spain 3 (H)Tuesday September 29: Czech Republic (A), kick-off 7.45pmSaturday October 3: Croatia (A), kick-off 5pmTuesday October 6: Czech Republic (H), kick-off 7.45pm

🗣️ "I think it's a bit of a missed chance" 👀Anthony Gordon says mistakes cost England the win tonight against Spain at Wembley 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿#ITVFootball | @gabrielclarke05 | @England pic.twitter.com/AJBxVNjbjq

A highly entertaining game. England will probably argue the game changed on Kane’s missed penalty, but Spain missed a lot of very clear chances and will feel they deserved the victory. A losing start to the Nations League for Tuchel and his team, but there were some positives. Gordon, Bellingham and Anderson were all excellent. Some of the defending, not so excellent.

Possession: England 47%-53% SpainShots: 13-15Shots on target: 5-5Corners: 6-3Touches in opposition box: 37-15

England have one last chance with a corner out on the left. This will be it. Spain are able to deal with it and clear their lines.

Then comes the final whistle at Wembley and the world champions Spain claim a 3-2 victory in north London. It was an absorbing game, where momentum swung one way and then the other, but it is Spain who are the victors.

Baena brings down Rogers with a silly challenge to gift England a free-kick deep in the Spanish half. This could be England’s last chance.

Anderson is over it but his delivery is poor, easily caught by Unai Simon.

England are running out of time to find an equaliser.

O’Reilly appears to be suffering with cramp but England have made all five substitutions.

A late change for England as Branthwaite replaces Guehi.

Rogers delivers a dangerous cross from the right that runs through the six-yard box and forces Pubill to put it behind for a corner.

England take it short before Anderson clips it in but Laporte heads away.

Garner should have done so much better with that. His run into the Spain box on the left side is picked out by Anderson’s pass. Garner has Calvert-Lewin waiting at the back post but the former massively overhits the cross.

Double substitution from England as Calvert-Lewin and Gibbs-White replace Kane and Saka. Rare to say Kane taken off, especially when England are behind.

Saka goes down under a challenge from Cucurella inside the Spain penalty box but no penalty is forthcoming. VAR has cleared the incident. Moments later, Bellingham is then booked for stopping Spain going on the counter.

Spain make a change as Merino replaces Olmo.

The way Spain control possession and keep the ball is impressive. They toy with you pretty well and often look so composed.

Baena, who has been superb since coming on, feeds a lovely pass into the path of Oyarzabal on the right side of the box. Oyarzabal takes one touch before lifting it over Trafford into the England net. That is a lovely assist from Baena and lovely finish from Oyarzabal.

Mikel Oyarzabal SCORES against England AGAIN! 🎯Spain retake the lead after a slick finish from the Spaniard 👏#ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/pPT3KvRHWl

Given the quality of the opposition and the sustained threat he carried, that might have been Gordon’s best-ever performance in an England shirt. Him and Bellingham have been excellent. But now he’s been replaced by Morgan Rogers.

Guehi joins O’Reilly in the book for a cynical foul on Olmo. You can put that yellow card in the category of a professional foul.

England are making a double change as Garner and Rogers come on for Lewis-Skelly and Gordon. Garner was not in the initial squad but takes his chance now after the withdrawals.

Spain also make a substitution as Pedri replaces Ruiz.

At one end, Yamal has a shot blocked after England gave the ball away before Lewis-Skelly’s shot down the other end is easily saved.

The first booking of the night sees O’Reilly shown a yellow card for a foul on Yamal.

England come close to going back in front. After good work from Bellingham, Saka has it on the right side of the box. Saka cuts inside onto his left and looks to pick out the far corner but his effort goes narrowly wide.

Another big mistake from England is punished. It is absolutely dreadful from O’Reilly, who gives the ball away so poorly deep inside the England half. Spain capitalise and it is the man who has only just come on, Baena, who curls into the bottom corner from the edge of the box. All to play for with half an hour to go at Wembley.

SPAIN EQUALISE! 🇪🇸A brilliant finish from Alex Baena after a Nico O'Reilly mistake 🎯#ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/tXygPfbPmb

Yamal and Baena exchange a lovely one-two on the right side of the box and you think the former will find the far corner but his effort goes wide.

How did Yamal MISS that! 🤯A big opportunity goes begging to pull Spain level! #ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/jyzLm9VBd5

Cucurella has a real habit of making himself unpopular wherever he plays. The Wembley crowd have been booing his every touch and were not happy with him staying down after the ball hit him in the head. Spain haven’t got going at all in this second half.

Spain have made a double change as Oyarzabal and Baena replace Torres and Williams.

Kane steps up but his effort smashes into the bar. Kane slipped just as he took it. In fact, a free-kick is given to Spain as it was a double hit.

Kane MISSES from the penalty spot! 😧Harry Kane slips when he strikes the ball, let off for Spain and Luis de la Fuente#ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/pvg3GGa9ma

The referee overturns the original decision and points to the spot. A foul from a Barcelona midfielder on a Real Madrid midfielder is given.

Yet more England appeals for a penalty. Bellingham goes down, believing he was fouled by Rodri, but the referee gives nothing. There is contact but is it enough for a penalty? The referee had a good view and there is a decent shout for a penalty.

The referee is being sent to the screen so we know what that usually means...

Certainly no sitting on the lead from England at the start of the second half. Tuchel was adamant that Bellingham should have been awarded a penalty after going down in the area.

And Tuchel might get his way as VAR have sent referee Davide Massa to the screen.

England want a penalty. Saka goes down under a challenge from Laporte from behind but those appeals are waved away. VAR checks and clears the incident. Laporte got the ball.

Chance for England. Bellingham’s cross from the left picks out Quansah in the centre of the box but the defender’s header from eight yards out misses the target. What an opportunity that was for Quansah to score his first international goal.

Spain are unbeaten in nearly 40 competitive matches and, as it stands, that run is set to come to an end. Still a long way to come though tonight and Spain could have been 3-0 up before England even scored one goal.

We are back under way at Wembley. No changes for either side at the break.

During half-time, Kyle Walker received a framed shirt to celebrate his 96 England caps.

What a response from our #ThreeLions! 💪 pic.twitter.com/qBoY0J79JL

2 - Lamine Yamal has scored the third quickest goal England have ever conceded at Wembley Stadium, behind only first minute goals for Scotland in 1957 and Hungary in 1953.Punch. pic.twitter.com/NxVp1qOnVi

Possession: England 45%-55% SpainShots: 6-8Shots on target: 2-2Corners: 3-3Touches in opposition box: 10-10

Tuchel will be delighted with the half-time score and England’s spirit after going behind so early. But how on earth have Spain only scored once? They’ve missed a couple of one-on-ones, hit the post and blazed over the bar. Highly entertaining and England will know they will have to defend better if they are going to hold on to their lead.

An absorbing and end-to-end first half is brought to an end. Somehow, despite the fact at one point they could have been 3-0 down, England lead 2-1 at the break.

Cucurella’s cross from the left loops all the way to the back post, where it strikes the frame of the goal. I do not think Cucurella meant that.

It is chances galore at both ends, with the latest falling to Ruiz, whose shot from the edge of the box is deflected wide for a corner. Bellingham heads away at the front post.

England gift the ball away so poorly and Yamal should punish them with his second goal of the game but he blazes high over the bar.

What on earth has happened to Spain? O’Reilly’s cross from the byline picks out Kane, who guides a header towards goal. Cucurella makes an absolute mess of things, effectively kneeing the ball past his keeper and into his own net. Kane will try and claim it but surely that has to go down as an own goal. 10 minutes ago, Spain should have been 3-0 up. Now, England are 2-1 ahead.

I think we'll give that goal to Harry Kane 🎯England come from behind to lead Spain thanks Harry Kane, with assistance from Marc Cucurella ⚽️#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/X3qSOWUhVT

England are inches away from taking the lead. Saka drives forward towards the Spain box and lays it across to Kane, whose shot goes just wide. Should Kane have scored? Maybe.

SO CLOSE FROM KANE! 🫣England nearly go in front 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/YgoRblxuiH

Somehow, England are on level terms. Spain should have been 3-0 up but England equalise with a clinical counter-attack. Anderson wins the ball back for England on the edge of their own box and plays it forward to Gordon, who flicks it brilliantly first time into the path of Bellingham, who drives into the Spain half. Gordon is on his bike and is ready to receive the forward pass from Bellingham. Gordon takes it to the Spain box before slotting home clinically past Simon.

ENGLAND ARE LEVEL! 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿A brilliant finish from Anthony Gordon after a breathtaking counter attack 👏#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/z0nSfWIHVd

England have missed Declan Rice’s delivery so far this evening. Saka has floated a couple of corners straight into the hands of Spain goalkeeper Simon and there have been some promising free-kicks wasted too.

No love lost between the Real Madrid team-mates Jude Bellingham and Marc Cucurella, there. Bellingham was unhappy with a challenge from the left-back and let’s just say they exchanged words afterwards.

If Olmo had slotted that home, the assist from Yamal would have been quite incredible. A quite sensational flick from Yamal plays Olmo in behind on the right side of the box and the latter’s shot goes narrowly wide of the far post.

Saka’s shot is blocked and the ball spins behind for an England corner out on the right. Saka takes the corner he won but his inswinger is caught by Unai Simon.

England want a penalty. Lewis-Skelly goes down inside the Spain penalty area under a challenge from Cubarsi and his appeals are waved away. The referee was spot on with that call.

That is a second sitter missed of the half from Torres and Spain should be 3-0 up. Rodri times his through ball to perfection and Torres’ first touch is glorious to take him past Anderson and away. Torres is one-on-one with Trafford and should score but his effort slides by the left post. How Spain are not 3-0 up is beyond me.

Another let off for England 😧Ferran Torres misses another big chance one-on-one with James Trafford #ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/KFkJoJUW6c

That is a waste from Bellingham. The Real Madrid man is found by Quansah on the edge of the box and Bellingham should get his shot off quickly but dithers for too long. Bellingham then goes down far too softly, wanting a free-kick, but those appeals are rightly waved away.

England have enjoyed more of the possession thus far but are still yet to register a shot through 25 minutes.

The Spain fans are certainly enjoying their night in north London. In general, they have a lot to be happy about currently holding the World Cup and Euros trophies as well as the fact that their team is 1-0 up this evening.

That is a big save from Trafford and a big miss from Torres. Yamal plays a through ball to pick out the run of Torres, whom many in the ground think is offside. However, he was clearly being played onside by Quansah and Torres, who is fine scoring form this season for PSG, should score with a one-on-one opportunity but is denied by Trafford. England could and perhaps should be 2-0 down.

BIG SAVE from James Trafford 🧤The Leeds United goalkeeper keeps out Ferran Torres#ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/nj5b8AUSQU

Anderson plays a lovely switch from right to left to pick out Gordon in space. Gordon takes just one touch before getting it out of his feet quickly, curling a cross to the back post. He is looking for Saka but Cucurella just about deals with it, even though he did not know much about it. The ball appeared to come off Cucurella last but a goal-kick is given.

After a very shaky start, England are beginning to grow into the game, slowly, but it is gradually happening.

England are really not helping themselves at the moment, gifting the ball away in dangerous area. This time it is Lewis-Skelly who gives it away and Spain end up with a corner.

The delivery is drilled to the edge of the box, where Yamal’s powerful volley is blocked by Gordon.

Spain keep it alive and the ball comes back into the England box. Torres fires into the bottom corner but the offside flag goes up and replays show he was clearly offside.

The OFFSIDE Flag saves England's blushes 👀Ferran Torres saw his close range finish chalked off #ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/unIj6NsO7z

England have their first sight of the Spain goal. Kane plays Gordon in down the left and the latter gets past his man easily. He gets to the byline before crossing but Unai Simon in the Spain goal is on hand to cut it out.

What on earth are you doing Guehi? Spain take the lead inside two minutes and it is a real gift. Guehi should pass to O’Reilly or Gordon to his left but instead comes back towards his own goal, seemingly unaware that Yamal is right behind him. What then follows is a clinical finish from Yamal, who drives into the England box before curling towards the far corner, with the ball going in off the inside of the post. That will help Yamal’s pursuit of the Ballon d’Or. Dreadful from Guehi, fantastic from Yamal.

WHAT A START FROM SPAIN 🇪🇸Lamine Yamal pounces on a Marc Guéhi error to give Spain an early lead at Wembley #ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/Et83EyTPlp

Now Tuchel is out with his arms crossed after that nightmare start from England. The Spain fans are in good voice.

We are under way at Wembley. There is VAR in use.

Tuchel was not shown on the big screens ahead of kick-off. He’s just got up off his seat for the first time and entered his technical area to complain about something.

Before we get under way at Wembley, we stop to remember the great Kevin Keegan with a minute’s applause, with a wreath being laid down on the side of the pitch. England are also wearing black armbands to remember Keegan. Wembley also pays tribute to a few other England players who have died over recent months.

Here come the two sides and it is time for the national anthems. Marcha Real followed by God Save The King. There are plenty of Spanish supporters in attendance tonight and they are making their voices heard.

Here comes the Wonderwall compilation. Harry Kane said yesterday that he wants to win the Nations League next summer and then celebrate by going to one of the Oasis gigs.

Spain have been forced into a late alteration during the warm-ups and it comes at right-back, with Eric Garcia injured so Marc Pubill comes in.

I quite like Tuchel’s idea of giving Trafford the first two Nations League games, against Spain tonight and Czech Republic in Prague, and then going back to Pickford for the final two, in Croatia and against the Czechs at home. Harry Kane wants England to address how they lost their identity and went “against our beliefs” at the World Cup.

In a brutally honest assessment of the tournament, the England captain admitted Thomas Tuchel’s team did not play to their full potential in several games – even before the painful semi-final exit against Argentina.

Kane, who played golf instead of watching the World Cup final, revealed the 2-1 Atlanta defeat hurt more than missing a penalty four years earlier in Qatar, when England were knocked out by France in the quarter-finals.

“This one hurt more than any other one. I would probably say even more than when I missed a penalty in Qatar because of the manner that it happened,” Kane said. “It was not us as a team.

“We trust our players and the player know very well that if you miss a camp then someone plays well in your position that the competition is always on. You have to make sure to be available and to produce top-level performances in camp and if you do so, that counts for something. Right now, it is not on my list of worries. I am not wired like this. From the moment I arrived at SGP my full focus is 100 per cent with the players who are here.

“There is no threat, distrust or threat of consequences. It will come naturally. I truly believe that we have the opposite. You will talk to our captain, Harry Kane, who has the most minutes for club and country and is happy to be here while teammates of his are enjoying a 10-day break. He is the role model and that is the vibe we have here.”

Most of Spain’s winners from that evening are playing here at Wembley. Dani Carvajal, Robin Le Normand and Alvaro Morata are those who are not playing from that team.

James Trafford is poised to start for England ahead of Jordan Pickford against Spain tonight.

Pickford has been England’s No1 for eight years but Thomas Tuchel is set to make a change to face the world champions in the Nations League opener at Wembley.

Trafford went to the World Cup in the summer and has started the Premier League in good form following his move to Leeds.

In the first match since the World Cup, changing his goalkeeper is a major selection decision from Tuchel.

Elsewhere, Jarell Quansah is set to play at right-back ahead of Trent Alexander-Arnold while Myles Lewis-Skelly is also in line to return to the starting XI after being recalled into the squad after missing the World Cup.

England begin their Nations League campaign with a home game against the world champions Spain. This is England’s first game since the World Cup, with their dreams of glory ended by Argentina in the semi-finals, but they did finish third after beating France in a high-scoring third/fourth play-off. The last meeting between these sides saw Spain beat England to win Euro 2024. They also faced off in the Nations League back in 2018, with Spain winning at Wembley and England taking victory over in Spain.

England’s plans for these games has been disrupted by a number of withdrawals. Cole Palmer had earned a recall having been left out of the World Cup squad but the Chelsea forward has withdrawn due to a minor injury, despite playing the full game for Chelsea against Brentford in the final game before the international beak.

“He [Palmer] plays with discomfort and pain and cannot play on the highest level with discomfort and pain,” Tuchel said. “Chelsea informed us. That is my understanding. We are not managing load. This is not an ‘international break’. It is a competitive environment, where the players love to train and be together. That is what we created. We will never compromise on that. We will never let this feeling creep in that the players do not want to come [to England camps]. We focus on the guys who absolutely want to play for England.

“For sure it is a missed opportunity. It is another missed opportunity. He misses too many opportunities. I do not blame him for it, it is just a fact. He misses way too many camps with injuries. I only want to rely on what I personally witness and see within my team. For that you have to be in camp. If you are not in camp there is a next level to impress that you cannot achieve because you can only do it with me on the pitch and with us on the pitch. It is a missed opportunity.”

Declan Rice has also withdrawn from the squad despite playing the full game in Arsenal’s defeat to Brighton as have Kobbie Mainoo, Marcus Rashford and Tino Livramento. Morgan Gibbs-White and James Garner have been called up as a result.

Trent Alexander-Arnold is back in the fold for the first time since June 2025. 18-year-old Liverpool winger Rio Ngumoha made his England debut against New Zealand during the World Cup warm-ups and takes his place in this squad, although he does make the matchday squad for tonight’s game. England will also take on Czechia, Croatia and then Cezchia again during this international break.

Having been crowned world champions back in July, Spain are now champions of both Europe and the world. Back in June 2025, Spain made the Nations League final but lost on penalties to Portugal. Ahead of this international window, The Royal Spanish Federation has extended Luis de la Fuente’s contract until 2032. After tonight, Spain will host Croatia and Czechia before travelling to Croatia to cap off this international window.

This is an extended international break, with four games to take place during this window. Team news from Wembley to follow shortly.

#1489. Arsenal, Liverpool, Chelsea Chase £100m England Midfielder

Arsenal, Liverpool and Chelsea have all contacted Bournemouth about England midfielder Alex Scott, according to CaughtOffside, which cites The i Paper. Liverpool and Chelsea want to move in January, while Arsenal would rather wait until next summer. Bournemouth’s stance on selling the 23-year-old has softened, but the reported asking price is above £100m, and Scott turned down two contract offers over the summer.

The interest has clear reasons behind it. Andoni Iraola coached Scott at Bournemouth before taking over at Anfield in June, and Liverpool want to reunite them. Chelsea lost Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City in a £125m deadline-day deal and had a reported £64m bid for Scott rejected earlier in the summer. Arsenal already have Declan Rice, Bruno Guimaraes, Martin Zubimendi and Myles Lewis-Skelly, so CaughtOffside sees Chelsea or Liverpool as the more logical destinations for his playing time.

Scott wins the ball, presses and carries it through midfield, and he started Bournemouth’s first five league games this season before a quadriceps injury on England duty in October kept him out for weeks. Fitness is the first concern, because knee problems have interrupted much of his time on the south coast. End product is the second. He has scored five league goals in 85 appearances since joining in 2023, so he will not solve a shortage of chances alone.

Not at £100m, and not as a January priority. Liverpool rank 18th for big chances after ten league games, according to This Is Anfield, and Scott offers energy rather than creativity. The real gap sits beside Ryan Gravenberch, where Curtis Jones left in the summer, and nobody arrived to share the defensive work.

Scott could be the aggressive partner in Iraola’s double pivot, freeing Dominik Szoboszlai and Florian Wirtz to play higher, yet that is a heavy fee for a player only just rebuilding match fitness, with Liverpool fourth and nine points behind Arsenal.

Chelsea’s case is simpler. The division’s biggest summer spenders lost their midfield engine and can justify the price more easily. Arsenal’s patience makes sense, since Rice, Guimaraes and Zubimendi leave no room for a £100m squad player. A Liverpool bid would only inflate the market Chelsea are already shaping. If Iraola wants a January signing, a specialist holding midfielder for far less money does more for the top-four push.

#1488. Liverpool Transfer News: Dutch Star’s Agent Tests Market

Liverpool transfer news: Ryan Gravenberch’s agent, José Fortes Rodriguez, is exploring ways to take his client out of Anfield, according to CaughtOffside. The site relays a claim from the X account @ITKSpace that Fortes has held “loose but direct contact” with several European clubs, none of them named. No formal exit request has been lodged, and the 24-year-old could still stay, so this reads like a camp checking the market rather than a player pushing to leave.

Liverpool hold the stronger hand. His six-year extension, signed in March, runs to 2032, so any buyer would face a substantial asking price. Real Madrid have been linked before, though nothing here says they are interested now.

Iraola’s 4-2-3-1 relies on two central midfielders, and Gravenberch, so commanding at the base of Arne Slot’s title-winning side, has struggled to settle. Iraola benched him for three straight games at one stage, he collected a second yellow card in the 3-0 home defeat by Manchester City on 11 October, and a heel problem has since kept him out of the Arsenal and Fenerbahçe games. He has no goals and one assist in the league this term.

His strengths are clear. At 6ft 3in he carries the ball through pressure and starts attacks from deep. Defending space and tracking runners is the weakness, and it shows when his partner also surges forward.

No, not this winter and not at a price set by his worst few weeks. Gravenberch is 24, tied down until 2032, and his market value has slipped sharply since last December, so selling now would hand a buyer the bargain that March contract was meant to rule out.

The real problem sits elsewhere. Iraola received no new midfielder in the summer, and his double pivot has no natural holding player. Gravenberch has admitted he prefers the number eight role, yet Mac Allister and Szoboszlai, who started the 3-1 win at Crystal Palace that lifted Liverpool to fourth, already occupy those spots. Nineteen-year-old Trey Nyoni has mostly played the deeper role this season.

Keep him through January, get him fit, and judge him again in a settled pairing. If Liverpool then sign a proper holding midfielder next summer, Gravenberch becomes a surplus eight, and a big-club bid at the right figure would deserve a hearing. Selling before that signing arrives just removes the one midfielder who can still carry the ball out of pressure.

#1486. Villa Midfielder Has £80m Price Tag For Arsenal: Is He Worth It?

Arsenal transfer news: Aston Villa do not regard Boubacar Kamara as available, even with Arsenal interested, according to CaughtOffside. The report says an offer of around £80m could change that stance, although Villa negotiate from strength because the 26-year-old’s contract runs until 2030.

January looks highly unlikely. Villa have already lost Amadou Onana to a torn ACL suffered at the World Cup, and the Belgian is not expected back until around April. Unai Emery cannot lose a second holding midfielder in the middle of a season. The summer is different. CaughtOffside says Villa could entertain a significant bid then, provided they can reinvest the money in a proper replacement and strengthen the squad around him.

TBR Football reported in July 2025 that he sat on Arsenal’s long list of midfield targets, and his numbers explain why. Kamara has started all 10 of his Premier League games this season, completing 86.3% of his passes, including 83 line-breaking balls, while making 28 tackles and 40 recoveries. He wins 56% of his duels and can play at centre-back, which would give Mikel Arteta cover in two positions.

The weaknesses are just as clear. He has no goals this season, only three shots and an xG of 0.14, and he has committed 20 fouls and conceded a penalty. He also missed the closing weeks of 2024/25 through injury.

The role he would play is obvious: a ball-playing six next to Declan Rice. Martín Zubimendi occupies it now, and Arsenal lead the league with 27 points from 10 games, six clear of Manchester City, with seven clean sheets.

No, not at that price. Arsenal spent £75m on Bruno Guimarães in August, and Arteta still has Rice, Zubimendi, Mikel Merino, Martin Ødegaard and Myles Lewis-Skelly competing for the same central spaces.

FotMob values him at €49m, roughly £43m, so Villa would be asking close to double his market value for a player who turns 27 this month and offers little in the final third. Villa’s insistence on reinvesting the fee also hands them the leverage, which means Arsenal would pay a premium on a seller’s timetable.

The only sensible trigger is a departure, perhaps Zubimendi or the 30-year-old Merino, leaving Arsenal short of a proven Premier League six. Kamara is a better holding midfielder than most of the market, but a title-leading side already has that job covered, and £80m would buy cover rather than improvement.

#1485. Derek McInnes urges his Rangers side to stop switching off after edging out Aberdeen in thriller

Published: 18:37 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 18:42 EST, 24 November 2026

Derek McInnes last night hit out at his dozy Rangers side for switching off in the latter stages of a hard-fought 3-2 home win over Aberdeen and warned them they will be made to pay over the course of the season if they carry on being so naive.

Goals from Ryan Naderi, Djeidi Gassama and Raskin in the first ten minutes of the second half put the Ibrox outfit in total command after Brad Lyons had put the visitors a goal up at the break.

However, Findlay Marshall made it a nervy finish for Rangers after scoring for the Dons on 58 minutes and it took a brilliant save from keeper Ivor Pandur to deny Nicky Devlin before Rangers saw it out to take their unbeaten run to 14 games and close the gap on Celtic at the head of the Premiership to just one point.

‘I am relieved to win,’ said manager McInnes, who made three changes and altered the shape at the interval. ‘I thought we only played with the intelligence, speed and intensity for about 20 minutes and, in that period, showed how good we can be.

‘But we put the game at risk. We lost a cheap goal and weren’t aggressive enough. We lost two goals, really, from set-plays.

‘At 3-1 up against a team as game as Aberdeen were — and they were really good value — our naivety for the second goal is beyond me.

Rangers boss Derek McInnes was relieved to win but urges his side to keep focused

Nicolas Raskin slots home the third goal for Rangers in their thrilling 3-2 win over Aberdeen

‘I am not sure it was a free-kick in the first place, but we turn our backs. It is almost as if we are in a daydream and we allow them to manipulate the ball. Great finish from wee Findlay Marshall, but we put ourselves in the mire there by just knocking off.

‘We were so naive at times in the game. We scored good goals at good times but I still think Aberdeen will be disappointed not to get something.

‘We should have stayed in charge of the game and the second goal we lose allows Aberdeen to keep going with a bit of oxygen and carry a threat. I am disappointed with the lack of control in the game and I am not really happy with a lot of what we saw.

‘That has to change because we will not always be able to outscore the opposition.

‘We hit Aberdeen like a train in the second half and they found themselves 3-1 down because of the quality and intelligence of our play. For whatever reason, we then started playing back the way again. We played more passbacks to my goalkeeper than I can remember in a long time.

‘We need to play forward and show more control in the game. I am looking for better from my team.’

Raskin, meanwhile, has urged his Rangers team-mates to blast themselves to the top of the table on Saturday night and really pile the pressure on arch-rivals Celtic.

The Light Blues play host to third-placed Falkirk on Saturday afternoon with Celtic going to Hearts the following day and the Belgian midfielder wants to make sure they don’t let the defending champions off the hook the way they have in previous years.

‘We need to keep it going,’ said Raskin. ‘In recent years, we have not been able to put enough pressure on the other team and now we are doing it, so that is good.

‘We will see how everybody reacts after next Saturday.’

Djeidi Gassama scored to complete a stunning turaround for Rangers early in the second half

Raskin has also revealed it took a stern half-time team talk from manager McInnes along with those substitutions to spark his side into life after a dreadful first-half performance.

‘I think we made the game hard for ourselves in the first half,’ said the Belgian. ‘The manager had an honest discussion in the dressing room and we came back and scored two early goals, which helped. But we weren’t focused enough after the third goal and conceded to make it even harder.

‘We showed character again. The manager said what a manager has to say when you are losing, playing badly, you are 1-0 down and you have to win the game.’

Aberdeen boss Mario Frick left Ibrox feeling his side had missed a real opportunity.

‘I am disappointed with the five or six minutes after half-time. That hurts,’ he said.

‘We saw a good performance, Rangers were beatable tonight.

‘We need more time. We have to improve. We have to talk about those ten minutes. After 3-1 down, we came back and we believed in ourselves. We deserved an equaliser.’

#1483. Chelsea’s £43m Winger Gamble Is Stalling: Should They Accept A Discount?

Chelsea transfer news: Birmingham Live reports that Alejandro Garnacho’s future needs resolving, because the winger has not started a match for Aston Villa and a permanent move depends on certain conditions being met. Chelsea sent the 22-year-old to Villa Park on a season-long loan in July, with a reported £43m obligation to buy next summer. Neither club has revealed the trigger, and reports link it to appearances.

The numbers explain the concern. FotMob lists four Premier League outings, all from the bench, without a goal or assist, while Football365 counts only 95 minutes across seven substitute appearances. Football Insider claims Villa are prepared to back out of the deal if his form doesn’t improve.

Garnacho’s strengths haven’t changed. His pace, directness and willingness to take on defenders earned a £40m move from Manchester United in 2025. The weakness is end product, and it followed him to London with eight goals in 43 games for Chelsea, only one of them in 24 Premier League appearances. Unai Emery left him out of the squad for the Manchester United game.

Chelsea have no obvious use for him either. Xabi Alonso told him in July that regular football wasn’t guaranteed, and the 3-4-2-1 Alonso favours uses Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer behind João Pedro, with Pedro Neto and Estêvão competing for the wide roles.

FotMob values him at about €29m (roughly £25m), far below the €71m peak recorded in August 2024, and Manchester United are reportedly entitled to 10 per cent of any future fee. If the clause isn’t triggered, he returns in July 2027 on a contract running to 2032.

Yes, and soon. Chelsea built the deal to protect £43m, but the clause relies on appearances from a manager who isn’t picking him, so the price drops with every unused substitution. The sporting case for a return is thin. Alonso’s system asks wide players to defend as wing-backs, while Garnacho’s value lies in isolating a full-back, and the £117m Rogers signing already covers the left-sided attacking role.

A mid-£20m sale, even after United’s cut, would still return more than half of the £40m Chelsea paid and clear a contract running to 2032. Chelsea should open talks with Villa in January about a lower fixed fee, or line up other buyers for the summer. A clause that depends on a manager picking a player he has benched was never a safe way to protect £43m.

#1482. Man United sent new relegation warning by 36-goal midfielder before Brentford clash (exclusive)

By Ben Knapton | 28 Nov 2026 10:12

Manchester United must keep the threat of relegation from the Premier League "in the back of their mind" ahead of Saturday's clash with Brentford, Gordon Strachan has exclusively told Sports Mole.

Mauricio Pochettino seeks his first win as Red Devils head coach at the third attempt when Man Utd welcome the Bees to Old Trafford at 3pm, after defeat to Liverpool and a draw with Sporting Lisbon in his opening two fixtures.

Owing to last weekend's 4-0 horror show at Anfield, Man United enter gameweek 12 in a lowly 19th place in the Premier League table, three points below Ipswich Town in the relative safety of 17th.

After 11 matches of the 2025-26 season, Tottenham Hotspur had 18 points - 10 more than Man United's current total - and the Lilywhites only managed to avoid relegation on the last day of the season.

Ex-Man Utd midfielder Strachan has therefore warned the Red Devils that the prospect of an infamous demotion cannot be ignored, as he believes that few fans head to Man United matches expecting to watch a well-oiled machine at this moment.

"I think you have to keep that in the back of your mind," Strachan said. "If people make decisions, that's 10% of their mind, and the other 90% is, how do we get out of this?

"How do we get to a team that, whether you're a Man United supporter or someone at the top, you want to go along and watch them and think this is a good football team?

"At the moment, anybody who goes to Manchester United does not have that feeling that they're going along to watch a good, fit, organised football team.

"Every coach will say, I'm organised, I'm this, I'm that. You can be organised, but if you don't have physical fitness, mental strength and character, then it doesn't matter.

"It doesn't matter how long you put these players into positions where they should be if they don't have the mental and physical bravery to carry out these instructions, and you don't have the confidence when you get the ball back. How do you score goals without that?"

Man United currently hold the honour of being one of six ever-present Premier League clubs who have never been relegated, alongside Spurs, Everton, Arsenal, Liverpool and Chelsea.

It has now been over 50 years since the Red Devils dropped down from the first tier, as they were last relegated back in the 1973-74 season following the departure of several household names.

Denis Law and Bobby Charlton were no longer representing the club, while the legendary George Best only made fleeting appearances as Man United finished 21st in the 22-team table.

However, the Red Devils spent just one season in the Second Division, earning promotion back to the top flight at the first attempt by winning the title with 61 points from 42 games.

Strachan joined Man United in 1984 - 11 years after their demotion - and scored 36 goals in 198 games for the Red Devils as a midfielder, winning one FA Cup in the process.

Gordon Strachan was speaking to Sports Mole on behalf of William Hill Football Odds.

#1481. Liverpool Open Talks With Argentine Midfielder: Is He Worth A New Deal?

Liverpool transfer news: Liverpool have opened contract talks with Alexis Mac Allister, according to @tribuna_ftbl, with his current deal running until June 2028. The report arrives days after his father, Carlos, told ESPN that no discussions had started, although he hinted at news before the end of the year.

It also reverses the summer, when the club extended Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai but made no offer to the 27-year-old, something Mac Allister revealed in September while admitting he had stayed despite chances to leave.

His form explains the change. After a poor 2025/26 under Arne Slot, he has become Andoni Iraola’s first-choice midfielder alongside Szoboszlai, pushing Gravenberch to the bench. He has scored once in the Premier League and three times in the Champions League, including the winner against Atlético Madrid, and holds a 7.29 FotMob average rating across 758 league minutes. Liverpool sit fourth.

FotMob places him in the 88th percentile among midfielders for shot attempts, and he has said the man-to-man system suits him because it demands less communication than Slot’s approach. His weaknesses are just as clear.

His defensive contributions (45th percentile) and aerial duels (46th) sit below the midfield average, and pundit David Lynch has questioned whether his legs have gone in Iraola’s 4-4-2, where two central midfielders cover huge areas. He has also collected four league yellow cards already.

Yes, but not on the terms his summer rebound might demand. Ten league games of good form do not cancel a season in which he looked off the pace, so Liverpool should offer around three years, with wages pitched below the bumper deals Gravenberch and Szoboszlai signed.

The timing still makes sense. With 18 months left, he enters the final year next summer, when Liverpool would face either a discounted sale or a free departure. His FotMob valuation of €66m has almost halved from the €130m peak of September 2025, so selling now would lock in the lowest price.

Iraola also needs a controller to sit beside Szoboszlai’s runs, and no one in the squad does that better. The caveat is that Mac Allister turns 28 next month, so Liverpool must pair him with a quicker partner next summer rather than treat his renewal as the end of the midfield rebuild.

Canton says the 24-year-old Germany international is certainly appreciated at the Emirates.

The ranking reflects an awkward summer for Mikel Arteta. Arsenal sold Leandro Trossard and Gabriel Martinelli, missed out on Vinicius Junior and signed only Christos Tzolis for about £34m.

Tzolis started the first five league games, then suffered a hamstring injury on international duty. Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke have covered since, and Madueke rescued a point in Saturday’s 2-2 draw at Newcastle, which left Arsenal six points clear for now.

Nusa, the 21-year-old Norwegian winger, has six goals and eight assists in 15 matches for Leipzig. Sky Sports reports that the Bundesliga club won’t sell him in January, so a summer deal looks more realistic, with Leipzig reportedly valuing him between £60m and £77m. Schade is the quicker route, but Arsenal asked about him in the summer and got nowhere, according to TEAMtalk. His contract runs until 2028.

Schade has scored three times in ten Premier League appearances from 2.44 expected goals, and his pace suits a side that already creates through Tzolis. He can play either flank or centrally. The weaknesses show elsewhere: no assists, three chances created in 781 minutes, seven completed dribbles at a 25% success rate and 43.8% of duels won. FotMob values him at about £47m.

Not in January, and certainly not as a consolation. Arsenal lead the league, Tzolis remains the first-choice left winger, and Madueke has just shown he can deliver there. Schade would add depth, but he wouldn’t add what Arteta lacks: a winger who beats his man and drags two defenders with him against low blocks.

Nusa builds his game on exactly that, and his output at Leipzig now justifies waiting until next summer. Schade’s returns suggest he would sit behind a fit Tzolis, which is hard to justify at a price Brentford would set after already refusing an approach.

A bid becomes sensible only if Tzolis breaks down again or Leipzig block Nusa completely, because Schade needs no time to adapt to the Premier League. Even then, anything above £50m would pay for potential rather than production, and a 25% dribble success rate tells Arsenal he isn’t the specialist they need.

#1479. Alguacil reveals conviction regarding how Olympiacos could have beaten Milan

Olympiacos head coach Imanol Alguacil believes that his side would have beaten AC Milan had they hung on a bit longer before conceding.

Everything was going according to plan for the Greek side when Lorenzo Pirola’s header hit the bar then Mike Maignan and nestled in to put them a goal up, before Jota Silva fired in a second following Koni De Winter’s stray pass out from the back.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

With Milan’s Europa League hopes in need of revival, Omari Hutchinson stepped up with a masterclass. He gave Ruben Amorim’s side hope with a fine individual effort, then he set up Alphadjo Cisse for the equaliser and Christian Pulisic for the go-ahead goal, before Diego Moreira sealed it.

It was therefore a bittersweet night for Alguacil, one in which his side showed they can dominate one of the big names in the competition, but ultimately emerging empty-handed. He analysed the game in a post-match press conference which MilanNews attended.

The team showed what they could do for 60 minutes. How can you explain what happened?

“At a key moment in the match, we went from a possible 3-0 lead to 2-1, and our confidence crumbled. Milan reacted well: they’re stronger, they have experience, they’re a historic team, and if you’re not focused, you risk losing, as happened.

“Milan gave it their all, but until the 60th minute, we played a great match, like a Champions League team.”

Are you satisfied with the defence’s performance? Is this formation likely to continue going forward?

“I don’t know. A coach has to find solutions, especially because it depends on how we recover our players. We have some out, others played today, and we’ll see the consequences.

“We’ll see who I have available, also thinking about the next match, but Olympiacos, despite the change in formation, played very well.

“We played well, took the lead, deserved the 3-0, and I’m convinced that if we had held on to a 2-0 lead for a few more minutes, we would have won. The 2-4 scoreline seems unfair to me.”

Five players out, but the team still proved to be strong. Is there a chance you can directly advance to the last 16 and go deeper?

“I don’t know where the limit is, I don’t have a definitive answer. I’ll try to get the most out of the team. The lads are training hard, and it’s unfair to have conceded these four goals. In the end, we lacked energy. Milan are a Champions League team, very technical, but I’ll hold on to these 65 minutes.

“We played better than Milan, and I’ll try to make it impossible to play this hour of play again in the next games. By doing so, it will be easier for us to win.”

#1478. Arsenal face £84m Antonio Nusa transfer dilemma as RB Leipzig's January stance emerges

By Naim Beneddra | 28 Nov 2026 11:31

Arsenal could be forced to spend in excess of £84m to sign Antonio Nusa in January, with RB Leipzig reportedly reluctant to part ways with the Norway international midway through the season.

The Gunners are understood to be monitoring the 21-year-old as part of their plans to strengthen Mikel Arteta's attacking options in 2027, while Paris Saint-Germain have also been linked with the winger.

However, Leipzig's determination to retain one of their most influential players could make a summer transfer considerably more attractive from a financial perspective.

According to Sky Sport Germany journalist Philipp Hinze, Leipzig are under no pressure to sell Nusa in January and would only consider offers exceeding €100m (£84m).

"Different story next summer," Hinze added on X, suggesting that the Bundesliga outfit could adopt a more flexible stance at the end of the campaign.

Leipzig signed Nusa from Club Brugge for approximately £18m in 2024, and with the Norwegian under contract until 2029, the German club are in a strong negotiating position.

Arsenal have been linked with reinforcements on the left flank following the departures of Gabriel Martinelli and Leandro Trossard, with Christos Tzolis arriving during the summer to bolster Arteta's attacking department.

PSG's circumstances could make a January move more appealing to the French champions, given that Luis Enrique has lost both Desire Doue and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia to long-term injuries.

Arsenal, on the other hand, may find greater financial value in waiting until the summer, although Nusa's continued development could attract further competition for his signature.

Nusa's performances this season go some way towards explaining Leipzig's reluctance to sanction a mid-season departure. The winger has registered nine goals and eight assists in 17 appearances across all competitions, already surpassing his combined tally from the entirety of last season by eight.

His five goals and seven assists in the Bundesliga also put him level with Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane as the division's leading contributor to goals after 10 rounds of fixtures.

Nusa has demonstrated his ability to influence matches at Champions League level, scoring against Manchester City earlier this month before netting twice in Leipzig's 3-1 victory over Lens on Tuesday.

"I've been working hard on my finishing in training and want to help the team with my goals," the winger told the Bundesliga's official website following that victory.

The Norwegian's direct running and ability to beat defenders in one-on-one situations would give Arteta another means of breaking down deep defensive blocks, while his improving end product makes him an increasingly attractive long-term investment.

However, Arsenal would be paying a considerable premium for a player who is still in the process of establishing himself among Europe's leading wingers.

Previous reports had suggested that Nusa could cost the Gunners in the region of £67m. Leipzig's latest reported demands would represent a substantial increase on that figure.

With Arsenal competing for the Premier League title and looking to go one better in the Champions League after last season's final defeat, much will depend on whether Arteta considers another wide attacker essential to his ambitions for the second half of the campaign.
