#1477. Alonso ready to sell £47m Chelsea signing for a Barca star

Chelsea transfer news: Xabi Alonso wants Barcelona right-back Jules Koundé at Chelsea and is ready to sell Marco Palestra, his £47m summer signing, to make room, according to El Nacional. The outlet says Alonso has pushed the case, a claim it credits to FourFourTwo, and that Palestra has Serie A interest from Juventus, AC Milan and Napoli, though it mentions no bid.

Barcelona would reportedly listen to offers of around €50m, roughly £43m, because Hansi Flick doesn’t treat Koundé as untouchable. The 28-year-old has started three of six LaLiga games this season after an ankle sprain on 17 October kept him out for over a month. El Nacional calls him a backup behind Eric García and says he’d welcome the move.

Koundé completes 93.9% of his passes, wins 58.8% of his duels and has 58 France caps, a composed defender who could play right-back or on the right of a back three. His body is the worry: a hamstring problem in March, then an ankle injury that lingered.

Palestra won Serie A’s Defender of the Year award at Cagliari, and his 81 completed dribbles topped every defender in Europe’s top five leagues. A thigh injury delayed his Chelsea debut until October, and El Nacional puts him at 202 minutes across six matches. Alonso prefers Josh Acheampong at right-back and, per BBC Sport, uses Palestra from the bench before Malo Gusto. He scored once in 37 league games, and his crossing remains modest.

Not as a swap. Palestra is a wing-back who beats opponents on the outside, while Koundé is a passer and cover defender best placed on the right of three centre-backs. Selling one doesn’t remove the need for the other, and Chelsea’s real shortage is right-sided cover: Reece James is injured and has been used in midfield, and Acheampong, a centre-back by trade, is filling in at right-back.

Koundé would solve that, but Gusto is the sale to make. He has lost his place, is reportedly open to a January exit, and Chelsea priced him at £75m in June, so even a discounted fee would cover much of Koundé’s £43m.

Selling Palestra after 202 minutes would mean writing off a player Alonso recruited and said needs time to adapt, to buy a 28-year-old with a muscle-injury record. Chelsea were fifth, 11 points behind Arsenal, before Leeds visited, without European football. Buy Koundé if the medical is clean, sell Gusto and keep Palestra.

#1476. Liverpool track Swedish left-back with £38m price tag

Liverpool transfer news: Liverpool are tracking Borussia Dortmund left-back Daniel Svensson, according to fussball-news.de, which names them and Arsenal as the most interested clubs.

Manchester United, Leeds, Milan, Juventus, Inter and Real Madrid are also watching the 24-year-old. Liverpool and Milan are reportedly preparing concrete steps for the winter window, although the report attributes no bid to either.

Dortmund will not make it easy. They want to keep a player contracted until June 2029 and plan to raise his salary, while Svensson feels settled and has no wish for a rushed move. A sale would cost at least €45m (about £38m), and Premier League clubs are ready to test Dortmund with a €30m (roughly £25m) offer, yet FotMob values him at just €23m.

The numbers explain the interest. Svensson has started all 10 Bundesliga games this season. His expected assists total of 1.13 comes without a single assist, and he has made 22 tackles, 14 interceptions and 45 recoveries while passing at 86.1%. He can play in midfield.

The flaws are clear. He has won only eight of 29 aerial duels and landed six of 32 crosses. He also plays as a wing-back in front of a back three, so Andoni Iraola’s back four would ask him to defend more of the flank alone.

Iraola’s 4-2-3-1 sends full-backs forward, and Milos Kerkez, bought for a reported £40m last year, has no goals or assists in the Premier League this season. Kostas Tsimikas, 30, is the backup on a contract that expires next year.

Not in January, and not at €45m. A €30m offer would fail, and £38m for a player FotMob values at €23m is poor business. Summer 2027 is the realistic window, once Tsimikas’s deal has run down.

The bigger problem sits on the other flank. Ronald Araujo, a centre-back by trade, is filling in at right-back while injuries have hit that position all season, so Iraola needs a natural right-back more urgently than a second left-back. Kerkez is 22 and signed until 2030, so Svensson would challenge him rather than replace him, which is healthy given Kerkez’s lack of end product.

Kerkez arrived with two Premier League seasons behind him, while Svensson would have to adapt to a new league and a new system. Liverpool should buy a right-back first and hold a ceiling of around £35m for Svensson, because above that they would repeat the Kerkez gamble with less evidence.

He spoke to the midfielder as soon as the story broke and didn’t think McKennie had hinted at wanting to leave, calling his comments a general remark. #1473. Tottenham join race for Inter midfielder facing pay cut: Right move for Spurs?

Tottenham transfer news: Tottenham Hotspur are one of four clubs tracking Hakan Calhanoglu, according to Tuttomercatoweb. The Italian outlet lists Galatasaray, Juventus and Como alongside Spurs, although it gives no detail on how far Tottenham’s interest has progressed.

The timing matters because the Inter midfielder’s contract expires on 30 June 2027, which lets him agree a pre-contract with a foreign club from January. Inter want to extend but are trimming wages for their over-30s. Calhanoglu earns roughly £5.7m a year, and Inter are discussing £4.4m plus bonuses. He prefers to stay but hopes to avoid a heavy cut, and no formal offer exists yet.

Calhanoglu turns 33 in February. FotMob shows three goals in 485 minutes from nine Serie A appearances, 91.4% pass accuracy, 20 chances created and a 98th-percentile ranking for shot attempts among Serie A central midfielders.

Passing range, long-distance shooting and dead-ball quality remain his strengths. He wins only 44.4% of his duels, though, completes a quarter of his dribbles, and his recovery speed will keep dropping with age. FotMob values him at about £6.4m, down from a £39m peak in 2024.

Roberto De Zerbi wants his midfield to dictate play from deep, which suits Calhanoglu’s skills. Spurs have 15 points from 11 league games after beating Ipswich 2-0 on Saturday, their fourth win in five. Yet Sandro Tonali (£100m) and Mateus Fernandes (£85m) joined in July, and Rodrigo Bentancur, Conor Gallagher and Archie Gray compete for the same places.

Not as a priority. Money isn’t the obstacle. Tonali reportedly earns more than £275,000 a week, so Calhanoglu’s wages would barely register, and a free transfer costs no fee. Squad space is the problem. Spurs bought Tonali and Fernandes to run De Zerbi’s base for years, and a 33-year-old in the same role would either sit on the bench or take minutes from Gray and Lucas Bergvall, whom the club needs to develop.

Spurs would also struggle to sell the project without European football, while Galatasaray can reportedly offer higher wages. The case only strengthens if Tonali or Bentancur leaves, or if De Zerbi wants a penalty and set-piece specialist. Neither applies now, and nothing forces Spurs to act in January.

Calhanoglu’s output is real, but it comes with a decline in athleticism that a 33-year-old can’t reverse. Spurs would be paying for a short-term fix in a position where they have already invested £185m in the long-term answer.

#1471. RANGERS 3 ABERDEEN 2: Amid all the thrills and spills, McInnes' triple switch sparks second-half revival

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 18:40 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 18:50 EST, 24 November 2026

When these sides last met in the league at the end of August, Rangers were in such a dark place that you wondered if their season was already destined to be another thoroughly miserable episode.

Coming just three days after going out of Europe — for the second time — to an ordinary Jablonec team, the slender win Derek McInnes’ side claimed at Pittodrie that day felt like a can being kicked down the road.

In those early weeks, the players looked lost. The manager admitted that he didn’t know what style of football he was watching. The supporters were preparing for a long, hard winter.

It’s remarkable what can come from one scruffy win on the road. From that point to this, McInnes’ men have now gone 14 games unbeaten in all competitions.

They have the League Cup final to look forward to next month. They are now just one point behind Celtic in the Premiership and look eminently capable of putting in a serious challenge for the title. In keeping with so many performances throughout this run, however, this wasn’t particularly convincing. Flat and rudderless for 45 minutes, Rangers were deservedly a goal behind at the interval.

Credit where it’s due, though. Their response at the outset of the second period was outstanding with three goals coming in 11 minutes courtesy of Ryan Naderi, Djeidi Gassama and Nico Raskin.

That ought to have been the platform for many more to follow. But the performance slipped back a level. Aberdeen scored once and could easily have scored again.

Raskin (right) and Gassama celebrate after combining to put Rangers 3-1 up

Naderi capitalises on Muller's mishandling to fire Rangers level at the start of the second half

It was a truly thrilling match, full of slip-ups, incidents and moments of brilliance. The final stages were a tough watch for the home fans who hoped against hope that they’d see their side ease towards a routine victory.

As at Fir Park on Saturday, though, Rangers found a way and added another win to the ledger. And provided that remains the case in the coming weeks and months, none of the light blue legions will be complaining.

Despite ultimately not having quite enough to take something, Aberdeen manager Mario Frick will have been encouraged by much of what he saw here.

Had it not been for that atrocious spell at the outset of the second period, he’d have fancied his men to take something.

They certainly fashioned plenty of opportunities. It was the defensive side of the game which ultimately cost them.

McInnes drafted in Kevin Kelsy, James Penrice and Ben Godfrey with Dujon Sterling, Tuur Rommens and Kim Minsu dropping out. There was a change of shape too, with a switch to a 3-5-2. For the longest time, it did not work.

Lyons gets his head to Marshall's corner to put Aberdeen in front in the first half

While Frick kept faith with the diamond-shaped midfield which served him so well in Ayrshire, he made three changes. In came Ayoub Mouloua, Afeez Aremu and Findlay Marshall at the expense of Hicham Mahou, Ante Palaversa and Stuart Armstrong.

Before the game, there was a minute’s silence in memory of the late, great Ralph Brand. What a pity a couple of clowns in the visiting section were unable to keep their mouths shut for that long.

Rangers started brightly with Penrice’s delivery from the left causing chaos. Dan Neil had a stab at it, then Naderi. Aberdeen survived.

Once Frick’s side settled, Nicky Devlin’s cross was met by Marshall. His header was straight at Ivor Pandur.

Rangers’ general play was broken, their build-up more ponderous than patient. Gassama did manage to drop a shoulder and get a strike away but Aremu’s positioning ensured Marius Muller was untroubled.

Naderi was again Rangers’ most effective player, although the bar was set pretty low initially. The Czech’s lay-off invited Godfrey to let fly. His strike was well off target.

While Gassama got into plenty of promising positions, his crossing continually let him down early on. On the other flank, Badredine Bouanani could not do right for doing wrong.

When the ball broke kindly to Naderi on the edge of the box, Ibrox expected the net to bulge. This time the man of the moment fired over. Rangers’ efforts in the first half were summed up by Naderi being tripped by Gavin Molloy on the edge of the box. Bouanani’s effort from the free-kick was woeful.

Aberdeen were aggressive and organised. And when the moment arose, they went forward in numbers.

McInnes shows his delight after his half-time changes helped turn the game around

They edged in front on the half hour after Marshall won a corner which was a consequence of Frick’s men being prepared to back themselves.

Marshall curled the set-piece deep to the far post. Brad Lyons seemed to be invisible to those in light blue as he made a late run. Olwethu Makhanya belatedly reacted but it was too late.

Lyons got enough on his header to beat Pandur and force Raskin to make the block behind his keeper.

The minute the scoreboard indicated that VAR were checking for a goal, you suspected the Belgian hadn’t done quite enough to keep it out. After a lengthy delay came confirmation of that fact.

How would Rangers respond up until the break? Not terribly well. Lyons’ crude foul on Gassama gave Bouanani a chance to make amends with a set-piece. This one smashed into the wall. Seconds later, the winger fired well over the top when he ought to have done better.

The Dons could easily have doubled their advantage. Jack Milne carried well and rattled the ball into Kevin Nisbet’s feet. The forward played a smart pass around the corner. Mouloua was only denied by a terrific save from Pandur.

There was still time for Mouloua to be thwarted by the outstretched leg of Makhanya as he moved to turn home a cut back.

Bluntly, it was no surprise that McInnes made three changes at the break. Off came Godfrey, Kelsy and Bouanani. On went Minsu, Rommens and Findlay Curtis. The impact was extraordinary.

Re-energised, within 45 seconds Rangers were level. Minsu’s speculative shot did come through heavy traffic. Still, Muller had to hold it. Credit to Naderi for anticipating the fumble. The instant it bounced towards him, he instinctively lashed it home for his 10th of the season. Subdued to that point, the home fans roared their approval. And they’d quickly be off their seats again.

As Aberdeen’s attack broke down, Naderi played a simple pass into space. Gassama had too much pace for the chasing pack. Did he have the finishing? Absolutely. What a turnaround.

Gassama squeezes his shot under Muller to put the home side ahead just after the restart

Two goals in 90 seconds then became three in 11 second-half minutes. Gassama did superbly to motor down the left, look up and play in Raskin. The Belgian smashed the ball back across goal and in.

That should have been that. Yet three minutes later, the Dons were back within a goal of McInnes’ men. Afforded too much time on the left, Alexander Briedl picked out Marshall with his cross. Marshall swept it home with his left foot via the inside of the post.

Remarkably, the Dons might well have levelled. Pandur made a fine save when Minsu threatened to turn an Aberdeen corner into his own net. The ball bounced off Nisbet and just wide.

Terrific throughout, Marshall saw a good strike whistle just wide. The fact the Dons made Rangers sweat for the win will be some consolation.

#1470. Manchester City’s £31m left-back wanted in Turin: Loan or sale in January?

CalcioMercato reports that Juventus have started monitoring Rayan Aït-Nouri ahead of the transfer market reopening, and the Manchester City left-back seems ready to listen. The Algeria international wants to restart his career elsewhere, views Turin favourably and has told his entourage to strengthen contacts, while the interest from Juventus is real and the club intends to act soon to test the deal’s feasibility.

City want to sell outright and reinvest immediately, whereas Juventus prefer a loan with an option to buy, which suits a club bound by a UEFA settlement agreement. They first asked in August and City refused, while Gazzetta dello Sport says Luciano Spalletti wants competition for Andrea Cambiaso.

City paid Wolves a reported £31m in June 2025 and gave him a contract until 2030, yet Enzo Maresca reportedly ranks the 25-year-old behind Joško Gvardiol and Nico O’Reilly. He had played 168 minutes in all competitions by mid-November, none of them in the Premier League, and his only starts have come in the EFL Cup.

His strengths explain the fee. Aït-Nouri scored nine goals and set up 15 in 135 Premier League games for Wolves, added five assists in 1,605 minutes last season, and can also operate in central areas.

The weakness is defensive security, because he is an ultra-attacking left-back. That matters now, with City on one point from their last four league games after losing 3-1 at Nottingham Forest and drawing 1-1 with Fulham on Saturday.

No, not in January, and not on terms that leave City carrying all the risk. Maresca has used Nico O’Reilly in midfield this season, yet O’Reilly started only seven of City’s first 15 games while managing a back problem, so an available specialist left-back is no luxury. Khusanov, Nunes and Guéhi all picked up knocks at Forest, which leaves the back line short.

City should treat the Juventus talks as a pricing exercise. A straight loan sends a 25-year-old on a contract until 2030 away for six months and returns him no more valuable, so only a loan with an obligation to buy close to the £31m fee makes sense.

Otherwise, give him a league start, see whether his attacking threat helps a side that keeps conceding, and let Maresca’s evidence decide. A club that paid £31m for a left-back last year has not shown he cannot do the job; it has shown only that the manager prefers somebody else.

#1469. Lethal Trent Alexander-Arnold sends Tuchel a statement in England victory

Thomas Tuchel has never been inclined to place much faith in the most famous right-back at his disposal, Trent Alexander-Arnold, once of Liverpool, now of Real Madrid, and – back in an England shirt – still capable of changing games in the blink of an eye.

England always looked likely to defeat a beleaguered Czech Republic team down to 10 men with just 25 minutes played, but it still required one man to conjure the moment of inspiration in this Nations League tie. This was the first cap in 15 months for the right-back now known simply as “Trent” in an England shirt – as well as his Real Madrid jersey – rather than the six syllables of his surname. With the game level at half-time, two minutes into the new half, he twice won the ball before landing a cross on the head of Anthony Gordon for the first goal.

TRENT ➡️ GORDON ⚽️🔥Anthony Gordon can't stop scoring for England, 3 goals in his last 3 games for England 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/xmqPIULJ24

Will the Alexander-Arnold with England experiment survive? One feels that Tuchel will need a little more to convince him to abandon whatever reservations he has about the Liverpudlian. A week short of his 28th birthday, Alexander-Arnold was winning just his 35th cap. His Real Madrid team-mate Jude Bellingham, a second-half substitute, was earning his 58th cap less than two months after his 23rd birthday. Bellingham was on as captain in place of the man he replaced, Harry Kane, scorer of England’s second. Bellingham’s international career has taken a much less rocky path than that of his Real team-mate.

Having missed the World Cup finals this summer, and had little good fortune around previous tournaments, one wonders if Euro 2028 might be the watershed moment for Alexander-Arnold. Either way, against opponents who sit back, he is lethal when it is time for the big delivery. Alexander-Arnold may not have the breadth of England experience that some of his peers have accumulated, but he does have plenty of experience of big games.

“I make that run time and time again,” Gordon said of his anticipation of the Alexander-Arnold cross, “but only a set number of players have that ability, that technique and the bravery to risk a mistake to play that pass. And that’s why I have been dying to play with him [Alexander-Arnold]. He’s been on his own journey but has trained really well this week. He should have played more. Sorry – he would have loved to have played more.”

A Freudian slip from the Barcelona winger, another Liverpudlian in Spain, who himself has barely put a foot wrong for England of late. He has three goals in three games for England, including the World Cup semi-final against Argentina. This was an England team that Tuchel fine-tuned, first to give a rest to Bellingham and in other quarters, too. Lewis Hall started at left-back. Trevoh Chalobah won his third England cap at centre-back. Alex Scott, of Bournemouth, was given his debut off the bench in the second half and Rio Ngumoha won the second cap of his England career, just one month after his 18th birthday.

As for Kane, his 87th goal for England now puts him within two goals of Robert Lewandowski, among four greats in the seven ahead of Kane on the all-time international goalscorers’ list. By the end of this international break the England captain should have equalled Peter Shilton’s record 125 caps. It has been an astonishing career even if it ends tomorrow. Following the missed penalty against Spain, Kane was again the man in the right place at the right time when Morgan Rogers’s shot was blocked in the second half.

“Strange to get an early red card,” Tuchel said. “Not the best for the team and spectators. It’s an awkward one, but we kept going, got a win and that’s what counts.” Not quite a vintage Czech Republic team, either, and when their best player of the opening stages, the attacking midfielder Pavel Sulc, of Lyon in Ligue 1, was dismissed after 25 minutes, it certainly did not become any easier for the home team. Sulc, the Czech player of the year in 2025, had mistimed a tackle on Elliot Anderson, which on a VAR review, the Turkish referee Umut Meler decided was worthy of an upgrade from yellow to red. It was high on the right calf of the England midfielder.

Czech Republic DOWN TO 10 MEN! 🟥Pavel Šulc sees red for a dangerous challenge on Elliot Anderson#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/B2YOLuS0vL

England had looked once more a little open to the counter-attack in the early stages, with Sulc one notable runner. This was not an opponent of the quality of Spain and Tuchel’s players were able to recover the situation. When they lose the ball in the opposition’s half, England tend to look vulnerable.

Even before the red card Rogers had hit a post. Myles Lewis-Skelly, playing in midfield, was booked for a foul on Lukas Serv and was pursued thereafter by the Czech players hoping to get an upgrade on the yellow card. He was substituted at half-time, with Eberechi Eze on in his place.

“I spoke to Ant [Gordon] at half-time,” Alexander-Arnold said later to ITV, “and I said if I’m getting in those spaces make sure you get to the back post. You don’t expect to get it that fast, but it did and it worked.”

Two minutes after the break, Alexander-Arnold suddenly burst into life. He won the ball back in his own area and then drove forward in search of the return. When that did not come, he raced back to win the ball again and unleashed one of those right-footed outswingers to the back post, where Gordon guided in the header. “Really proud to score that,” Gordon said, “because I can’t tell you the number of hours I’ve spent practising headers.”

Kane scored the second just a minute before he was replaced and Bellingham took the captain’s armband and the role as a No 9. One day someone will have to step into those goalscorer’s boots on a permanent basis and try to replace Kane – although it may be a while yet.

Thomas Tuchel has backed Jude Bellingham as a future England captain after giving him the armband in the victory over the Czech Republic.

In the absence of Declan Rice, who was vice-captain at the World Cup, Bellingham assumed the role when he came on for Harry Kane, who is now in his 10th season as England captain and also scored in the 2-0 win in Prague.

Tuchel, who needs to check on Bellingham ahead of Saturday’s game against Croatia after a “niggle,” has praised the midfielder’s attitude during the extended international break one year after he was back from an injury but left out of the squad.

“If you are the captain at the end of these matches, you can be the permanent captain,” Tuchel said when asked whether Bellingham could eventually lead the team. “He was the captain against New Zealand before the World Cup. It is always a reward and always an honour.

“I think he loves to be with us at the moment. That’s what I feel, and we had this small talk today about his role. We felt in our hearts or our stomachs to say ‘let’s go again, let’s start again’ and also our heads told us maybe 30 minutes is enough for this match because he hasn’t played in this quick turnaround through this season. He has done it before, but not in the season, so we didn’t want to be the first ones to try that.

“But even in this little encounter, you can see that he’s confident and happy to help from the bench. So it’s a reward. It’s good. He had a little niggle at the end of the match, so hopefully it’s nothing serious, and he’s available for Croatia.”

Nico O’Reilly is a doubt for the Croatia match in Rijeka and there are also concerns over Ezri Konsa, who was on the bench but not fit enough to play.

Trent Alexander-Arnold provided an assist for Anthony Gordon in the Real Madrid full-back’s first cap in 15 months. Gordon, meanwhile, has now scored in the first two Nations League games of the campaign and is staking his case to be an indispensable player for Tuchel.

“He’s getting there. He’s defending his shirt, he’s defending his position, an excellent performance again after his performance against Spain,” Tuchel said.

“He was very decisive today and had an excellent goal. It was very, very difficult, but the technique and finishing was excellent. He scored against Spain, so he has decisive actions and he’s defending his shirt and his position. He does it on the highest level and he’s a very important player.”

England returned to winning ways with a 2-0 win over Czech Republic in Prague.

Pavel Sulc’s first-half red card after a VAR review of his clumsy challenge on Elliot Anderson took the sting out of the initially lively hosts and Anthony Gordon gave Thomas Tuchel’s men a deserved lead early in the second half.

The forward headed home a fantastic cross by Trent Alexander-Arnold, who was making his first start under the German coach, before skipper Harry Kane scored to settle any nerves.

So who played well for England and who failed to impress? Rate each player with our voting tool, and have your say in the comments.

We got that [goal] at the start of the second half which is what we needed. The longer it’s 0-0, it gets harder and harder and harder.

He’s a willing runner, great to play with him. I saw the run and was able to execute the pass,

It’s always a pleasure and an honour to represent my country. It’s been a long time. I’ve always believed that I can play for England and I want to. The manager’s given me the opportunity and I tried to do what he wanted me to do to the best of my ability and I hope he’s happy with how I played.

🦁 #1301Alex Scott reflects on a special night, earning his first senior England cap 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿#ITVFootball | @gabrielclarke05 | @England pic.twitter.com/lC34bAPbbd

I knew exactly where I wanted to go, where I needed to go but I needed some guidance. I think the same way as him [Jude]. We don’t think there’s any limit on what we can achieve, wanting to win, wanting to win in a good way by going for the throat. Fearlessness.

It ate me up for a good couple of weeks after [losing the semi-final]. I’d scored… on the same pitch as Messi, the man I idolised as a kid. It was the highest possible moment of my entire life. And within 20 minutes it had come completely crashing down. There’s been a lot of controversy, a lot of talk about that. Going forward, if we are going to lose a game, it’s going to be like how we lost to Spain. We went for their throats, we missed a penalty and lost the game. But the way we went for them, no regrets. I want to stay as far away from that [regret] as possible.

[Did you ever think you would sign for Barcelona?] Yes. No one ever achieves anything in life by playing it safe. My personality is based on being bold, taking risks and going for whatever you want.

At this level we’re all as talented as each other but only the most mentally competitive and driven people can maintain success for a long time.

I always thought in England that people respected me because I was fast and I pressed but they never respected my quality and people are starting to take notice that I’m not just quick. In Barcelona if you’re not technical, if you’re not smart, you’d stand out like a sore thumb.

[Where do you see this squad in two years?] European champions.

The intensity we played with and the way we took it to the best team in the world [is what we’ve taken out of the Spain game]. We can be really proud of that. It was really good. Obviously tight margins decide games but overall we’re happy with the way we dusted the World Cup off and all that emotion.

Massively [relishing a run in the No 10 position in place of Bellingham]. I want to try and show what I can do in that role and make a positive impact.

The atmosphere here [is always intense] and they have a new coach. We’ve done our research. We have to respect them. It’s going to be difficult and it’s up to us to hold our nerve.

The Professional Footballers’ Association has leapt to Cole Palmer’s defence following his withdrawal from the England squad.

The union’s CEO,  Maheta Molango, said the Chelsea forward is a victim of a “sick” system that is demanding too much from players physically.

“When England see five players who need to withdraw when the single most proud moment a player has is to be called up for the national team, you just ask yourself, what’s wrong about the industry?” Molango said at the Fifpro performance summit in London.

“You see people like Cole Palmer, someone who would have played four consecutive summers in a row had he gone to the World Cup, and you wonder why is he missing?”He’s missing because he’s a victim of the calendar and that’s something that needs to absolutely trigger the alarm bells.”

Man City used ‘sham’ sponsorships in £830m cheating scheme

Manchester City arranged “sham” sponsorships in a near-£1bn plot to flout Premier League rules, an independent commission has found.

It was confirmed on Tuesday that City had been found guilty of all charges related to “serious breaches” of the league’s financial rules, with the commission also upholding all but one in relation to their failure to co-operate with an investigation spanning over three years.

The commission found that, of £949.94m City claimed in commercial income over a nine-year period, only £119.25m was legitimate, with the remaining £830.69m illicitly paid by their Abu Dhabi owners.

Miroslav Koubek, their 74-year-old manager, the oldest in the competition’s history, promptly stood down and has been replaced by their first foreign head coach, Santi, the former Atlético Madrid centre-half, who spent 15 years moving from managing Spain’s U17s, to the U19s and then the U21s. #1468. Arsenal eye Serie A’s 11-goal striker: Should they pay £26m?

Arsenal transfer news from Italy centres on Monza striker Gustavo Varela, with Gianluca Di Marzio reportingthat the Gunners are very interested. The 21-year-old Portugal forward has scored 11 goals in 11 Serie A games since joining from Benfica B in July. Barcelona are equally keen, Inter watch him live at every match, and Napoli are reported as his strongest Italian suitor.

The interest makes sense. Viktor Gyokeres, signed for £64m in 2025, has two goals in 15 appearances and none in the Premier League, while Kai Havertz has started 10 of 11 league games for three goals. Arsenal’s results haven’t suffered, but their number nine position has produced little.

Finishing is the selling point. FotMob‘s data has him scoring well above his expected goals for a Monza side that won only two of its first 10 league games, and he averages around three shots per 90 minutes. The weaknesses are just as clear: he wins 34% of his duels, completes 41% of his dribbles and ranks in the ninth percentile among forwards for defensive contribution, which clashes with the pressing Arteta wants from his striker.

Di Marzio says Monza will listen at around £22m to £26m, with the money earmarked for other signings, after paying about £3m including bonuses. Flashscore reports Benfica hold a 20% sell-on and a right to match offers, and Varela’s agents meet Monza this week.

Yes, but in the summer and only if Gyokeres leaves. Arsenal’s results are strong, so a January rush for a 21-year-old would add risk without fixing a crisis. A fee near £26m looks modest beside the £64m Gyokeres cost, and Varela’s goals-per-game record argues for the gamble far more than Gyokeres’ two in 15 does.

The real risk is suitability. He also scores for a struggling side, so his chances come in games unlike most of the Premier League games Arsenal play. Arteta needs a number nine who presses and wins duels, and Varela does neither well, so Arsenal would be buying a finisher and building the rest of his game themselves.

That is workable if Varela arrives as competition for Havertz rather than the first choice. Arsenal should also expect resistance beyond the price, because Benfica’s matching right and Inter’s summer plans complicate any early bid.

Watching him until June costs Arsenal nothing, and another 20 league games will show whether this form is real or a hot streak.

#1467. Chelsea news: Why Xabi Alonso should be one defeat away from sack after more senseless decision-making

By Darren Plant | 28 Nov 2026 12:05

When Chelsea appointed Xabi Alonso as their new manager in May, it was viewed as a long-term appointment, one that would bring about much-craved stability at Stamford Bridge.

However, that should not mean that the Spaniard - a Bundesliga title winner and former Real Madrid boss - should get a free pass.

Sports Mole argued earlier this week that Alonso had already made nine mistakes since officially starting his role in July, two of which came in the 4-1 defeat at home to Leeds United.

Not only did he repeat one of those mistakes for the 3-2 loss at Nottingham Forest on Friday, his selection of Wesley Fofana - just days after the Frenchman's controversial interview that had not been sanctioned by the club - was bizarre as it was tone-deaf to the feelings of supporters.

Alonso reacted to Fofana justifiably being booed by the away support by calling for unity between the team and fans, yet he should be taking responsibility for having no understanding of the consequences of his decisions.

Despite being less than four months into his tenure, Alonso is already flirting with the sack. The 45-year-old can rightly claim that injuries to Maxence Lacroix, Reece James, Moises Caicedo and Joao Pedro have contributed to recent results, but he is passing the buck if he feels that is the overriding issue.

After Fofana hinted that his earnings at Chelsea helped convince him not to retire after a number of serious injuries and he joked about his decisive missed spot kick in an EFL Cup penalty-shootout defeat at Liverpool in October, selecting the £75m centre-back was bad enough.

However, playing Caicedo alongside him and in front of Emiliano Martinez - who is clearly being chosen on reputation rather than form - just added to the consensus that Alonso does not know how to manage this Chelsea team.

Fofana would subsequently clumsily foul Liam Delap to gift Forest a second-half penalty and he was promptly withdrawn a few minutes later. This was not the first time that Fofana has cost Chelsea with an individual mistake, and as harsh as some of the chants targeting Fofana were, his performances on the pitch and behaviour off it means that he should be nowhere near a Chelsea starting lineup in the future.

There were alternatives. Levi Colwill has struggled in Chelsea's defence this season, yet a partnership of him and Josh Acheampong in the middle of the backline against Forest felt far more acceptable than Fofana and Caicedo.

Meanwhile, prior to the Forest game, Martinez had conceded a goal every 41 minutes in a Chelsea shirt. By comparison, Mike Penders has shipped a goal every 79 minutes this season, and had only conceded goals from the penalty spot in the three matches before being dropped for the Argentine, who had been sidelined with a fractured jaw.

You can also question why Alonso chose to bench Emanuel Emegha after his goal against Leeds. He earned more minutes in that game than he did versus Forest, yet he still netted twice after his half-time introduction.

He had already irked fans with his insistence that having so little of the ball was acceptable. Chelsea were fortunate to beat Fulham and almost blew a three-goal lead against Brighton & Hove Albion, but regardless of Chelsea having more than 60% of possession versus Forest, the 31.5% possession stat in a 2-0 home defeat to Tottenham Hotspur opened up Alonso to the criticism that he is receiving now.

Alonso is certainly not completely to blame for Chelsea's demise. Even though he now possesses a worst win percentage than Lian Rosenior (46.67% to 47.83%), the West Londoners have now lost 20 of 46 matches since the departure of Enzo Maresca. The Italian ended his reign with just two wins in his last nine games, so Chelsea have been stuck in a rut for a year.

Some of the blame should be on the players. They downed tools under Rosenior and, despite senior names being signed in the summer, they still play with such an immaturity where Chelsea fans are anticipating the next mistake before it is made.

Nevertheless, that should not disguise the fact that Alonso is not the right manager for Chelsea. Given what also happened at Real Madrid, perhaps he is not wired to lead a high-profile club that comes with egos, politics and heightened pressure.

BlueCo will want to keep Alonso in charge for as long as possible. They will not want to acknowledge another mistake, but how can Alonso stay in his role in the dugout when his decision-making is so muddled, and he is not prepared to drop players with big egos when they are not performing? We haven't even touched upon Cole Palmer's weakening impact at Chelsea under Alonso.

If Chelsea lose to Crystal Palace, Alonso should be sacked. Liverpool, Manchester City and Aston Villa follow that game, and it is not beyond the realms of possibility that Chelsea could quickly find themselves in a relegation scrap, with or without Alonso.

That said, even if Chelsea do beat Palace, it would merely buy Alonso time and waste everyone else's. He may have only been in charge of 15 games, but he is already edging closer to his position being untenable.

#1466. Chelsea’s England playmaker on Man Utd’s radar

Chelsea transfer news around Cole Palmer has flared again, with Mauricio Pochettino’s arrival at Manchester United reviving the noise. Reporter Dean Jones insists the England playmaker’s future at Stamford Bridge is not in doubt, but he admits the sentiment around it is becoming harder to ignore.

Palmer, a boyhood United supporter, has been linked with Old Trafford before. United appointed Pochettino on 18 November after sacking Michael Carrick following one win in ten league games. The Argentine made Palmer one of his most used players at Chelsea, where the pair built a positive relationship, and Palmer scored 22 league goals in 2023/24.

Jones rates the chances of Palmer joining United as extremely low. United’s January budget stands at roughly £50m, and they want a left-back, a centre-back and a striker. A player FotMob values at €100m, roughly £87m, sits outside both the money and the shopping list. Jones also sees no sign that Palmer wants to leave, and says relations at Stamford Bridge would need to break down badly first.

Palmer has started all 11 of Chelsea’s Premier League games this season, playing 970 minutes for three goals, one from the penalty spot, and three assists. His 23 chances created include six big chances, and his 2.58 expected goals backs up the output. Xabi Alonso says, “The better Cole we have, the better Chelsea we have”.

Only ten of Palmer’s 31 shots have hit the target; he wins 46.9% of his dribbles, and he has collected two yellows and a red. Fitness worries more after an injury-hit 2025/26 that ended with him missing the World Cup.

No, but Chelsea should treat Jones’s condition as the real warning. Palmer’s contract runs to 2034, and United’s budget does not reach his valuation, so the danger lies in a deteriorating relationship, not a bid. That puts the onus on Alonso, Chelsea’s seventh permanent manager since 2021.

Morgan Rogers’ £117m arrival from Aston Villa creates the obvious flashpoint. If Palmer feels crowded out of the number ten role, or pushed wide right too often, the homesickness talk will return. Clear roles and managed minutes will protect him better than another forward.

The money belongs elsewhere. Alonso’s side beat United 2-0 on 31 October, then lost 1-0 at Sunderland eight days later, and defensive brittleness and thin squad depth keep undermining a front line that already scores. A back line that leaks goals will not.

#1465. Liverpool lining up Ajax teenager for January

Liverpool transfer news from Goal says Ajax teenager Abdellah Ouazane is a January target as attacking cover for Florian Wirtz. Julian Ward, Liverpool’s recruitment chief, has reportedly sped up plans to support the £116m playmaker, and Ouazane has become a serious option before the winter window opens. Wael Mohya and Gilberto Mora sit on the same shortlist.

The 17-year-old grew up supporting Liverpool and badly wants to play at Anfield. Ajax hold the leverage, though: his contract runs to 2028, and persuading them to sell a prized academy graduate mid-season will take careful negotiation. De Telegraaf also reported earlier this season that sporting director Jordi Cruyff wants to give him a new deal when he turns 18 on 15 January.

Ouazane is mainly an attacking midfielder who also plays wide or up front. FotMob‘s 2026/27 numbers show two goals and one assist in 12 Eredivisie games, only four of them starts, across 441 minutes. His goals and shot attempts rank in the 88th and 86th percentiles among comparable attackers.

The gaps are just as clear: he sits in the 19th percentile for defensive contributions and the 15th for aerial duels won, and a 45.7% dribble success rate suggests he still loses the ball too often against senior opponents. Real Madrid pulled out of a 2025 deal after his medical, though Ajax’s own checks cleared him.

Iraola’s Liverpool press harder and play more direct than they did under Arne Slot, so that defensive profile matters. Wirtz works as the central creator with Bradley Barcola, Victor Munoz and Rio Ngumoha out wide, which leaves the number 10 role as Ouazane’s only route in.

Yes, but as a planned investment rather than genuine cover. Wirtz missed several matches with a back problem last February, so depth behind him is a fair concern. Yet Liverpool sit fourth, a point behind second-placed Brighton after Sunday’s 4-0 win over Manchester United, and only eighth in the Champions League table after losing to Fenerbahce. January minutes will decide those races, and Ouazane has four Eredivisie starts and numbers that clash with Iraola’s pressing.

His lifelong Anfield dream and Ward’s record of targeting elite teenagers give Liverpool an edge, so they should push. If Ajax demand a premium for a mid-season exit, Ward should wait for the summer, when Liverpool can judge a full Eredivisie campaign. Four starts make him a bet on 2028, not insurance for February.

#1464. Three above a 7, two below a 5: Fan player ratings for Olympiacos 2-4 AC Milan

AC Milan rose from the canvas floor on the outskirt of Athens on Thursday night, coming from two goals down to beat Olympiacos 4-2.

With 50 minutes on the clock, Milan trailed by two goals after a Mike Maignan own-goal and a strike from Jota Silva. However, Omari Hutchinson inspired a comeback, halving the deficit with a great solo goal then setting up Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic to complete the turnaround.

Diego Moreira scored on the break in the final seconds of added time to add a fourth and make sure of the victory, which boost the Rossoneri back into the top 24 with three games to go.

Looking at what our readers gave the players for the win in Piraeus, there is a real mixed bag of scores which in many ways matches the two-sided nature of the performance.

Starting with the negatives, Koni De Winter really struggled all night and played a stray pass for the second goal, which resulted in an average score of 4.5 out of 10 from our readers. Pervis Estupinan didn’t do much better, getting a 4.6.

Sankhoun Diawara had one of his tougher nights and got a 5, while Goncalo Ramos only got a 5.3 and Ardon Jashari also fell below a passing grade, but only just (5.9). Mike Maignan was scored a 6.1 and Adrien Rabiot a 6.2.

Then we get to the difference-makers: Diego Moreira averaged a 7, Alphadjo Cisse a 7.3 and Omari Hutchinson one of our highest grades of the season, with an outstanding 9 out of 10.

The subs were as follows: Yunus Musah got a 6.6, Christian Pulisic an 8.1, Fikayo Tomori a 7/1, Filippo Terracciano a 5.9 and Christian Comotto a 6.1.

#1463. HIBERNIAN 2 DUNDEE 1: Hibs enjoy some long lost home comfort as Leith men win the battle of the wounded

Published: 18:46 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 18:51 EST, 24 November 2026

Hibernian ended their long wait for a Premiership home win after overcoming Dundee in a hard-fought contest at Easter Road.

Martin Boyle and Nicky Cadden – who curled home a stunning effort from outside the box – had the hosts in command before the interval.

But Dundee, still licking their wounds after an 8-0 savaging at the hands of Hearts on Saturday, showed plenty of fight after the break and pulled one back through Joe Wright.

The visitors tried in vain to grab an equaliser and it was Hibs who were left satisfied by their first three points at home since beating Kilmarnock on April 4.

Manager Marink Reedijk was thrilled to have bounced back from their 4-0 weekend home defeat at the hands of Dundee United, saying: ‘I think it’s a good reaction to what we have done against Dundee United.

‘It’s important that you get the three points at home. Again, that’s a big win. I saw a front foot team again, I saw togetherness again, I saw a team who fought for every ball.

Martin Boyle takes the acclaim after scoring the all-important second goal for Hibernian

‘That’s not easy, they have to be patient, you have to be secure, you have to wait for your moment and we took these moments and that was really good to see.

‘The goal of Nicky [Cadden] is one to, we say, put in a frame and put on your wall as a painting. The one of Martin [Boyle] is why Martin is so important for us. He can disrupt an opponent if they are so organised and so close to each other and so deep.

‘As long as we keep ourselves, I think these are good signs.’

Hibs played on the front foot as they looked to start repairing the damage from the weekend. On a rare start, Togo international Thibault Klidje was lively and saw a header crash into the side-netting before hitting a harmless snap-shot straight at Dundee goalkeeper Owen Goodman.

From a short corner routine Hibs worked space for Cadden on the edge of the box from Josh Mulligan’s lay-off and his driving effort whistled just past a post.

Dundee were desperate to keep it tight at the back but offered little going forward. Just when it looked like they were beginning to settle Hibs hit them with two goals in three minutes before the break.

The first came in the 40th minute when Boyle fired a penalty past Goodman after being tripped by Ryan Finnigan.

Nicky Cadden unleashes an absolute pearler into the top corner to put Hibs in front

Cadden then found the top corner with a sublime curling effort from his left foot just outside the box. It was another short corner routine that saw Miguel Chaiwa set up the wing-back.

Despite the hammer blow of losing two goals in quick succession before the break, Dundee demonstrated at the start of the second half that they were not going to roll over.

Steven Pressley’s side upped their intensity as they searched for a goal to get themselves back in the game and that arrived in the 67th minute courtesy of Wright.

Substitute Callum Jones’ free-kick should have been put away by Ryan Astley but the ball broke back to Wright and he slammed the ball high into the net from six yards.

That set up a tense finish but Hibs desperately held on for a rare home victory.

For Pressley, who changed half of his outfield XI following his side’s weekend humiliation, there were also positives to take.

The Dark Blues boss said: ‘We’re disappointed to not come away with anything and to obviously lose the game. But I also thought we restored some degree of pride tonight.

‘Going into half-time 2-0 down, losing two late goals in the half, can be a little bit demoralising, especially for a team that has a bit of fragility on the back of the weekend’s result.

‘I thought we responded brilliantly. We showed a lot of courage, a lot of determination, a lot of spirit and, as I’ve said, I think we certainly restored some level of pride that allows us a foundation to move into the weekend.’

#1462. Chelsea’s £42.5m Winger Could Head To Saudi Arabia

Chelsea transfer news has taken a Saudi Arabian turn, with Fabrizio Romano reporting that the Pro League could offer Alejandro Garnacho a January exit from his loan at Aston Villa.

Romano says that would only happen if Chelsea find a buyer and keep the player happy. Villa and Chelsea could also agree to terminate the loan and send the winger elsewhere, although Chelsea have no recall clause and no wish to take him back.

Garnacho joined in July on a loan that becomes a £42.5m permanent deal once he reaches a set number of appearances. Chelsea expected that in 2027, but Unai Emery left the 22-year-old out of the Champions League squad for the Galatasaray game. Romano suggests Villa are limiting his minutes to avoid triggering the obligation.

The numbers explain why. FotMob lists four Premier League appearances, no starts, 34 minutes, no goals or assists and an average rating of 6.04.

Garnacho still ranks in the 96th percentile for shot attempts among wingers and attacking midfielders, and the 62nd for chances created. He offers far less without the ball, sitting in the 17th percentile for defensive contributions and the 33rd for aerial duels.

Chelsea sit eighth with 16 points after Friday’s 3-2 defeat at Nottingham Forest, their third straight league loss and a gap of 12 points to Arsenal. They have created 14.5 xG across 11 league games, the 15th-best total in the division, so Xabi Alonso needs end product from wide areas.

Yes, but only at a price close to the £42.5m Villa agreed to pay.

Saudi clubs have made calls without a reported fee, and FotMob values him at €29m, roughly £25m. A bid near the obligation protects the money Chelsea expected in 2027. A bid near his valuation would leave them about £17m short.

Recalling him makes no sense. Chelsea would inherit a winger who cannot get into Villa’s squad, on a contract that runs to 2032, while Alonso’s real problems are chance creation and the four goals conceded at home to Leeds. Garnacho’s profile solves neither.

Letting the loan run is the worst outcome. Villa have every incentive to keep his appearances low, so he would return in June 2027 with fewer minutes behind him and a market value that keeps sliding from its €71m peak.

A Saudi sale at or near £42.5m would deliver what the Villa clause was meant to, just months earlier.

Scott has played six Premier League games this season, for 467 minutes, scoring once and creating 11 chances. He has completed 81.9 per cent of his passes, won four of seven dribbles and made 10 tackles and eight interceptions, according to FotMob. He progresses play and still defends.

The concerns are practical. Injury ruled him out for four to five weeks in October; he has two bookings, and he reportedly turned down a new contract rather than commit to Bournemouth beyond 2028.

Yes, but only for Scott alone. Moisés Caicedo wins the ball, yet nobody beside him moves it forward with Fernández gone, and Scott’s carrying and passing fill exactly that gap. Alonso, a deep-lying playmaker himself, needs a partner who lets Chelsea play out of pressure.

The price is the problem. Bournemouth know Chelsea have no alternative, and a fee that size for a player with six league appearances this season carries real risk if his fitness fails again. Chelsea concede too easily, and midfield control matters far more than another attacker.

Camara would cost less and offers more raw ball-winning, but relations with Monaco have turned sour, which complicates any return. Waiting for the summer carries its own danger, because Liverpool also like Scott. Chasing Camara as well would put two top-end fees into one position while the defence still leaks goals.

Chelsea should settle on Scott, agree terms early and spend the rest on a ball-winning reserve for Caicedo.

#1460. Cagliari vs AC Milan - prediction, team news, lineups

By Jonathan O'Shea | 28 Nov 2026 12:06

Wrapping up Serie A's 13th matchday, AC Milan will aim to maintain their momentum when they visit Cagliari on Monday night.

Milan have almost averaged four goals while winning their last three games, but the Sardinian side have lost five out of six since making a sharp start to the season.

Facing the prospect of early elimination, Milan kickstarted their ailing Europa League campaign on Thursday evening, when they travelled to Piraeus for a tough test against Olympiacos.

The seven-time European champions had lost three of their first four league-phase fixtures, while their unbeaten hosts had only dropped two points.

It initially looked like more Milanese misery would await, as Ruben Amorim's men fell two goals behind early in the second half; yet, a stunning comeback saw them winning 4-2 by the final whistle.

Partly thanks to Omari Hutchinson's fine solo strike, the Rossoneri inched into the playoff places, but they only sit 20th in the Europa League table and are far from certain to progress.

That victory followed a good run of results in Serie A since suffering their lone league loss to Bologna at the end of October.

After beating Inter in the Derby della Madonnina, then Genoa at Stadio Ferraris, breakout star Alphadjo Cisse scored again as Milan thumped Frosinone 5-1 last week.

Thrusting themselves into the Scudetto race, they have taken 15 points from the last available 18, while scoring at least twice on each occasion.

Amorim has averaged 2.25 points per game in Serie A, and his team are yet to lose on their travels around the Italian peninsula.

That does not bode well for Cagliari, who last beat Milan on home turf back in 2017, since when they have taken one point from six meetings on Sardinian soil.

More positively, the Rossoblu did defeat their Rossoneri rivals at San Siro on the final day of last season - a result that cost their hosts Champions League football.

This time, Fabio Pisacane's side will attempt to halt a slump down the Serie A standings, having taken just three points from their last six fixtures.

After losing one of the first six, last week's 2-0 loss to Como dropped them into the bottom half - albeit they remain some distance above the drop zone.

Now seeking back-to-back wins over Milan for the first time this century, Cagliari must try to find some missing firepower, having scored just three league goals on home turf this term.

Veteran playmaker Luka Modric recently joined Milan's long injury list, and Amorim also has fresh concerns about his main striker, Goncalo Ramos.

The latter could overcome a knock, but the visitors will travel without Modric, Mattia Gabbia, Samuel Chukwueze, Alexis Saelemaekers and Ruben Loftus-Cheek.

Cisse has started more regularly in the Europa League, scoring four goals so far, but he took his Serie A tally up to six last weekend.

The new Italy international would depuise for Ramos if required; otherwise, he must vie with Hutchinson, Christian Pulisic and Diego Moreira for selection in a support role.

Once in Cisse's current position as the Rossoneri's rising star, Cagliari striker Daniel Maldini has scored half of his team's 10 league goals this season.

Maldini is set to link up with either Paul Mendy, Yael Trepy or M'Bala Nzola in the final third, as Pisacane continues to search for another regular scorer.

The Rossoblu's boss will still be missing long-term absentee Mattia Felici, but Harry Winks is expected to play despite a persistent back problem.

Caprile; Ze Pedro, Kofler, Rodriguez; Grandu, Adopo, Winks, Deiola, Obert; Maldini, Nzola

Maignan; Gila, De Winter, Pavlovic, Diawara; Musah, Jashari, Rabiot, Moreira; Pulisic; Ramos

Milan may be fatigued by a busy schedule, but the Rossoneri have now found their rhythm under Amorim and are scoring for fun.

So, they should extend Cagliari's downturn on Monday evening, while keeping themselves in touch with Italy's top three.

#1459. Chelsea Plan Move For This Second-Tier France Star

Chelsea transfer news has an unusual name in it today: Saël Kumbedi, a 21-year-old right-back who plays in the 2. Bundesliga. TEAMtalk reports that Chelsea plan to move for the Wolfsburg defender in January or next summer, with Tottenham and Fulham also tracking him.

Top-flight clubs showed interest in the summer, but Kumbedi stayed after Wolfsburg’s relegation to chase an immediate return. His contract runs to 2029, so Wolfsburg hold the leverage now that FotMob values him at €17m (around £15m).

Kumbedi has started all eight league games this season, and FotMob rates him 7.26. His defending stands out, with 15 tackles, eight interceptions and 40 recoveries. He completes 83.6% of his passes and has created six chances. TEAMtalk also highlights his ability to play on the left.

He wins just 53.3% of his duels, has completed six of 17 dribbles and found a teammate with two of six crosses. He has no goals, and everything has come against second-tier opposition.

Chelsea’s right side is currently thin. Reece James had knee surgery on 16 October and may not return until 2027. Pedro Neto has covered at wing-back, while summer signing Marco Palestra came back from injury in October. The Daily Briefing claims Malo Gusto will leave in January. Xabi Alonso said he doesn’t expect to sign a replacement, and Chelsea sit eighth with 16 points from 12 games after a 4-1 home defeat to Leeds on 21 November.

Yes. January makes little sense, because Wolfsburg need him for promotion and can name their price. James should return around then, and Palestra and Neto already cover the position. Paying a premium mid-season for a second-tier player who would probably start on the bench is poor business.

Summer is different. Kumbedi’s tackling and recoveries suit a wing-back who must defend in transition, and playing on both flanks gives Alonso rotation while James’ fitness stays unreliable. Chelsea should still treat the step up seriously. A 175cm full-back who wins roughly half his duels and lands a third of his crosses will meet bigger, quicker wingers than he faces in Germany’s second tier.

If Gusto does leave, Chelsea need dependable cover first, not a long-term project. The sensible plan is a ceiling of about £15m and a close look at how he handles Bundesliga football if Wolfsburg go up. Kumbedi’s numbers justify a summer bid, but they don’t justify a January fee.

#1458. Moretto: Krösche ‘will bring a name’ to Milan with him but not Hardung – the situation

Markus Krösche will soon begin his work as AC Milan’s new Head of Football, but Timmo Hardung will not be joining him.

It has not been a well-kept secret that Milan have wanted to welcome Krösche as the new head of the management since the summer. Eintracht Frankfurt put up a wall a few months ago, but the German has since left his position and now seems all set for a new adventure in Italy.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Compensation has been agreed to release him fully from Eintracht, and the only question mark swirling concerned whether he would be joined by his right-hand man Hardung, with whom he has worked for years.

In a video published on Fabrizio Romano’s YouTube channel, Matteo Moretto took stock of the situation regarding the possible arrival of Hardung at Milan as sporting director alongside Krösche. His words are via MilanNews.

“I wanted to focus on Timmo Hardung, in the sense that I would like to specify a situation linked to the Rossoneri organisation that already exists, what he will become and what could be in the future,” he said.

“Everything has been said about Krosche at AC Milan and we are only waiting for the official announcement. Krosche will certainly bring someone with him, but this person, at the moment, is not Timmo Hardung, sporting director of Eintracht, Krosche’s right-hand man for a long time.

“There’s been talk that Hardung isn’t coming to Milan because of a deteriorating relationship with Markus Krösche. I actually wanted to deny this, in the sense that the two are on very good terms and still have a great rapport. This summer, the two worked closely together at Eintracht. So, in fact, they have an excellent relationship.

“If Hardung doesn’t join Krosche at Milan as sporting director, it’s certainly for other reasons, namely that perhaps there’s no room for Hardung in the structure and organisation designed by Gerry Cardinale. So it would be a choice tied to other dynamics within the Rossoneri.

“I can confirm that Krosche will bring one name, we’ll see if he then adds another name, which would be Hardung, but I think we’ll find out later. Contacts are in progress, but it’s not yet 100% clear whether Hardung will be able to join Krosche.”

#1457. Chelsea’s Under-Used £34m Argentine Tipped For Exit

Chelsea transfer news: Valentín Barco could become available, with a fresh report suggesting the 22-year-old is an option for any club open to a loan or a low-cost sale. Chelsea signed him from Strasbourg on 2 August for a reported £34m and gave him a contract until June 2033, so talk of moving him on after four months shows how his start has gone.

The numbers tell the story. Barco has made seven appearances and played 321 minutes in all competitions, scoring once in the 6-3 League Cup win over Leeds. In the Premier League, he has started one game in four appearances, totalling 119 minutes, and he has been an unused substitute in three straight league games since a three-minute cameo against Manchester United on 31 October.

The Argentina international, who stands 5ft 7in, is a left-footed midfielder whose game rests on passing and energy. FotMob data shows he has completed 90.9% of his league passes, 20 of them line-breaking, and made four tackles and four interceptions in those 119 minutes. Last season he contributed to 12 goals in 43 games for Strasbourg.

The weaknesses are just as clear. Barco has won 10 of 19 duels (52.6%) and lost possession five times in 125 touches, which matters in a midfield that must hold its shape against physical sides. His height limits him on second balls, and he only converted from left-back to midfield at Strasbourg.

No, and certainly not cheaply. Alonso’s side has lost three league games in a row, conceding eight goals against Sunderland, Leeds and Forest. Enzo Fernández has gone, and The Standard counted only five senior midfielders afterwards: Moisés Caicedo, Romeo Lavia, Barco, 36-year-old Jordan Henderson and Reece James. Losing one without a replacement would hurt Chelsea where they look thinnest.

The money argument is weak too. Spread over seven years, the reported fee costs roughly £4.9m a year on the books, and Transfermarkt still values him at €40m (about £34m), the figure Chelsea paid. A cut-price sale would write off money for no sporting gain.

A loan works only if Chelsea sign a midfielder first and the move guarantees regular starts in a league that tests him physically. Otherwise Alonso should give him the minutes he has lacked, because his passing could give a leaky side more control. Four months is too short to judge a £34m midfielder who has started once in the league.

#1456. Chelsea Track Serie A Centre-Back Real Madrid Can Reclaim

Chelsea transfer news centres on Como, where Goal reports that the Blues are closely monitoring centre-back Jacobo Ramon. Decision-makers at Stamford Bridge strongly admire the Spaniard, but Real Madrid hold an option to re-sign him at the end of the season, so any deal can only happen in the summer window, not mid-season.

The interest arrives at a bad moment for Xabi Alonso. Chelsea lost 3-2 at Nottingham Forest on Friday, their fourth league defeat in five games, and sit eighth. Wesley Fofana drew boos from the travelling fans, Maxence Lacroix reportedly faces a long hamstring layoff, and Axel Disasi and Benoit Badiashile are expected to leave permanently when their loans end.

Ramon sits on an 11-man centre-back shortlist reported by Simon Phillips, and Sports Mole, citing The Hard Tackle, says Chelsea have tracked him as depth for Alonso’s back three.

At 6ft 5in, the 21-year-old has won 40 of 61 aerial duels in Serie A this season and completed 92.8% of his passes, useful for a back three that builds from deep. FotMob also shows 20 tackles, 12 interceptions and one yellow card in 12 league appearances.

The weaknesses concern evidence, not ability. He has made only 10 league starts, has never played in England, and his three goals outrun an xG of 1.89.

Madrid sold him to Como for €2.5m (£2.1m) and can reportedly re-sign him for under €9m (£7.7m), keeping a 50% sell-on clause either way, while FotMob values him at €48m (£41m).

Yes, but not as the answer to Alonso’s immediate problems. Ramon cannot play before July, and the defence is leaking goals now, so a January centre-back has to come first.

Beyond that, he suits what Alonso wants. A defender who wins two-thirds of his aerial duels and passes at 92.8% covers a weakness Fofana’s form has exposed, and gives Colwill a partner with a different profile. His age also helps, since Chelsea must plan for Fofana’s uncertain future.

The limit is price. Madrid control the timing and collect half of any fee, so Chelsea would be paying a premium for a player sold for £2.1m last year. They should not go anywhere near £41m for ten starts of Serie A evidence. If the fee climbs, they can compare him calmly with Tomas Araujo, Murillo and Natan from the same shortlist. A January signing matters more to Alonso’s job than any summer deal for Ramon.
